The exceptional characteristics of graphene have catalyzed the study of graphene-like two-dimensional systems, known as 2D-Xenes. Silicene stands out as a leading candidate due to its compatibility with existing silicon manufacturing processes. Recent studies have highlighted its valuable electronic and mechanical attributes. Given the trend toward miniaturizing silicon devices and silicene's promising electro-mechanical behavior, there is a compelling need to explore its role in flexible electronics for nano electro-mechanical systems. Employing a theoretical framework that combines *ab-initio* density-functional theory with quantum transport theory, we examined the piezoresistance of silicene at the nanoscale. Similar to graphene, silicene exhibits a low piezoresistance gauge factor that varies sinusoidally with the transport angle. This modest gauge factor arises from silicene's stable Dirac cone and strain-insensitive valley degeneracy. Consequently, we suggest utilizing silicene as an interconnect in flexible electronic devices and as a reference piezoresistor for strain sensors. These findings will facilitate further investigations into flexible electronics applications across other 2D-Xene materials.

Determining and quantifying correlations within multipartite quantum systems represent a fundamental challenge in quantum information theory. This work presents a unitary quantum-mechanical framework for analyzing entanglement and Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen (EPR) steering in continuous-variable multimode states, deriving directly from Heisenberg uncertainty relations regarding canonical quadrature operators. We investigate correlations in two-party $(N\, \text{vs} \, 1)$-mode systems by examining the variances of specific EPR-like observables. Our findings reveal that the uncertainty sum of these nonlocal variables is bounded below by local uncertainties, with distinct strengthening effects observed for separable states versus one-way unsteerable states. Furthermore, analyzing the minimal properly normalized sums of these variances establishes necessary conditions for separability and EPR unsteerability in $(N\, \text{vs} \, 1)$-mode states across both steering directions. Specifically, when dealing with Gaussian states and measurements, these derived conditions align exactly with previously established criteria for separability and one-way unsteerability.

A semigroup is defined as permutable when its congruences are commutative. In a prior study, A. Nagy demonstrated that any permutable semigroup adhering to an arbitrary non-trivial permutation identity is either medial or constitutes an ideal extension of a rectangular band by a non-trivial commutative nil semigroup. The author subsequently posed the question: Does every permutable semigroup satisfying a non-trivial permutation identity necessarily possess the medial property? This paper provides an affirmative resolution to that problem.

Android applications often suffer from privacy data leaks, whether due to negligence or malicious intent. This study employs inter-component data-flow analysis to identify such leaks within Android apps. Unlike existing methods, our tool, IccTA, propagates context across components, significantly enhancing analysis precision. On the DroidBench benchmark, IccTA surpasses all other tools with 95.0% precision and 82.6% recall. Furthermore, when applied to a collection of 3,000 real-world applications, the approach identified 147 inter-component privacy leaks across 14 applications, achieving 88.4% precision. Additionally, utilizing ApkCombiner enables the detection of inter-application privacy leaks.

The COVID-19 pandemic is defined by two critical features: (i) the presence of asymptomatic infections (both identified and unidentified) that drive new transmissions, and (ii) dynamic characteristics resulting from emerging variants and Non-Pharmaceutical Interventions. We introduce the SUTRA model (Susceptible, Undetected though infected, Tested positive, and Removed Analysis), which integrates both features. When applied to a specific region, the model estimates two parameters based on daily new case counts. Provided these parameters remain relatively stable, the model forecasts future daily cases. However, if a parameter shifts due to the dynamic nature of the pandemic, SUTRA detects this change, relearns the updated values, and adjusts its trajectory predictions accordingly. This approach is scalable across various levels of granularity, from national to district levels, as long as daily case data is accessible. We applied SUTRA to 32 countries representing over half the global population, yielding three main conclusions: (i) the model accurately reproduces historical trends, and its robustly estimated parameters allow for the quantification of shifts in pandemic dynamics; (ii) the model demonstrates strong predictive power when pandemic characteristics remain stable; and (iii) natural immunity offers substantially superior protection against infection compared to currently available vaccines.

We demonstrate that the deterministic decision tree complexity of a (partial) function or relation $f$ extends to the deterministic parity decision tree (PDT) size complexity of the composed function/relation $f \circ g$, provided the gadget $g$ exhibits a property we term "stifling." We note that various simple gadgets of constant size—including Indexing on 3 bits, Inner Product on 4 bits, Majority on 3 bits, and random functions—satisfy this condition. While existing randomized communication lifting theorems ([G\"{o}\"{o}s, Pitassi, Watson. SICOMP'20], [Chattopadhyay et al. SICOMP'21]) imply PDT-size lifting, this approach has two limitations: first, it lifts the randomized decision tree complexity of $f$, which may be exponentially smaller than its deterministic complexity for partial functions or total search problems; second, the gadget sizes in these theorems scale logarithmically with the input size of $f$. Reducing gadget sizes to constants remains a significant open problem. Our findings indicate that even a random constant-size gadget facilitates lifting to PDT size. Furthermore, this result provides the first systematic method for converting lower bounds on the width of tree-like resolution proofs for unsatisfiable constant-width CNF formulas into lower bounds on the size of tree-like proofs within the resolution with parity system ($\textit{Res}$($\oplus$)) for closely related constant-width CNF formulas.

This study details the creation of a van der Waals tunneling device containing a defect-bound quantum dot coupled to NbSe$_2$. When a magnetic field is applied, the device displays a zero-bias conductance peak that splits at elevated field strengths, indicating a Kondo effect. Simultaneously, the junction maintains standard quasiparticle tunneling characteristics at finite bias. The simultaneous presence of a superconducting gap and a Kondo effect is atypical; however, it is attributed to the two-gap superconducting state of NbSe$_2$, where a magnetic field suppresses the low-energy gap linked to the Se band. Our findings demonstrate that van der Waals architectures, particularly those incorporating defect-bound dots, offer a promising and versatile platform for exploring the interaction between Kondo screening and superconducting pairing in unconventional superconductors.

Distance covariance serves as a widely adopted metric for assessing dependence between two random vectors, $X$ and $Y$, which may vary in dimension and type. While recent research has predominantly focused on the distributional characteristics of sample distance covariance in high-dimensional contexts under the assumption of independence, this study establishes the inaugural non-null central limit theorem for both the sample distance covariance and the more comprehensive sample (Hilbert-Schmidt) kernel distance covariance, chiefly within the Gaussian framework. This new theorem provides an asymptotically precise first-order power formula for the commonly employed generalized kernel distance correlation test used to evaluate independence. Notably, the derived power formula reveals a striking universality phenomenon: in the high-dimensional limit, the test's power is entirely governed by the quantity $n\cdot \text{dcor}^2(X,Y)/\sqrt{2}$, irrespective of specific kernel choices or bandwidth settings. Additionally, this separation rate is proven to be minimax optimal. The central proof technique relies on a meticulous expansion of the mean and variance of the sample distance covariance in high dimensions, demonstrating that the non-null Gaussian approximation hinges on a nuanced interaction between the dimension-to-sample ratio and the underlying dependence structure of $X$ and $Y$.

The characteristics of crystalline materials are heavily dictated by the population of dislocation defects, making the analysis of these defects in experimental samples highly valuable. While direct counting via transmission electron microscopy is useful, quantitative analysis of x-ray diffraction line profiles serves as a crucial complementary technique. As an indirect quantification method, this approach necessitates rigorous validation of the underlying physical models. In this study, we directly assess the capability of line profile analysis to quantify dislocation and stacking fault populations by utilizing atomistic models of deformed copper single crystals. We first analyze these models to establish precise defect details, serving as our "ground truth." Subsequently, we generate theoretical line profiles for these models and process them using the same methods applied to experimental data. This allows us to compare inferred defect measures against the exact known values. Our findings demonstrate that line profile analysis can reliably predict both dislocation density and stacking fault fractions across two orders of magnitude. Additionally, we illustrate how the outer cut-off radius for mean-square strain in the Warren and Averbach framework corresponds to the cell size in artificially constructed restrictedly-random dislocation distributions based on Wilkens' model. Collectively, these results provide significant new validation for employing line profile analysis to quantify line and planar defects in crystalline materials.

Deploying machine learning models in high-stakes environments like healthcare relies not just on accuracy but also on fairness, robustness, and interpretability. While Generalized Additive Models (GAMs) offer interpretability and a long track record in these fields, they miss key deep learning capabilities such as differentiability and scalability. This study introduces NODE-GAM and NODE-GA$^2$M, neural architectures that scale effectively and outperform traditional GAMs on large datasets while maintaining interpretability superior to other ensemble and deep learning approaches. We demonstrate that these models uncover meaningful data patterns. Furthermore, we show that self-supervised pre-training enhances model accuracy—a benefit unavailable to non-differentiable GAMs.

The minimal $U(1)_X$ extension of the Standard Model (SM) represents a straightforward and theoretically motivated framework that enhances the SM by incorporating the seesaw mechanism to naturally account for light neutrino masses, alongside diverse phenomenological implications. Within this model, the $U(1)_X$ charge assigned to every SM field is defined by the charge of the SM Higgs doublet, denoted by the free parameter $x_H$. Consequently, when $x_H \neq 0$, the Higgs boson acquires a trilinear interaction involving the $Z$ boson and the $U(1)_X$ gauge boson ($Z^\prime$). This interaction facilitates a novel associated production channel for the Higgs boson in conjunction with a $Z$ boson, mediated by a $Z^\prime$ boson in the $s$-channel at high-energy colliders. This study calculates the cross-sections for this associated Higgs production at both high-energy proton-proton and electron-positron colliders, demonstrating distinctive signatures from the $Z^\prime$-mediated process that are amenable to experimental verification in the near future.

Three-dimensional (3D) freehand ultrasound (US) reconstruction, which operates without a tracker, offers significant advantages over tracked or 2D methods in numerous clinical settings. This study introduces a method to estimate 3D spatial transformations between US frames by leveraging both preceding and subsequent 2D images through feed-forward and recurrent neural networks (RNNs). By utilizing temporally accessible frames, we developed a multi-task learning algorithm that exploits a vast number of auxiliary tasks for predicting transformations. Validated using over 40,000 US frames collected from 38 forearms of 19 volunteers (228 scans total), the hold-out test performance was measured via frame prediction accuracy, volume reconstruction overlap, accumulated tracking error, and final drift, with ground truth provided by an optical tracker. Results highlight the critical importance of modeling temporally and spatially correlated input frames and output transformations, noting that performance improves with additional past and/or future frames. The top-performing model predicted transformations between moderately spaced frames, specifically at an interval of fewer than ten frames at 20 fps. No significant benefit was observed by incorporating frames more than one second away from the target transformation, regardless of whether LSTM-based RNNs were used. Notably, the proposed approach suggests that explicit within-sequence losses designed to ensure transformation consistency or minimize accumulated error may be unnecessary. To ensure reproducibility and facilitate future research, the implementation code and volunteer data will be made publicly available.

We examine Rumin's filtration applied to the de Rham complex of a Carnot group. While the Pansu pullback induced by a Sobolev map maintains the filtration structure, it does not necessarily constitute a chain map. However, we demonstrate that this Pansu pullback generates a mapping between the corresponding spectral sequences. This result offers an alternative perspective on the Pullback Theorem presented in our earlier work.

Segmenting ventricles from cardiac magnetic resonance (MRI) images is a primary step in diagnosing various cardiac conditions, including coronary heart disease and pulmonary hypertension. Although manually outlining the right ventricle demands significant time and effort, automated segmentation remains difficult because of irregular shapes and ambiguous boundaries. This study introduces a deep learning approach designed to accurately segment the right ventricle without the need for post-processing, achieving state-of-the-art results on the RVSC-MICCAI 2012 dataset with a Dice coefficient of 0.86 and a Hausdorff distance of 6.73 mm. To address severe class imbalance within the dataset, we employ a novel adaptive cost function. Furthermore, we conduct a thorough comparative analysis of loss functions, network architectures, and ensembling strategies to establish a robust framework for biomedical segmentation.

The Information and Communication Technology (ICT) sector is fundamentally transforming both household appliances and industrial operations. The rise of emerging technologies—such as Cloud and Fog computing, the Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Blockchain—underscores the expanding role of ICT across business, education, healthcare, and domestic settings, thereby driving unprecedented data generation. Projections indicate that by 2025, 75 billion devices will process over 175 zettabytes (ZB) of data annually. Additionally, 5G mobile technology significantly boosts network speeds, facilitating real-time uploads of ultra-high-definition videos and creating substantial streams of big data. Moreover, AI-enabled smart devices, functioning autonomously like self-driving vehicles, further contribute to this surge in data production. This rapid expansion and the resulting massive volume of heterogeneous data present severe challenges regarding storage and management. This article provides a comprehensive review of current issues and obstacles in storing big data, along with proposed countermeasures from security and management standpoints, and explores future prospects for cloud storage. The study details these challenges and identifies emerging research dynamics within the field of cloud storage.

Optimization problems incorporating sparsity constraints represent a significant category of global optimization challenges. Conventional thresholding algorithms for these problems typically utilize traditional steepest descent or Newton-like directions to generate iterates, followed by a specific thresholding operation. However, traditional hard thresholding often discards substantial portions of dense vectors, resulting in the loss of critical information. Recent research by Zhao (SIAM J Optim, 30(1), pp. 31-55, 2020) suggests that applying hard thresholding to compressible rather than dense vectors helps mitigate this information loss. Conversely, optimal $k$-thresholding offers a novel approach that overcomes the inherent limitations of hard thresholding by performing both thresholding and objective function minimization concurrently. This paper proposes the Partial Gradient Optimal Thresholding (PGROTP) method, which integrates partial gradients with optimal $k$-thresholding. We establish solution error bounds and convergence properties for this algorithm under appropriate conditions and discuss its application to sparse optimization problems in signal recovery. Experimental results using synthetic data demonstrate that the PGROTP algorithm is efficient and performs comparably to several existing methods.

Hole doping in Nd${}_{2}$NiO${}_{4.00}$ can be realized through the substitution of trivalent Nd ions with divalent alkaline earth metals or via oxygen doping to form Nd${}_{2}$NiO${}_{4+\delta}$. This study examines the interaction between oxygen and spin ordering in the low-oxygen-doping regime of Nd${}_{2}$NiO${}_{4.10}$. Despite the relatively low doping level, where only one of the twenty available interstitial tetrahedral sites is occupied, single-crystal neutron diffraction reveals a complex three-dimensional modulated structure linked to oxygen ordering even at ambient conditions. The modulation vectors are identified as $\pm$2/13\textit{\textbf{a*}}$\pm$3/13\textit{\textbf{b*}}, $\pm$3/13\textit{\textbf{b*}}$\pm$2/13\textit{\textbf{b*}}, and $\pm$1/5\textit{\textbf{a*}}$\pm$1/2\textit{\textbf{c*}}, with satellite reflections extending up to the fourth order. Temperature-dependent neutron diffraction indicates that oxygen and magnetic ordering coexist below the Néel temperature ($T_{N} \simeq$ 48 K), with the Ni sublattice wave vector defined as \textbf{\textit{k}}=(100). Furthermore, magnetic satellite reflections exhibit the exact same modulation vectors as the oxygen ordering, confirming a unique simultaneous 3D modulated arrangement for both spin and oxygen structures in Nd${}_{2}$NiO${}_{4.10}$. Analysis of temperature-dependent magnetic intensities suggests two magnetic phase transitions occurring below 48 K and 20 K, signifying distinct onset temperatures for magnetic ordering in the Ni and Nd sublattices, respectively.

As the second installment in a series examining the initial perturbation of mean curvature flow, this work investigates cases where the first singularity resembles an asymptotic conical shrinker. The noncompact nature of this limiting shrinker presents significant challenges. To address these, we apply the Feynman-Kac formula to determine the precise asymptotic behavior of the linearized rescaled mean curvature equation along an orbit and adapt the invariant cone method for non-compact settings to analyze local dynamics near the shrinker. Consequently, we demonstrate that under a generic initial perturbation, the rescaled mean curvature flow successfully avoids the conical singularity.

Analyzing facial attributes in real-world scenarios is highly challenging due to complex variations in faces. Current approaches typically rely on cropped and aligned face images, which makes attribute prediction heavily dependent on the accuracy of face detection preprocessing. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel deep architecture that jointly learns both facial attribute analysis and face detection. Our framework is capable of processing natural images directly, and experiments on the CelebA and LFWA datasets demonstrate that it achieves state-of-the-art performance.

Although early formulations of Bell's theorem treated factorizability as the direct expression of locality, Bell later contended that factorizability follows from the more foundational concept of local causality. This paper demonstrates that, contrary to widespread belief, deriving factorizability from local causality necessitates an additional, non-trivial assumption that is similar to yet strictly independent of settings independence. Essentially, this extra condition requires the independence of the measurement apparatus states. We conclude that models can be constructed which adhere to both local causality and settings independence; however, by violating this supplementary assumption—and consequently factorizability—such models can still violate Bell's inequality.

This study examines the Aharonov-Bohm effect on the ground state of a confined electron within a quantum ring electrostatically defined in a phosphorene monolayer. Due to the strong anisotropy of effective masses in phosphorene, ground-state oscillations are suppressed in a circular ring configuration, as this anisotropy interrupts the circulation of persistent currents. However, deforming the confinement potential into an ellipse can offset this mass anisotropy, thereby restoring ground-state parity transformations that align with AB periodicity. Furthermore, a specific ratio of the ellipse's semi-axes yields an energy spectrum identical to that of a circular ring with isotropic effective mass. We identify a generalized angular momentum operator that commutes with the continuum Hamiltonian at this specific semi-axis ratio, which resolves the avoided crossings of energy levels for states sharing the same parity and spin. Additionally, we analyze ground-state oscillations for the two-electron ground state.

This work revises the finite element formulation for Lagrange, Raviart-Thomas, and Taylor-Hood spaces. We address the Laplace equation using both first- and second-order formulations, comparing results from Lagrange and Raviart-Thomas spaces by varying the polynomial order of shape functions and mesh refinement. Furthermore, we solve the Navier-Stokes equations in a two-dimensional steady-state domain and a three-dimensional domain exhibiting turbulent behavior. All numerical experiments are conducted using the MFEM library, which is also analyzed.

This paper examines the unique mild solution $u(t,x)$ of a one-dimensional stochastic heat equation defined on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R$, which is driven by time-homogeneous white noise interpreted in the Wick-Skorokhod sense. The primary contribution is the derivation of the spatial derivative, $\partial_x u(t,x)$, expressed as a closed-form Feynman-Kac formula. Furthermore, utilizing the chaos expansion of this derivative, the study determines its optimal Hölder regularity, particularly with respect to the spatial variable.

This paper introduces a straightforward method for achieving macro photography (enlarged images) using a smartphone or tablet. We first outline the technique, which involves placing a water droplet on the camera lens. Subsequently, we examine potential applications for science education at primary and secondary levels. As highlighted in the discussion, the method's simplicity and effectiveness could make it a valuable instructional resource across various fields, including biology, physics, and general science.

Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly employed across various military and civilian sectors, including data acquisition and surveillance. A dependable network for command, control, and data exchange is essential for both mission success and safety. Existing cellular networks serve as suitable candidates for UAV connectivity due to their extensive coverage and robust security, though their reliability warrants thorough examination. This study utilizes Long-Term Evolution (LTE) infrastructure to support drone communication and data transfer in a rural setting. We analyze the communication performance of LTE-connected drones during low-altitude operations across varying altitudes and speeds. Our findings indicate that in such environments, higher flight elevations yield superior signal quality and result in fewer handovers. Additionally, increased flight speeds cause a slight decline in communication performance.

Functional spatio-temporal data frequently emerge in environmental and climate contexts, where observations are gathered across a three-dimensional spatial domain over time. Originally developed for modeling multivariate space-time data, the MATLAB D-STEM v1 software suite has recently evolved into D-STEM v2 to accommodate functional data indexed by both space and time. This paper outlines the enhanced modeling features of D-STEM v2 alongside the complexity reduction methods necessary for managing extensive datasets. Two case studies illustrate the processes of model estimation, validation, and dynamic kriging: one focusing on ground-level air quality in Beijing, China, and the other on globally collected atmospheric profile data via radio sounding.

The CMS collaboration has measured the transverse momentum ($p_T$) spectra of charged particles across different collision centralities in PbPb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 2.76$ TeV. These findings are benchmarked against a pp reference spectrum, derived by interpolating data from measurements at $\sqrt{s}$ values of 0.9 and 7 TeV. The nuclear modification factor ($R_{AA}$) is calculated by dividing the PbPb $p_T$ spectrum, normalized by the number of binary collisions ($N_{coll}$), by the pp spectrum. Furthermore, the measured $R_{AA}$ for the 0–5% centrality bin is evaluated against various theoretical models.

Although videos depict continuous events, most existing video synthesis frameworks handle them discretely over time. This work reimagines videos as time-continuous signals and extends neural representations to create a continuous-time video generator. We begin by designing continuous motion representations using positional embeddings. Next, we investigate training on extremely sparse video data, demonstrating that an effective generator can be learned with as few as two frames per clip. We then reformulate the traditional image-video discriminator pair into a holistic discriminator that aggregates temporal information by concatenating frame features. This approach reduces training costs and offers a richer learning signal, enabling direct training on 1024² videos for the first time. Built upon StyleGAN2, our model incurs only about 5% higher training costs at the same resolution while achieving nearly identical image quality. Furthermore, our latent space exhibits similar properties, allowing spatial manipulations to propagate temporally. We can generate videos of arbitrary length and frame rate, whereas previous methods struggle to produce even 64 frames at a fixed rate. Our model is evaluated on four modern 256² benchmarks and one 1024² benchmark. In terms of quantitative metrics, it outperforms the closest competitor by approximately 30% on average. Project website: https://universome.github.io.

Real-world situations often compel humans to navigate complex trade-offs, such as deciding whether to adhere strictly to traffic regulations or break speed limits during emergencies. These instances require weighing collective norms against individual goals and desires. To build effective AI-human collaborations, artificial agents must be endowed with a model of how humans balance these competing factors within complex environments governed by both explicit and implicit rules. Agents equipped with such models can either mimic human behavior or highlight decision-making scenarios that could be optimized. In response, we introduce a novel Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) approach called Max Entropy Inverse Soft Constraint IRL (MESC-IRL). This method learns implicit hard and soft constraints regarding states, actions, and state features from demonstrations across both deterministic and non-deterministic environments, which are modeled as Markov Decision Processes (MDPs). Our approach allows agents to infer human constraints and preferences without requiring explicit modeling by designers and facilitates the transfer of these constraints across different environments. Furthermore, this method generalizes previous research that focused solely on deterministic hard constraints, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

The Logistics Specification and Analysis Tool (LSAT) serves as a model-based engineering instrument for designing and analyzing manufacturing systems. Within LSAT, systems are defined using a domain-specific language. This paper introduces a conversion approach that translates an LSAT specification into an automata structure to determine system behavior.

Both the ATLAS and CMS experiments at the LHC have observed a particle with a mass near 125 GeV, consistent with the Standard Model (SM) Higgs boson, yet both report an event excess in the diphoton decay channel beyond SM predictions. This leaves open the possibility that the observed particle is not the SM Higgs but rather a different entity. This paper introduces a minimal dilaton model where LHC signals are attributed to an additional singlet scalar, approximately 125 GeV in mass, which slightly mixes with a heavier SM Higgs (mass > 600 GeV). If this scalar possesses a vacuum expectation value significantly exceeding the electroweak scale, it represents a linearly realized dilaton field. Although current Higgs search constraints disfavor this specific parameter region, the singlet scalar framework remains a viable alternative to the SM Higgs for interpreting experimental results.

Recent research indicates that recommendation systems frequently encounter popularity bias, a phenomenon where frequently rated items are over-recommended while less popular ones are neglected. Scholars have investigated this issue through two lenses: (i) assessing how much the system's output deviates from user expectations regarding popular items, and (ii) measuring the exposure of long-tail items via catalog coverage and novelty metrics. This paper focuses on the first perspective within the book domain, though the insights are transferable to other areas. Utilizing the Book-Crossing dataset, we categorized users into three groups based on their preference for popular items: Niche, Diverse, and Bestseller-focused. We then evaluated nine state-of-the-art algorithms alongside two baselines (Random and MostPop) using both accuracy metrics (such as NDCG, Precision, and Recall) and popularity bias measures. Our findings reveal that most advanced algorithms exhibit significant popularity bias in the book domain, failing to satisfy the expectations of Niche and Diverse users despite their larger profile sizes. In contrast, Bestseller-focused users consistently receive higher-quality recommendations regarding both fairness and personalization. Additionally, our study highlights a trade-off between personalization and the unfairness of popularity bias for users in the Diverse and Bestseller groups; specifically, algorithms capable of high personalization tend to suffer more from popularity bias unfairness.

This study utilizes JWST-MIRI MRS spectra from the MIRI mid-INfrared Disk Survey (MINDS) GTO program to examine the protoplanetary disk surrounding the low-mass T Tauri star GW Lup. We identify emission from $^{12}$CO$_{2}$, $^{13}$CO$_{2}$, H$_{2}$O, HCN, and C$_{2}$H$_{2}$, marking the first detection of $^{13}$CO$_{2}$ in a protoplanetary disk. By analyzing these molecules, we characterize the physical and chemical environment within the inner few astronomical units of the disk. The high spectral resolution of JWST-MIRI MRS combined with high signal-to-noise data is crucial for identifying these species and determining their column densities and temperatures; notably, the Q-branches, including hot-bands, are highly sensitive to these parameters. Our results indicate that $^{12}$CO$_{2}$ emission in the GW Lup disk is intense, arising from optically thick regions at approximately 500 K. In contrast, $^{13}$CO$_{2}$ is optically thinner, traces a larger and deeper emitting area within the disk, and corresponds to a lower temperature of roughly 200 K. The derived $N_{\rm{CO_{2}}}$/$N_{\rm{H_{2}O}}$ ratio of 0.25 is notably higher than values obtained from other targets using \textit{Spitzer}-IRS data. This elevated abundance ratio may result from an inner cavity in the gas and dust located between the H$_{2}$O and CO$_{2}$ snowlines, or from a dust trap at this location preventing water-rich icy grains from crossing the water snowline. This work highlights JWST's unique capacity to investigate inner disk structures and chemistry by detecting previously unseen weak molecular features.

In prior research, we established a search methodology for staus arising from the decay of the heavy CP-even Higgs boson $H$ within the minimal supersymmetric standard model (MSSM), specifically under conditions of large $\tan\beta$ and significant stau mixing. This study evaluates the efficacy of that strategy by testing it against a complementary mixing framework where both CP-even and CP-odd heavy Higgs bosons contribute to $\widetilde{\tau}_1\widetilde{\tau}_2^{*} \;+\; c.c$ pair production. We continue to concentrate on final states characterized by two opposite-sign tau leptons and substantial missing transverse energy. Our findings indicate that the proposed search strategy, though optimized for the large stau mixing case, retains considerable sensitivity to the complementary mixing pattern. For example, with an integrated luminosity of merely 100 fb$^{-1}$, we can rule out heavy Higgs masses exceeding 850 GeV for average stau masses surpassing 290 GeV. Furthermore, we expand upon the results from the earlier large mixing scenario by presenting exclusion limits at 100 fb$^{-1}$ and assessing both exclusion and discovery prospects for a potential high-luminosity LHC phase (1000 fb$^{-1}$). Lastly, we examine the feasibility of distinguishing between the two mixing scenarios when they exhibit identical relevant mass spectra and both achieve discovery significance using our search approach.

We introduce a novel perturbation technique for calculating specific time transfer functions in a stationary spacetime, where the metric represents a minor deviation from a background metric with known, closed-form solutions. The resulting perturbation terms are formulated as line integrals along the null geodesics of the background metric. Distinct from previous methods, this approach yields time transfer functions entirely devoid of unbounded terms and avoids any increase in light travel time. The method proves highly effective when applied to a linearized Schwarzschild-like background metric. When utilized for an isolated body undergoing slow rotation about a symmetry axis, it generates integrals solvable by any symbolic computation software. We derive explicit formulas for the mass dipole and quadrupole moments, as well as the primary gravitomagnetic term arising from the body's spin. Additionally, a concise numerical analysis is presented regarding the 2002 Cassini experiment.

This paper introduces Clio, an information flow control (IFC) system that seamlessly integrates cryptography to enforce confidentiality and integrity policies on untrusted storage. Clio shields developers from the need to manually handle keys and cryptographic primitives by utilizing the IFC system's policy language to automatically select the correct keys and perform the necessary cryptographic operations. We demonstrate Clio's security using a novel proof technique that combines cryptographic proof styles with standard results from programming language theory. Additionally, we provide a prototype implementation of Clio along with a case study that illustrates its practical viability.
We provide two concise proofs establishing the best-known asymptotic lower bound for the largest element in a set of $n$ positive integers featuring distinct subset sums.

This research investigates the geometry of bilipschitz mappings $f \colon \mathbb{W} \to \mathbb{H}$, where $\mathbb{H}$ denotes the first Heisenberg group and $\mathbb{W}$ represents a vertical subgroup within $\mathbb{H}$ of codimension $1$. The images produced by these maps, known as Rickman rugs in the Heisenberg group, are the central focus. The primary result establishes that any Rickman rug within the Heisenberg group possesses a corona decomposition consisting of intrinsic bilipschitz graphs. Consequently, Rickman rugs are shown to be countably rectifiable via intrinsic bilipschitz graphs. In this context, an intrinsic bilipschitz graph is defined as an intrinsic Lipschitz graph that also qualifies as a Rickman rug. However, general intrinsic Lipschitz graphs are not necessarily Rickman rugs, even locally, as demonstrated by a counterexample provided by Bigolin and Vittone.

Charge noise stands as a primary driver of environmental decoherence in silicon spin qubits, creating a significant barrier to the development of scalable and reproducible qubit fabrication. In this work, we present a detailed characterization of the charge noise environment affecting a quantum dot within a CMOS-fabricated silicon nanowire. By examining various quantum dot configurations, we demonstrate that charge noise can be tuned across two orders of magnitude, spanning from 1 $\mu$eV$^2$ to 100 $\mu$eV$^2$. Specifically, we identify the top interface and reservoirs as the dominant sources of this noise, showing that their impact can be reduced by adjusting the quantum dot's extension. Furthermore, we introduce a new technique for measuring charge noise in the few-electron regime. Our measurements reveal a notably higher noise level of 40 $\mu$eV$^2$ at the single-electron stage, confirming that charge noise is strongly dependent on the electron occupancy of the quantum dot.

This note establishes the rigidity of the sharp Cheng-Yau gradient estimate for positive harmonic functions on surfaces with nonnegative Gaussian curvature, as well as the rigidity of the sharp Li-Yau gradient estimate for positive solutions to the heat equation and associated estimates for Dirichlet Green's functions on Riemannian manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature. Additionally, we derive the corresponding stability results.

We introduce NeSF, a technique for generating 3D semantic fields using only posed RGB images. Instead of traditional 3D representations, our approach utilizes recent advances in implicit neural scene representations, where 3D structure is defined by point-wise functions. By leveraging this framework, we recover 3D density fields and subsequently train a 3D semantic segmentation model supervised by posed 2D semantic maps. Although trained solely on 2D data, NeSF produces 3D-consistent semantic maps from novel camera viewpoints and can be queried at any arbitrary 3D location. Importantly, NeSF is agnostic to the specific density field generation method used, and its performance scales with the quality of the underlying density field. Empirical results show that our method achieves quality comparable to competitive 2D and 3D segmentation baselines on complex, realistically rendered synthetic scenes. NeSF represents the first approach to deliver truly dense 3D scene segmentations with only 2D training supervision, without requiring any semantic input during inference on new scenes. We invite readers to visit our project website for more information.

For a continuous Schrödinger operator $-\Delta + V$ subject to a confining potential, its eigenfunctions exhibit exponential decay, a rate determined by the portion of $V$ exceeding the relevant eigenvalue, a phenomenon quantifiable via Agmon's method. Similar localization characteristics apply to the eigenvectors of discrete Schrödinger matrices. This note surprisingly demonstrates that eigenvector localization estimates remain valid when substituting a discrete Schrödinger matrix with any real symmetric $Z$-matrix. Specifically, for a real symmetric non-singular $M$-matrix $A$—a case common in random matrix theory and statistical physics—the landscape function $u = A^{-1} 1$ serves as an effective localization potential. By deriving an Agmon-type distance function from this potential, one can describe the exponential decay of eigenfunctions away from potential "wells," where individual eigenfunctions typically localize to a single well.

We investigate an array of logical circuits using a mesoscopic, thermodynamically consistent model tailored for modern complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor transistors, examining how recent thermodynamic uncertainty relations constrain their function near thermal energy levels. For a single NOT gate, our analysis reveals direction-dependent dynamics and identifies an optimal balance between dissipated heat and the certainty of operation time. In the case of a memory storage device, we observe an exponential correlation between the energy needed to maintain a state and its retention duration. Regarding a clock, we determine that cycle time certainty and the trade-off between this certainty and heat dissipation per cycle are maximized when biasing voltages are close to thermal energy. Furthermore, we show that a straightforward control mechanism for the clock can ensure a monotonic rise in cycle time certainty with increasing biasing voltage, thereby mitigating performance degradation at high voltages. These findings establish a framework for evaluating the thermodynamic costs of practical computing devices, enabling the design and control of circuits for thermodynamically optimal performance.

This document outlines the scientific rationale for the proposed Daksha mission, a high-energy transient observatory consisting of two satellites designed to survey the entire sky across the 1 keV to >1 MeV energy range. Daksha's primary goals are to identify and characterize electromagnetic counterparts to gravitational wave events and to investigate Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs). As a versatile all-sky monitor featuring broadband spectral capabilities, high sensitivity, and continuous coverage, Daksha is poised to detect fainter and rarer sources than any current or future mission. The mission will advance GRB research through polarization analysis, prompt soft spectroscopy, and high-resolution time-dependent spectral studies. Additionally, Daksha will enable continuous monitoring of X-ray pulsars, detection of magnetar outbursts, and identification of high-energy counterparts to Fast Radio Bursts. By utilizing Earth occultation, the twin-satellite system will deliver daily flux measurements of bright hard X-ray sources such as active galactic nuclei, X-ray binaries, and slow transients like novae. Correlating data from the two satellites will allow for the probing of primordial black holes via gravitational lensing. Furthermore, a dedicated set of detectors continuously aimed at the Sun will provide superior hard X-ray monitoring, while the mission's high sensitivity and temporal resolution will facilitate the characterization of Terrestrial Gamma-ray Flashes.

This research investigates the elliptic sinh-Gordon and sine-Gordon equations defined on the real plane, presenting novel families of solutions. By employing a Bäcklund transformation that links the elliptic forms of these equations, we develop new harmonic maps between surfaces, specifically where the target space possesses a constant curvature of -1.

Transformer-based architectures, including BERT, have significantly enhanced performance across numerous natural language processing (NLP) tasks. Among these, ClinicalBERT, which incorporates clinical knowledge, has attained state-of-the-art results in clinical named entity recognition and natural language inference. However, a primary constraint of standard transformers is their high memory demand, stemming from the full self-attention mechanism. To address this, models like Longformer and BigBird were developed using sparse attention mechanisms, which lower memory complexity from quadratic to linear relative to sequence length. These architectures expanded the maximum input sequence length from 512 to 4096, thereby improving long-term dependency modeling and yielding optimal outcomes in diverse tasks. Drawing inspiration from these advancements, we present two domain-specific language models, Clinical-Longformer and Clinical-BigBird, pre-trained on extensive clinical corpora. We assessed both models across ten baseline tasks, including named entity recognition, question answering, and document classification. Our findings indicate that Clinical-Longformer and Clinical-BigBird consistently and significantly outperform ClinicalBERT and other short-sequence transformers in all downstream applications. The source code is accessible at [https://github.com/luoyuanlab/Clinical-Longformer], and the pre-trained models are available for public download at [https://huggingface.co/yikuan8/Clinical-Longformer].

We examine a non-linear Langevin equation driven by non-Gaussian noise arising from a non-linear bath. We argue that the parameters within the Langevin equation are not physical; instead, physical parameters are derived via a path-integral formulation, where the Langevin parameters are connected to physical ones through renormalization flow equations. Using both numerical and analytical methods, we calculate the two-point velocity function, demonstrating that it saturates to the bath temperature despite non-linearities. Furthermore, we numerically determine the four-point velocity function, showing that it converges to the analytically predicted thermal four-point function when the non-linear Fluctuation-Dissipation Relation (FDR) [1] holds. However, if the non-linear FDR—which reflects the time-reversibility of the thermal bath—is violated, the system fails to thermalize; instead, its four-point velocity function stabilizes at a steady state.

Equation-free modeling seeks to derive low-dimensional macroscopic dynamics from complex, high-dimensional systems that dictate the evolution of microscopic states. This method utilizes lifting and restriction operators to map between macroscopic and microscopic states. By integrating these operators with microscopic simulations, the approach allows for the application of Newton solvers to implicitly defined macroscopic systems or enables more efficient solutions through direct numerical simulation. A primary challenge lies in constructing these operators, which typically demands prior insight into the specific application. In this paper, we introduce an application-independent algorithm that leverages diffusion maps to generate these operators directly from simulation data. The source code is accessible at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5793299.

Defect prediction has emerged as a prominent research area because it holds the promise of reducing software quality assurance workload. While current methods have investigated factors like complexity and developer metrics, no existing study has evaluated programming style for this purpose. This paper investigates how stylistic metrics influence both within-project and cross-project defect prediction. The study employs four established machine learning algorithms: Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine, Decision Tree, and Logistic Regression. Data from 14 releases across five popular open-source projects were used for the experiments, with performance assessed using F1, Precision, and Recall metrics. The findings indicate that stylistic metrics serve as effective predictors for defects.

We tackle the challenge of safely executing complex bimanual robot manipulation tasks under sparse reward conditions. These difficult problems can be broken down into sub-tasks performed either concurrently or sequentially by different robots to enhance efficiency. Although prior reinforcement learning methods mainly address the compositionality of sub-tasks, two critical issues are often overlooked when learning cooperative strategies for dual robots: (i) domination, where one robot attempts to complete a task alone, leaving the other inactive; and (ii) conflict, where one robot interrupts another's workspace during simultaneous sub-task execution, resulting in unsafe collisions. To resolve these challenges, we introduce a novel technique called disentangled attention, which offers intrinsic regularization to ensure both robots focus on distinct sub-tasks and objects. We evaluated this approach across five bimanual manipulation tasks. Results demonstrate that our proposed intrinsic regularization effectively prevents domination and minimizes conflicts, yielding significantly more efficient and safer cooperative policies compared to all baselines. Project materials and videos are available at https://mehooz.github.io/bimanual-attention.

Current volumetric gain calculations for robotic exploration rely on 3D occupancy maps, whereas sampling-based methods operate within reachable free space. This mismatch renders existing gain calculations unsuitable for comprehensive environmental exploration. To resolve this, we introduce a concave-hull-based volumetric gain metric integrated into a sampling-based framework. This concave hull is formed using viewpoints from a Rapidly-exploring Random Tree (RRT) and nodes that could not expand, with any area outside this hull designated as unknown. By computing volumetric gain based on viewpoint configurations rather than occupancy maps, our approach prevents the inefficient or erroneous exploration behaviors caused by previous methods. We evaluated this strategy against the current state-of-the-art RRT-based approach in a benchmark environment, demonstrating that our method requires only 38.4% of the average running time of existing solutions while exhibiting greater robustness.

Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) and adaptive sharpness-aware minimization (ASAM) are designed to enhance model generalization. This project validates their generalization capabilities from a sharpness-aware perspective through three experiments. The results indicate that optimization techniques based on sharpness awareness can significantly improve a model's generalization ability. Additionally, our findings suggest that ASAM enhances generalization performance on un-normalized data, though further research is required to confirm this observation.

Social and behavioral researchers are increasingly utilizing technologies like fMRI, smartphones, and gene sequencing to generate 'high-dimensional' datasets characterized by more variables than observations. While interest in understanding how these variables function within established processes is growing, substantive theoretical frameworks remain scarce. This gap necessitates exploratory mediation analysis, for which structural equation modeling serves as the standard; however, this technique fails when the number of variables exceeds the number of observations. Alternative strategies include running multiple univariate mediation models, which erroneously assume mediator independence, or applying regularization, which can result in elevated false positive rates in current implementations. This paper introduces a hybrid 'Coordinate-wise Mediation Filter' approach that integrates elements of both filtering and regularization by performing filtering conditional on other selected mediators. Simulation results demonstrate that this method outperforms existing techniques, and an empirical application illustrates its utility in epigenetic research.

Conducting code reviews with a security focus is notoriously challenging; prior research indicates that developers frequently overlook even well-known and easily identifiable vulnerabilities. Early findings suggest this oversight stems largely from reviewers' mental attitudes and habitual practices. This study examines whether explicitly instructing developers to prioritize security during reviews enhances vulnerability detection and evaluates the additional impact of providing a security checklist. To address these questions, we conducted an online experiment involving 150 participants, 71% of whom possess at least three years of professional development experience. Our findings reveal that merely prompting reviewers to focus on security increases the likelihood of detecting vulnerabilities by eightfold. However, the inclusion of a security checklist—whether tailored to the specific changes or existing vulnerabilities in the code—did not yield significant further improvements. These results validate the mental attitude hypothesis and highlight the need for further research into optimizing security checklists. Data and materials: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6026291

In a $(G^1, G^2)$ edge coloring of a graph $G$, each edge belongs to either $G^1$ or $G^2$. For two bipartite graphs $H_1$ and $H_2$, the bipartite Ramsey number $BR(H_1, H_2)$ is defined as the smallest integer $b \geq 1$ such that any $(G^1, G^2)$ coloring of the complete bipartite graph $K_{b,b}$ guarantees the presence of $H_1$ as a subgraph of $G^1$ or $H_2$ as a subgraph of $G^2$. Alternatively, for bipartite graphs $H_1, H_2$ and a positive integer $m$, the $m$-bipartite Ramsey number $BR_m(H_1, H_2)$ is the minimum integer $n$ ensuring that every subgraph of $K_{m,n}$ contains either $H_1$ or the complement of $H_2$. While the values of $BR_m(K_{2,2}, K_{2,2})$, $BR_m(K_{2,2}, K_{3,3})$, and $BR_m(K_{3,3}, K_{3,3})$ have been established in prior research, this paper determines the precise value of $BR_m(K_{2,2}, K_{4,4})$ for all $m \geq 2$.

67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko, a Jupiter-family comet, served as the target for the Rosetta mission, which achieved the first successful orbit and landing on a comet. This endeavor was supported by an extensive ground-based observing campaign. We created a pipeline to calibrate and measure the photometry of 67P during its 2016 perihelion passage, utilizing visible-wavelength broadband imaging gathered from various facilities. By using background stars within the field, the pipeline calibrated the comet's brightness to the Pan-STARRS 1 photometric system, enabling the compilation and comparison of multiple datasets. The results align with predictions from previous apparitions: 67P exhibits no significant changes in activity levels between orbits, and coma colors remain stable throughout the apparition. We identified an outburst on August 22, 2015, measuring approximately 0.14 mag. The brightness and estimated mass of this event are consistent with outbursts directly observed on the nucleus by Rosetta. Although an in situ outburst was detected simultaneously with the ground-based observation, directly linking these two events remains challenging.
We provide corrections regarding the proofs of theorems in the paper "Opial inequality in q-Calculus," where q-Opial type integral inequalities were established.

We utilize standard gravitational wave inference techniques on binary black hole merger waveforms generated by dynamical Chern-Simons gravity, a modified theory rooted in string and loop quantum gravity. This framework incorporates a length-scale parameter $\ell$, marking the threshold where quantum gravity effects emerge. Using numerical relativity simulations that diverge from general relativity predictions in the strong-field merger phase, we generate data for systems analogous to GW150914 across various $\ell$ values and signal-to-noise ratios. Our study involves two distinct analytical approaches: a template-based method employing general relativity waveforms to reveal degeneracies between the two theories, and a morphology-independent BayesWave analysis that does not presuppose consistency with general relativity. While BayesWave successfully reconstructs the simulated signals, general relativity waveform models fail to fully replicate the modified-gravity signatures, indicating that such deviations are detectable with current tools. Furthermore, we observe that templated analyses may underperform compared to morphology-independent methods in recovering beyond-general-relativity waveforms, even at achievable signal-to-noise ratios of $\gtrsim 20\text{--}30$, depending on the magnitude of $\ell$.

This study introduces a deep learning framework designed to derive luminosity, effective temperature, and surface gravity for O-type stars based on their optical spectra. Building on prior research that evaluated various machine and deep learning techniques to fit stellar models via classification and regression, this work details a neural network approach capable of estimating individual physical parameters even when the signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) is below 20. The paper outlines the development of three distinct recurrent neural network architectures, their training on synthetic stellar spectra, and validation against nine observed spectra, including a comparison with previous findings. Furthermore, it discusses methods for characterizing stellar spectra to reduce input dimensionality and optimize computational efficiency.

To search for neutrinoless double-$\beta$ decay in $^{76}$Ge, experiments utilize germanium detectors where the source and detector are the same material. Enhancing the detector mass is crucial for the success of upcoming studies. This report details the characterization and testing of five prototype detectors fabricated in inverted coaxial (IC) geometry using material enriched to 88% in $^{76}$Ge. IC detectors merge the substantial mass of traditional semi-coaxial Ge detectors with the superior resolution and pulse shape discrimination capabilities of point contact detectors, which have historically been limited to lower masses. Performance tests yielded satisfactory results both when the detectors were operated inside a vacuum cryostat and when placed bare in liquid argon within the GERDA setup. At the double-$\beta$ decay Q-value of $^{76}$Ge (Q$_{\beta\beta}$ = 2039 keV), the measured resolutions achieved approximately 2.1 keV full width at half maximum in the vacuum cryostat. Following 18 months of operation within the ultra-low background environment of the GERmanium Detector Array (GERDA) experiment, with an accumulated exposure of 8.5 kg$\cdot$yr, the background index after analysis cuts was determined to be $4.9^{+7.3}_{-3.4}\times 10^{-4}$ counts/(keV$\cdot$kg$\cdot$yr) around Q$_{\beta\beta}$. These findings confirm that IC detectors are viable for the next-generation LEGEND experiment.

For neutron star mergers detected via gravitational waves (GW), the most prominent candidate for an electromagnetic (EM) counterpart is the afterglow produced by an ultra-relativistic jet. When observed, this afterglow is typically viewed off-axis, as exemplified by the case of GW170817/GRB 170817A. Analyzing the temporal evolution of such off-axis afterglows allows researchers to infer the jet's lateral structure and statistically constrain model parameters, including the system's inclination relative to the line of sight. Combined with GW data, afterglow modeling offers the tightest constraints on this inclination, thereby refining cosmological parameter estimates like the Hubble constant derived from GW-EM events. Nevertheless, afterglow modeling relies on assumptions regarding jet structure and frequently neglects lateral spreading. This study demonstrates how incorporating lateral spreading into afterglow models can significantly alter the estimated inclination of GW-EM events.

This letter introduces a unified framework for designing prescribed-time controllers that handle time-varying input and state constraints for normal-form nonlinear systems with unknown dynamics and uncertain input gains. The methodology relies on a time-domain mapping technique, which establishes a correspondence between any infinite-time system and a prescribed-time system in both directions. It is demonstrated that designing a constrained nonasymptotic prescribed-time controller can be simplified into an asymptotic control design problem for a related constrained infinite-time system. To constructively represent this associated infinite-time system, Faà di Bruno's formula and Bell polynomials are employed. The proposed results are flexible as they are not limited to a specific mapping function. Furthermore, necessary and sufficient conditions for uniform (practical) prescribed-time stability and attractivity are derived as corollaries of the primary findings.

Using the variational Monte Carlo method, we examine how correlation effects influence spin-orbit coupling (SOC) within a two-orbital Hubbard model defined on a square lattice. Our analysis focuses on an effective SOC constant, $\lambda_{\text{eff}}$, incorporated into the one-body component of the variational wave function, with particular emphasis on the quarter-filling regime ($n=1$). We observe that $\lambda_{\text{eff}}$ scales linearly with the bare SOC value $\lambda$ and varies with electron-electron interactions via the $(U'-J')$ term across a broad parameter range in the paramagnetic (PM) phase, where $U'$ represents the interorbital Coulomb repulsion and $J'$ the pair hopping. In this PM phase, strengthening electron-electron interactions drives a transition to an effective one-band state, rendering the upper band empty as $\lambda_{\text{eff}}$ increases. Additionally, we map out phase diagrams that account for magnetic ordering and analyze the impact of carrier doping on $\lambda_{\text{eff}}$. Our findings indicate that $\lambda_{\text{eff}}$ is enhanced in strongly correlated regions near the Mott transition, necessitating the inclusion of correlation effects beyond the Hartree-Fock approximation to accurately describe this boosted SOC.

We examine a spatially flat Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker background containing an ideal gas and a multifield Lagrangian composed of two minimally coupled scalar fields evolving within a field space of constant curvature. For this cosmological framework, we categorize the scalar field potential to ensure the existence of variational point symmetries and derive the associated conservation laws. Furthermore, we present analytic solutions for specific potential forms where the cosmological field equations form a Liouville integrable system via point symmetries. The model's free parameters are restricted to yield analytic solutions describing an inflationary epoch, and we subsequently analyze the stability of these exact closed-form solutions, which represent scaling solutions with significant physical implications for the model.

This paper calculates the number of $n$-dimensional representations for a dihedral group $G$ of order $2m$ (where $m \geq 3$) for any positive integer $n$, and determines the dimensions of the associated spaces of $G$-invariant bilinear forms over the complex field $\mathbb{C}$. We explicitly address the existence of non-degenerate invariant bilinear forms. These findings are significant because of their applications in physical sciences.

Out-of-distribution detection (OOD) addresses the challenge of identifying anomalous inputs for neural networks. While specialized methods have historically been developed to reject such predictions, research has also demonstrated that combining feature extraction models with outlier detection algorithms is highly effective for this purpose. Our approach utilizes outlier detection algorithms to identify anomalous inputs with reliability comparable to dedicated OOD methods. This process requires no adaptation of the neural network and relies solely on the model's softmax scores. The method operates unsupervised using an Isolation Forest and can achieve further improvements by incorporating a supervised learning technique like Gradient Boosting.

This paper investigates the joint design of waveforms and passive beamforming for wireless power transfer (WPT) systems assisted by intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS). Using an alternating optimization framework, we develop both generalized multi-user and low-complexity single-user algorithms to maximize weighted sum DC output current, adhering to transmit power limits and unit modulus constraints on IRS phase shifts. The proposed approach jointly optimizes the input signal waveform and IRS phase shifts based on users' individual frequency-selective channel state information (CSI). We analyze two IRS deployment configurations—frequency-selective IRS (FS-IRS) and frequency-flat IRS (FF-IRS)—while accounting for the nonlinearity of energy harvesters. Our findings demonstrate that IRS can offer additional passive beamforming gains in DC output power compared to conventional WPT methods and significantly impact waveform design by exploiting passive beamforming, frequency diversity, and harvester nonlinearity. Although FF-IRS yields lower DC current than FS-IRS, it still achieves a substantial increase in DC power relative to traditional WPT designs. Performance evaluations validate that jointly optimizing waveforms and passive beamforming while considering energy harvester nonlinearity significantly enhances the performance of both single-user and multi-user WPT systems.

Despite the introduction of multi-factor authentication schemes that strengthened existing verification methods, these systems have proven susceptible to increasingly advanced and targeted attacks. This study introduces an innovative two-factor authentication framework that integrates honeytokens into the verification process. Currently, the system functions in conjunction with Google Authenticator. The proposed method's distinctiveness and straightforward design are intended to enhance overall system security by adding extra protective layers through a more robust and efficient authentication mechanism.

Numerous mesons exhibiting characteristics inconsistent with a $\bar cc$ configuration have already been identified, such as the isospin-1 $Z_c$ mesons. This work employs lattice QCD to examine the spectrum of exotic charmonium-like mesons, specifically targeting $\bar cc \bar qq$ states with $J^{PC}=1^{+\pm}$ and isospin 1. As the inaugural investigation of four-quark states possessing these quantum numbers, non-zero total momentum, and two distinct lattice volumes, we derive energy levels and calculate the scattering length for $D\bar D^*$ interactions near the threshold via Lüscher's formalism. Preliminary findings indicate that energy shifts for eigenstates primarily composed of $D\bar{D}^*$ are negligible in the $1^{++}$ channel and consistent with zero in the $1^{+-}$ channel.

Recent research has explored online crowdsourcing fact-checking as a strategy to limit fake news on social media, yet the specific conditions under which this approach successfully curbs misinformation remain ambiguous. To investigate this, we conceptualize distributed fact-checking as "peer policing," a mechanism that lowers the incentive to share false information while incentivizing the propagation of accurate news. Simulations on synthetic square lattices and small-world networks reveal that social network structures facilitate the self-organization of fake news distributors into echo chambers, enhancing the resilience of misinformation against fact-checking efforts. Furthermore, using a Twitter dataset to create a more realistic scenario, we examined the impact of strategically selecting individuals as fact-checkers. Our findings indicate that targeted interventions can be remarkably efficient, achieving equivalent results with only 20% of the fact-checkers typically required, though efficacy varies based on network topology. In the limit of weak selection, we derived analytical formulas for the critical threshold of crowdsourced fact-checking relative to payoff values within our game-theoretic framework. These insights offer practical guidance for designing model-driven strategies to mitigate misinformation that disrupts political discourse.

Research continuously seeks more effective and robust methods to enhance teaching and learning quality. Despite researchers and data scientists striving for transparency and responsibility in analyzing educational data, the danger of training machine learning models on biased datasets remains a persistent threat, potentially resulting in the misinterpretation of student behavior. This risk often arises from an incomplete grasp of how learning log data is generated. Furthermore, as the drive for increasingly user-friendly experiences shifts Learning Management System functionality from servers to clients, a significant byproduct is the reduction of crucial logs. This paper addresses these challenges by presenting examples of learning log data extracted from Moodle and highlighting potential misinterpretations concealed within them, aiming to stimulate a broader discussion on data comprehension and the loss of data knowledge.

Let $B^{H}$ denote a fractional Brownian motion in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ with Hurst parameter $H\in\left(0,1\right)$, where $f:\left[0,1\right]\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}^{d}$ is a Borel function and $A\subset\left[0,1\right]$ is a Borel set. We establish sufficient conditions under which the image $(B^{H}+f)(A)$ possesses a positive Lebesgue measure or a non-empty interior. This analysis relies on investigating the density properties of the occupation measure associated with $(B^{H}+f)$. Specifically, we demonstrate that if the parabolic Hausdorff dimension of the graph of $f$ exceeds $Hd$, the density constitutes a square integrable function. Conversely, if the Hausdorff dimension of $A$ surpasses $Hd$, the density admits a continuous version. These findings enable the derivation of the previously mentioned result.

The significance of parameter selection in supervised learning is widely acknowledged, yet the vast number of possible parameter combinations often leads to inadequate procedures. This deficiency can result in misleading or confusing outcomes. In this opinion paper, we illustrate through a compelling example that the issue is far more severe than commonly understood. Specifically, in the domain of multi-label classification for medical code prediction, an influential study performed rigorous parameter tuning on a full dataset but failed to re-tune parameters when shifting to a subset of frequent labels, instead applying the same settings. This subset subsequently became a standard benchmark, driving subsequent research and claims of advancing the state of the art. However, we found that if the original authors had conducted proper parameter tuning for the subset, later studies would likely not have surpassed their initial results. Consequently, the actual progress made by these follow-up developments remains ambiguous. This case underscores that neglecting thorough parameter selection can render research progress in our field uncertain or even illusory.

We define two permutations, $\pi$ and $\rho$, as having separated descents at position $k$ when $\pi$ lacks descents prior to $k$ and $\rho$ lacks descents subsequent to $k$. This work presents a counting formula based on reduced word tableaux to calculate the structure constants for products of Schubert polynomials associated with such permutations. Our methodology relies on extensions of Schützenberger's jeu de taquin algorithm and the Edelman-Greene correspondence, implemented through bumpless pipe dreams.

The Glosten-Milgrom model characterizes a single-asset market featuring informed traders, a market maker, and noise traders. We establish an analogy between this financial framework and a Szilard information engine by {\em i)} demonstrating that the optimal work extraction protocol in the engine mirrors the market maker's pricing strategy in the financial model, and {\em ii)} defining a market equivalent of physical temperature through the analysis of market order distributions. Furthermore, we prove that the expected gain of informed traders is upper-bounded by the product of this market temperature and the traders' information holdings, precisely paralleling the formula for maximum work extractable from an information engine cycle. This alignment suggests that concepts from information thermodynamics can illuminate financial markets and yield generalized inequalities akin to the extended second law of thermodynamics.

Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) offer a promising avenue for creating wireless networks that are efficient in both spectrum usage and energy consumption. This paper investigates RIS-enhanced orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) communications, extending current research that typically focuses only on frequency-flat channels. First, we present the delay adjustable metasurface (DAM), which utilizes varactor diodes. Unlike conventional reflecting elements, each component in the DAM can store and retrieve incoming electromagnetic waves by dynamically adjusting its electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) characteristics, thereby introducing an additional delay to the reflected signals. Second, we formulate a rate-maximization problem that jointly optimizes transmit power allocation, RIS reflection coefficients, and RIS-induced delays. To handle the coupling between these optimization variables, we propose an efficient algorithm that delivers a high-quality solution for this non-convex problem by alternately optimizing transmit power and the RIS reflection pattern (including coefficients and delays). Third, to reduce the complexity of optimizing RIS reflection coefficients, we develop a low-complexity scheme that aligns the strongest taps of all reflected channels, ensuring that the maximum delay spread after applying extra RIS delays remains within the cyclic prefix (CP) length. Finally, simulation results indicate that the proposed design significantly enhances OFDM rate performance and the RIS's adaptability to wideband signals compared to baseline schemes that do not employ DAM.

This study investigates correlated imaging in the presence of atmospheric turbulence, deriving analytical formulas to quantify how turbulence impacts image resolution. In contrast to direct imaging, correlated imaging mitigates turbulence effects to some degree and enables the reconstruction of high-resolution images. These findings are validated through numerical simulations that model turbulence-induced phase distortions by employing random phase screens within the propagation paths.

Smartphones, tablets, and camera systems, such as those found in vehicles and UAVs, are commonly fitted with IMUs that can precisely measure the gravity vector. Leveraging this data allows for the alignment of camera $y$-axes, thereby reducing their relative orientation to a single degree of freedom. Under this assumption, we introduce a novel solver that achieves global optimality by minimizing algebraic error in the least-squares sense for over-determined relative pose estimation. By utilizing the epipolar constraint, the optimization is transformed into solving two polynomials with just two unknowns. Additionally, a rapid solver is developed based on a first-order approximation of rotation. We evaluate our proposed methods against state-of-the-art approaches on four real-world datasets containing approximately 50,000 image pairs in total. Furthermore, we have compiled a new dataset captured by a smartphone, comprising 10,933 image pairs along with gravity direction data and ground-truth 3D reconstructions.

We present an Eulerian Perturbation Theory designed to analyze tracer clustering in cosmological models containing massive neutrinos. Our methodology involves translating recently derived Lagrangian Perturbation Theory results into the Eulerian framework. By incorporating Effective Field Theory counterterms, IR-resummations, and a biasing scheme, we calculate the one-loop redshift-space power spectrum. To validate these predictions, we compare the resulting power spectrum multipoles with synthetic halo catalogues from the Quijote simulations, observing excellent agreement for scales where $k\lesssim 0.25 \,h \text{Mpc}^{-1}$. While identical fitting precision can be achieved at higher wave-numbers, the theory then fails to accurately estimate the linear bias parameter. We also examine the implications for the tree-level bispectrum. Furthermore, since computing loop corrections is computationally expensive, we develop an accurate approximation that retains only the primary features of the kernels, which arise from modifications to the growth rate. Consequently, we demonstrate how FFTLog techniques can significantly accelerate loop computations using these simplified kernels.

Temporal graphs, which model graph evolution over time, have become a significant focus of research. Existing studies on temporal graph patterns or motifs often rely on simple temporal constraints, such as journeys or existential constraints with finite delays. This paper introduces timed automata to express these constraints, establishing a comprehensive and robust concept of temporal basic graph patterns (BGPs). A primary challenge addressed is evaluating these constraints across extensive sets of matchings. A key advantage of timed automata is their support for iterative state assignment, facilitating early match detection and the pruning of non-matches. We present algorithms to retrieve all instances of temporal BGP matches within a graph and provide results from an extensive experimental evaluation that highlights various performance trade-offs. Our findings indicate that an on-demand algorithm processing total matchings incrementally is superior for cyclic patterns on sparse graphs. Conversely, for acyclic patterns, dense graphs, or scenarios where partial matching connectivity is guaranteed, optimal performance is achieved by maintaining partial matchings over time and enabling fully incremental automaton evaluation.

The Gaia catalog identifies V1311 Ori as part of a compact bound group comprising four active M-type dwarfs situated 39 parsecs away. Kinematic data, isochronal age estimates, and youth indicators such as H-alpha emission, lithium presence, and rapid rotation suggest a likely association with the beta Pictoris and 32 Ori moving groups. The primary component, Star A, is a known close binary with a preliminary 80-year visual-spectroscopic orbit established. Star B has been resolved into a pair separated by 0.08 arcseconds, while stars C and D are likely single. Given the non-hierarchical arrangement with projected separations of approximately 10,000 astronomical units, this pre-main-sequence system may represent either a young sextuple system or a bound but dynamically unstable mini-cluster (trapezium) that has thus far avoided disruption, effectively bridging the gap between moving groups and wide hierarchical systems.
