The prototype features a horn-shaped electron waveguide exhibiting Rashba spin-orbit interaction, connected to two leads of varying widths. It is shown that when electrons enter from the narrow lead, the resulting spin conductance fluctuates near a constant value across a broad energy range; however, reversing the transport direction strongly suppresses the spin conductance. This significant asymmetry originates from spin-flipped transitions induced by the spin-orbit interaction.

Creating natural and expressive human motion stands as the ultimate goal in computer animation. However, this task remains difficult because of the vast diversity of possible movements, humans' high sensitivity to motion details, and the complexity of accurately modeling them. Consequently, existing generative methods often suffer from either poor quality or limited expressiveness. While diffusion models have demonstrated remarkable generative power in other fields and offer a many-to-many mapping suitable for human motion, they are typically resource-intensive and difficult to control. To address this, we present the Motion Diffusion Model (MDM), a classifier-free diffusion-based generator specifically adapted for human motion. Built on a transformer architecture and incorporating insights from motion generation research, MDM uniquely predicts the sample rather than the noise at each diffusion step. This design choice allows for the integration of established geometric losses on motion locations and velocities, such as foot contact loss. Our model serves as a flexible framework supporting various conditioning modes and generation tasks. We demonstrate that MDM can be trained with lightweight resources while achieving state-of-the-art performance on leading benchmarks for text-to-motion and action-to-motion generation. https://guytevet.github.io/mdm-page/

We examine the interference of two Gaussian states at a beam splitter to investigate the correlations within the resulting bipartite system. We show that nonlocal correlations (entanglement) emerge if and only if the fidelity between the input states drops below a specific threshold determined solely by their purities and the beam splitter's transmissivity. This finding elucidates the necessity of squeezing for entanglement and offers a method to optimize entanglement generation using passive devices.

Understanding individual occupations is crucial for advancing both research and policy. As large-scale administrative records increasingly serve as proxies for labor market activity, there is a growing need for automated job classification methods. We developed such a classifier using a dataset from Bumeran, Mexico's largest job bank (last accessed: 19-01-2022). Our approach employed various machine learning algorithms, including Support Vector Machines, Naive-Bayes, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) deep learning. These models were trained to categorize job offers into one of 23 distinct, non-uniformly distributed classes: Sales, Administration, Call Center, Technology, Trades, Human Resources, Logistics, Marketing, Health, Gastronomy, Financing, Secretary, Production, Engineering, Education, Design, Legal, Construction, Insurance, Communication, Management, Foreign Trade, and Mining. To address class imbalance, we utilized synthetic oversampling techniques such as SMOTE, Geometric-SMOTE, and ADASYN. Ultimately, the proposed convolutional neural network architecture yielded the best performance when paired with the Geometric-SMOTE algorithm.

Bitcoin, a leading cryptocurrency, offers substantial opportunities alongside significant challenges, characterized by high potential returns and risks. Due to its high volatility and the intricate factors influencing it, developing effective price forecasting methods holds considerable practical value for global financial investors and researchers. This paper introduces a novel method, MRC-LSTM, which integrates a Multi-scale Residual Convolutional Neural Network (MRC) with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) to predict Bitcoin closing prices. Specifically, the Multi-scale residual module utilizes one-dimensional convolution to adaptively detect and fuse features across various time scales within multivariate time series. Meanwhile, LSTM excels at capturing long-term dependencies, making it a staple in financial time series forecasting. By combining these techniques, the model achieves highly expressive features and efficiently learns trends and interactions in multivariate data. The study incorporates external factors, including macroeconomic variables and investor attention, alongside Bitcoin market trading data. Experimental results on predicting daily Bitcoin (USD) closing prices demonstrate that MRC-LSTM significantly outperforms other network architectures. Additionally, experiments conducted on Ethereum and Litecoin further validate the model's effectiveness in short-term forecasting for multivariate cryptocurrency time series.

We introduce the inaugural multimodal sarcasm dataset for Spanish, comprising synchronized text, audio, and video clips with sarcasm annotations. This collection spans two major dialects—Latin American and Peninsular Spanish—to ensure broad dialectal representation. We propose several sarcasm detection models to serve as future baselines. Our findings indicate that text-only detection (89%) underperforms compared to text-audio integration (91.9%), with the highest accuracy (93.1%) achieved by combining all three modalities: text, audio, and video.

We investigate the minimization of power-law repulsive-attractive interaction energies, which are prevalent in various physical and biological contexts. Our analysis demonstrates the existence of global minimizers within a discrete framework and establishes bounds for their supports that remain independent of the number of Dirac deltas across specific exponent ranges. These discrete global minimizers represent the stable spatial configurations of flock patterns in swarming models. Furthermore, global minimizers for the continuum problem are derived using compactness arguments, and we support our findings with numerical simulations.

The Feynman integral is widely recognized as a leading approach for constructing generally covariant, nonperturbative interacting quantum field theories (QFTs) that do not rely on a fixed causal background. Recent studies indicate that when the spacetime metric is dynamic and subject to quantization alongside other fields, the Feynman integral in its original Lorentzian signature—without Wick rotation—may be unavoidable, despite known mathematical obstacles that currently prevent a rigorous definition of the integral in this signature. However, the Feynman integral formulation admits a differential equivalent known as the master Dyson-Schwinger (MDS) equation for field correlators. This paper demonstrates that a specific presentation of the MDS equation can be formulated with mathematical rigor by precisely defining the associated function spaces and operators and establishing their properties. Consequently, the MDS equation can replace the Feynman integral as a robust foundation for constructive QFT in arbitrary signatures, independent of a fixed causal structure. Furthermore, the study establishes a canonical method for applying Wilsonian regularization to the MDS equation within this generally covariant framework. The central achievement of the paper is a necessary and sufficient condition ensuring that the solution space of the regularized MDS equation is nonempty for conformally invariant Lagrangians. This theorem also yields a convergent iterative algorithm for generating regularized MDS solutions whenever the solution space exists, which may eventually facilitate the discretization of Lorentzian signature QFTs onto a lattice while maintaining the original metric signature.

Free-breathing cardiac MRI is increasingly viewed as a viable alternative to breath-held cine protocols, making it suitable for pediatric patients and others unable to hold their breath. However, since slices are acquired sequentially, respiratory and cardiac motion patterns vary between them; current methods handle each slice independently. This approach fails to leverage inter-slice redundancies and requires manual intervention or complex post-processing to align reconstructed images for quantification. To address these limitations, we introduce an unsupervised variational deep manifold learning framework for the simultaneous reconstruction and alignment of multislice dynamic MRI. This method jointly optimizes deep network parameters and latent vectors that encode motion-induced dynamics directly from a subject's k-t space data. By minimizing representation non-uniqueness through this variational framework, the approach achieves superior image alignment and reconstruction quality.

We establish a broad preservation theorem that maintains selective independent families throughout countable support iterations. This result offers a unifying framework for various existing findings regarding models where the independence number $\mathfrak{i}$ is strictly less than $\mathfrak{c}$, covering applications such as iterations of Sacks forcing, Miller partition forcing, $h$-perfect tree forcings, and coding with perfect trees. Furthermore, by utilizing this theorem, we demonstrate that $\mathfrak{i} = \aleph_1$ within the Miller Lite model. A central component of this preservation theorem is the concept of "Cohen preservation," which we examine in depth.

We employ a large N-body simulation to examine characteristic scales within density gradient profiles surrounding halos with masses between $10^{12}$ and $10^{15} h^{-1}{\rm M_\odot}$. Our investigation analyzes these profiles separately along the major ($T_1$) and minor ($T_3$) axes of the local tidal tensor, exploring how characteristic scales vary with halo mass, formation time, and environment. We identify two distinct prominent features in the gradient profiles: a deep "valley" and a significant "peak." Utilizing Gaussian Process Regression, we fit the gradient profiles and pinpoint local extrema to define the scales associated with these features. Around the valley, we detect three distinct types of local minima, which correspond to caustics formed by particles orbiting halos. The presence and depth of these three caustics are heavily influenced by the direction of the local tidal field, as well as the halo's formation time and environment. The first caustic, situated at a radius $r > 0.8R_{200}$, aligns with the splashback feature and is dominated by particles at their first apocenter post-infall. The second and third caustics, located near $0.6R_{200}$ and $0.4R_{200}$ respectively, can be reliably identified only in older halos. While the first caustic is consistently the most prominent feature along the $T_3$ axis, it may not be so along $T_1$ or in azimuthally averaged profiles, indicating that caution is necessary when using averaged data to study the splashback radius. We find that the splashback feature is approximately isotropic when distinguishing between the first caustic and the others based on proper separations. Additionally, we identify a peak feature in the density gradient profile at approximately $2.5R_{200}$. This feature is most prominent along the $T_1$ axis and results from mass accumulation from structures outside the halos. We further discuss the origins of these features and their implications for observations.

This research investigates polynomial-time approximation schemes (PTASes) for constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs), including Maximum Independent Set and Minimum Vertex Cover, specifically on sparse graph families. Baker's method yields a PTAS for planar graphs, minor-excluded classes, and similar structures. Regarding maximization finite-valued CSPs (where constraints are arbitrary non-negative functions), Romero, Wrochna, and \v{Z}ivn\'y [SODA'21] demonstrated that the Sherali-Adams LP relaxation provides a straightforward PTAS for all fractionally-treewidth-fragile classes, representing the broadest known "sparsity" condition for such schemes. We generalize these findings to general-valued CSPs, which incorporate "crisp" (or "strict") constraints requiring satisfaction by every valid assignment. The sole requirement for these crisp constraints is that their domain includes an element at least as feasible as any other, though potentially less valuable. For minimization general-valued CSPs featuring crisp constraints, we introduce a PTAS applicable to all Baker graph classes—a definition by Dvo\v{r}\'ak [SODA'20] that covers every class where Baker's technique succeeds, with the possible exception of fractionally-treewidth-fragile classes. Although this result is typical for problems meeting specific monotonicity conditions on crisp constraints, we demonstrate that this can be weakened to diagonalisability, a property of relational structures linked to logics, statistical physics, and random CSPs.

This survey explores and contrasts the recently defined codegree squared extremal function with established concepts such as the Turán function, minimum codegree thresholds, and uniform Turán densities. For a 3-uniform hypergraph $G$, the codegree squared sum, denoted $\textrm{co}_2(G)$, is calculated as the sum of the squares of the codegrees $d(x,y)$ for every pair of vertices $x,y$, effectively representing the square of the $\ell_2$-norm of the codegree vector. Our primary focus is determining the maximum possible value of $\textrm{co}_2(G)$ for an $H$-free 3-uniform hypergraph $G$ on $n$ vertices, a quantity we label the codegree squared extremal function, $\textrm{exco}_2(n,H)$. We systematically investigate these extremal sums for diverse 3-uniform hypergraphs employing a range of methodologies, including both the flag algebra method and classical approaches like the stability method. Specifically, we asymptotically establish the codegree squared extremal numbers for matchings, stars, paths, cycles, and $F_5$ (the 5-vertex hypergraph with edges $\{123,124,345\}$). Furthermore, adhering to a survey structure, we present multiple conjectures and provide a comprehensive overview of Turán densities, minimum codegree thresholds, and codegree squared extremal numbers for prominent hypergraphs.

The network slicing methodology within the 5G Radio Access Network (RAN) is pivotal for advancing next-generation network systems. RAN slicing involves partitioning substrate resources into distinct, self-contained, and programmable slices. Supported by Network Function Virtualization (NFV), each RAN slice comprises multiple Virtual Network Functions (VNFs) and virtual links instantiated on substrate nodes. This study addresses two core objectives: first, establishing the theoretical basis for a VNF mapping plan optimized for RAN slice recovery; and second, developing algorithms for the efficient mapping and embedding of VNFs. Specifically, we introduce four efficient algorithms—the Resource-based Algorithm (RBA), Connectivity-based Algorithm (CBA), Group-based Algorithm (GBA), and Group-Connectivity-based Algorithm (GCBA)—to tackle resource allocation and VNF mapping challenges. Furthermore, extensive experiments were performed to verify the robustness of RAN slicing using the proposed algorithms.

We examine the possibility of stochastic gravitational waves arising from first-order electroweak phase transitions within a framework featuring pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone dark matter and two Higgs doublets. In this model, the dark matter candidate naturally avoids direct detection limits and reaches the observed relic density through thermal production. Three scalar fields acquire vacuum expectation values associated with phase transitions in the early universe. We identify parameter regions capable of driving first-order phase transitions while satisfying current experimental constraints, subsequently analyzing the resulting gravitational wave spectra. Our analysis reveals that specific parameter points generate robust gravitational wave signals, potentially detectable by future space-based interferometers such as LISA, Taiji, and TianQin.

Medical diagnostic robot systems are gaining increasing prominence due to their objectivity and precision. Diagnosing mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is regarded as a vital strategy for preventing Alzheimer's disease (AD). Currently, physicians rely on various clinical examinations to diagnose MCI, a process that is costly and dependent on individual doctor expertise. Consequently, developing a robot-based diagnostic system is essential to mitigate human biases and achieve superior accuracy. This paper introduces a novel Group Feature Domain Adversarial Neural Network (GF-DANN) designed for amnestic MCI (aMCI) diagnosis, incorporating two key modules. First, a Group Feature Extraction (GFE) module utilizes adversarial learning to capture group-level features, thereby minimizing individual variations. Second, a Dual Branch Domain Adaptation (DBDA) module is engineered to reduce distribution discrepancies between source and target domains. Evaluated across three datasets, GF-DANN outperformed both traditional machine learning and deep learning approaches, achieving an accuracy of 89.47% on the DMS dataset, with sensitivity and specificity rates of 90% and 89%, respectively. Furthermore, a comparison of three EEG data collection paradigms indicates that the DMS paradigm holds significant potential for constructing an aMCI diagnostic robot system.

When interactions are present, a simple harmonic oscillator's frequency shifts away from its non-interacting value. These frequency modifications can be calculated perturbatively using various approaches, some of which mirror quantum field theory techniques where parameters evolve or "run" upon introducing interactions. This paper reviews existing methods and introduces novel ones aligned with quantum field theory frameworks. Additionally, we examine systems with multiple oscillators to determine how non-linear terms alter small oscillation frequencies within a linear system, revealing a distinct beat phenomenon in degenerate coupled oscillatory setups.

This study introduces a model reduction technique that maintains structural properties for linear, time-invariant port-Hamiltonian systems. It demonstrates that a low-order system of the same type can be developed to interpolate the original transfer function at a specified set of frequencies.

Conventional paralinguistic analysis for detecting emotions in speech typically relies on either discrete or dimensional (continuous-valued) labels, leading existing models to adopt one of these specific formats. However, psychological theories by researchers such as Russell and Plutchik suggest that these two representations contain shared and complementary information. This paper aims to computationally validate that perspective. We introduce a model designed to simultaneously predict both continuous and discrete emotional attributes, demonstrating how leveraging the relationship between them can enhance the robustness and accuracy of emotion recognition. Our methodology employs multi-task and hierarchical multi-task learning frameworks that explicitly model the interplay between continuous and discrete emotion labels. Experiments conducted on two prominent datasets, IEMOCAP and MSPPodcast, reveal that our unified approach yields statistically significant performance gains over strong baselines using non-unified methods. Furthermore, we show that training on one label type (discrete or continuous) improves performance on tasks requiring the other label type, a concept we term the "mismatched training approach," providing both experimental evidence and reasoning for this strategy.

Achieving high-quality calibration, including flat-fielding and background subtraction, is essential for co-adding and tiling astronomical images in the near-infrared. This paper introduces a comprehensive workflow for creating imaging mosaics using the Magellan Infrared Spectrograph (MMIRS) at the 6.5-meter MMT in Arizona, along with open-source tools developed for MMIRS pipeline data reduction and mosaic preparation. The described process covers pre-observation planning, such as designing dithering patterns and mosaic layouts, as well as post-processing procedures for absolute astrometric and photometric calibration. Additionally, the workflow generates HiPS maps to visualize the final data products within Aladin and Aladin Lite.

MIMO-NOMA cellular networks offer a promising solution for handling massive connectivity. This study investigates the application of low-latency machine learning within the MIMO-NOMA uplink context, where significant data volumes from numerous sources must be transmitted to a nearby edge server for processing. A delay-aware edge learning framework named DACEL is introduced, facilitating collaboration among data sources, the base station, and the edge server. Building upon the delay analysis of DACEL, a NOMA channel allocation algorithm is developed to minimize learning latency. Simulation outcomes demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves superior performance compared to baseline schemes regarding learning delay reduction.

Remaining Useful Life (RUL) refers to the time elapsed from the present moment until equipment failure. Accurate and reliable RUL prognostics equip decision-makers with critical insights necessary to implement effective maintenance strategies, thereby optimizing equipment usage and preventing expensive failures. This study introduces an end-to-end deep learning framework combining multi-layer perceptron (MLP) and long short-term memory (LSTM) layers to forecast RUL. Following data normalization, inputs are first processed by MLP layers for feature extraction, then passed to an LSTM layer to capture temporal patterns, and finally through additional MLP layers to generate RUL predictions. The proposed architecture was evaluated using the NASA Commercial Modular Aero-Propulsion System Simulation (C-MAPSS) dataset. Despite its relative simplicity compared to recent advanced models, the developed system surpasses them by significantly reducing both the competition score and the root mean square error between predicted and actual RUL values. This paper examines how this end-to-end model achieves such superior performance and compares it against other deep learning and state-of-the-art approaches.

The widespread adoption of Twitter has facilitated a rise in fraudulent behaviors, specifically the rapid accumulation of followers to artificially inflate a profile's social standing. Driven by the desire for increased visibility and audience reach, many users have turned to blackmarket services that provide fake followers through collusive networks of compromised and compliant accounts. These services remain challenging to identify because they mimic the behavior of legitimate users. To address this, we introduce DECIFE, a framework designed to detect collusive users engaged in blackmarket "following" services aimed at exchanging artificial followers. Our approach begins by constructing a heterogeneous network that integrates user-tweet-topic relationships along with linguistic attributes and follower dynamics. This network is decomposed into four distinct subgraphs to capture semantic connections between users. We then employ an attention-based subgraph aggregation network to synthesize node representations from these subgraphs. Finally, these combined representations are evaluated using a hypersphere learning objective to identify collusive actors. Extensive experiments on a curated dataset demonstrate the efficacy of DECIFE against other state-of-the-art methods. To our knowledge, this represents the first effort to detect such collusive users involved in blackmarket following services on Twitter.

Building upon the Lyapunov-Schmidt analysis introduced in our recent work (arxiv:2101.12665), we investigate the geometric center of mass associated with the asymptotic foliation of area-constrained Willmore surfaces derived from initial data for the Einstein field equations. When the scalar curvature of the initial data vanishes at infinity, we demonstrate that the geometric center of mass coincides with the Hamiltonian center of mass. Conversely, we find that the location of large area-constrained Willmore surfaces depends on the energy density distribution. Specifically, if the scalar curvature lacks asymptotic symmetry, the geometric center of mass may diverge from the Hamiltonian center of mass.

Rising occurrences of extreme weather and cyberattacks have created a new threat landscape, where malicious actors target stressed critical infrastructure components just before, during, or shortly after such events. This paper introduces the study of Compound Cyber-Physical Threats and proposes a two-stage framework to analyze operational disruptions in electric power grids and their economy-wide consequences under three scenarios: a heatwave, a cyberattack, and a compound event where the cyberattack coincides with the heatwave. The first stage employs a bilevel optimization problem to model the attacker's adversarial strategy at the upper level, while the lower level simulates power network disruptions using an optimal power flow model. The second stage integrates electricity supply disruptions with a Computable General Equilibrium model to assess impacts across all economic sectors. Analysis of the New York Independent System Operator reveals that while a 9% demand increase during a heatwave does not cause unserved load, a cyberattack can result in 4% unserved load on Long Island. However, the compound scenario escalates unserved load on Long Island to 13%, affecting nearly 600,000 customers. Furthermore, state and local government enterprise activities could decline by 30% in the compound scenario. These findings underscore that vulnerabilities in federal, state, and local government entities to power outages can impact a wide demographic.

Repeating fast radio bursts (FRBs) and giant pulses (GPs) from pulsars exhibit certain similarities, prompting an investigation into their potential relationship through the analysis of cumulative energy distributions. This study utilizes observations of repeating FRB 121102 and the GPs of the Crab pulsar. We determine that the power-law slope for GPs with a fluence of at least 130 Jy ms is $2.85\pm0.10$. The energy distribution of FRB 121102 is accurately modeled by a smooth broken power-law function. For bursts exceeding the break energy of $1.22 \times 10^{37}$ erg, the best-fitting slope is $2.90_{-0.44}^{+0.55}$, which aligns closely with the GP index at approximately 1.4 GHz. Furthermore, within the super GPs model framework, we evaluate the physical origin of repeating FRB 121102. We conclude that a model involving a millisecond pulsar is viable and preferred for explaining FRB 121102, even though the magnetar burst model remains more widely accepted.

We introduce (k,k') stabilizing codes, a category of delayless error correction codes tailored for controlling networks subject to erasures. These codes generate k output symbols for every input symbol, ensuring system stability upon receiving any k' of those outputs. Consequently, the design of these erasure codes explicitly incorporates the system requiring stabilization. Our research concentrates on Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) systems, constructing codes through independent encodings and multiple descriptions. We evaluate the theoretical efficiency and performance of these codes, with practical results demonstrated via simulation studies. Notably, these codes offer substantial improvements over other delayless methods, such as repetition codes.

This study employs photometric spot modeling to analyze the nearly four-year light curve of the Kepler target KIC 5955122, interpreting the data as resulting from persistent, dark, circular surface features. Using Bayesian methods, we generated a credible surface map revealing numerous small spots. Following the removal of certain artifacts, the residuals were reduced to $\pm 0.16$\,mmag. The shortest rotational period identified is $P = 16.4 \pm 0.2$ days, with an equator-to-pole differential rotation of $0.25 \pm 0.02$ rad/d. These spots are approximately half as bright as the undisturbed stellar photosphere and are confined to latitudes between $\pm 60^\circ$, with no evidence of near-polar activity. Furthermore, p-mode pulsations allowed us to constrain the star's evolutionary stage, the depth of its convective zone, and its radius and mass. We explore the hypothesis that the distinct active region signature observed in the light curve of this F9IV star stems from a flux-transport dynamo operating at the base of the convection zone. Specifically, we contend that the star transitioned from an active to a quiet state during the Q0–Q16 observation interval and, based on our dynamo model, predict that its characteristic activity cycle duration is comparable to that of the Sun.

Principal loading analysis functions as a dimensionality reduction technique that eliminates variables exerting minimal distortion on the covariance matrix. We enhance this approach by proposing the simultaneous utilization of both correlation and covariance matrices. Additionally, we recommend employing rescaled eigenvectors and present revised algorithms incorporating these modifications.

We examine collections of Lagrangian submanifolds within a specific symplectic manifold, subject to uniform curvature constraints derived from an auxiliary Riemannian metric. We demonstrate that for a broad range of metrics applicable to these collections, convergence to an embedded Lagrangian submanifold necessitates convergence in the Hausdorff metric. This range encompasses established metrics such as the Lagrangian Hofer metric, the spectral norm, and the shadow metrics proposed by Biran, Cornea, and Shelukhin (arXiv:1806.06630). The argument is grounded in a specific formulation of the monotonicity lemma, executed within a deliberately selected metric ball.

In digital pathology, analyzing Whole Slide Images (WSIs) is typically approached as a Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) task. While transformer-based architectures have been applied to WSI classification, they often require adaptations to address the unique challenges of this data type. Despite their success in classical Computer Vision (CV) and Natural Language Processing (NLP), standard reference transformer models from these domains have not been directly applied to pathology slide analysis. This study demonstrates the application of standard, frozen, text-pretrained transformer language models to WSI classification. We introduce SeqShort, a multi-head attention-based sequence reduction layer that summarizes each WSI into a fixed-length sequence of instances. This approach lowers the computational burden of self-attention on long sequences and incorporates positional information absent in other MIL methods. We show that our method is effective for cancer subtype classification without requiring a custom WSI-specific transformer or in-domain self-supervised pretraining, all while maintaining a reduced compute budget and fewer trainable parameters.

This study characterizes the H\"ormander classes $\symbClassOn{m}{\rho}{\delta}{\group,\textnormal{H\"or}}$ on the open manifold $\group = (-1,1)^n$. By equipping this manifold with a group structure, we demonstrate that global Fourier analysis on the group facilitates a definition of a global symbol on the phase space $\group \times \R^n$. Consequently, the pseudo-differential operator class linked to the global H\"ormander classes $\symbClassOn{m}{\rho}{\delta}{\group \times \R^n}$ coincides with the H\"ormander classes $\symbClassOn{m}{\rho}{\delta}{\group,\textnormal{loc}}$ established via local coordinates. Furthermore, the analytical and qualitative attributes of the classes $\symbClassOn{m}{\rho}{\delta}{\group \times \R^n}$ are examined through their global symbols, with specific attention given to $L^p$-Fefferman type estimates, Calder\'on-Vaillancourt theorems, and the spectral characteristics of the associated operators.

Dialogue systems lacking consistent responses fail to be engaging. This study introduces a system capable of maintaining consistency by responding according to a specified character persona. Capitalizing on the growing scale of language models, we propose an approach utilizing prompt-tuning—a method with minimal learning costs—on pre-trained large-scale models. Both automatic and manual evaluations conducted in English and Japanese demonstrate that this technique enables the creation of dialogue systems with more natural and personalized responses, utilizing fewer computational resources than fine-tuning.

The Coronal Multi-channel Polarimeter (CoMP) has created new possibilities for investigating transverse magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) waves in the solar corona. By utilizing the CoMP data archive, researchers have compiled a catalogue of quiescent coronal loops specifically designed for analyzing propagating kink waves. This collection comprises 120 loops observed from 2012 to 2014. Building on this catalogue, a statistical analysis was conducted on kink waves in the quiet solar corona, examining variables such as phase speeds, loop lengths, footpoint power ratios, and equilibrium parameters. These findings reveal a correlation between the damping rate and loop length, indicating that longer loops experience weaker wave damping. We propose that this trend arises from a diminishing average density contrast between the loops and the surrounding plasma as loop length increases. Ultimately, this catalogue serves as a foundational resource for the scientific community to advance the study of propagating kink waves in the quiet solar corona.

We extend Goodman surgery to the realm of projectively Anosov flows by performing the operation along a knot that is both Legendrian and transverse with respect to a supporting bi-contact structure. In the specific case where the flow is Anosov, this method recovers the flows generated by Goodman's original construction. The property of Anosovity for the resulting flow is deeply tied to contact geometry; leveraging this connection, we refine the sequence of surgery coefficients required to produce Anosov flows in specific instances. Furthermore, we interpret bi-contact surgery through the lenses of contact-Legendrian surgery and admissible-inadmissible transverse surgery, deriving new results regarding the tightness of contact and transverse structures. Beyond the context of Anosov flows, we construct novel projectively Anosov flows on hyperbolic 3-manifolds where the invariant foliations have leaves of genus $g > 1$.

Many optimization challenges can be translated into the Ising model, where every detail is represented through spin couplings. Consequently, solving the original mathematical problem becomes equivalent to determining the ground state of the associated spin system, a process typically realized through quantum annealing based on the adiabatic theorem. Certain drawbacks of this method can be mitigated or eliminated by employing a stochastic strategy and interacting with an external environment. We demonstrate that precise engineering of the system-bath interaction at the single-spin level can yield further enhancements to the annealing process.

As subsystem size and energy increase, bipartite entanglement entropies in energy eigenstates transition from groundstate scaling to a volume law. Previous research indicated that under conditions of strong or weak eigenstate thermalization (ETH), the entanglement entropies of all or nearly all eigenstates adhere to a single crossover function. These functions, dictated by the entropy of thermal states, exhibit universal scaling in quantum-critical regimes, a phenomenon supported by field-theoretical arguments and analyses of large non-interacting fermionic and bosonic systems. This study substantiates such scaling behaviors in integrable and non-integrable interacting spin-1/2 chains at criticality through exact diagonalization. Specifically, we examine XXZ and transverse-field Ising models, both with and without next-nearest-neighbor interactions. Our findings confirm that the crossover of thermal subsystem entropies aligns with a universal scaling function derived from conformal field theory. Additionally, we assess the validity of ETH regarding entanglement in these models; even within the relatively small system sizes amenable to simulation, the distributions of eigenstate entanglement entropies remain sharply peaked around the subsystem entropies of the corresponding thermal ensembles.

We derive the lens integral pentagon identity for three-dimensional mirror dual theories by reducing an equality for $\mathcal N=2$ lens supersymmetric partition functions of a specific supersymmetric IR duality, expressing the result in terms of hyperbolic hypergeometric functions.

We introduce a semi-classical framework to analyze transport characteristics in low-dimensional fermionic lattices subjected to external quantum stochastic noise. In these systems, which function as quantum stochastic resistors, bulk particle transport is diffusive and adheres to Ohm's and Fick's laws. This work extends prior exact investigations beyond one-dimensional constraints to ladder geometries, examining various dephasing mechanisms pertinent to diverse physical contexts, ranging from solid-state physics to cold atoms. Our findings reveal a non-trivial relationship between the conductance of these systems and the reservoirs' chemical potential. Subsequently, we propose a semi-classical method that aligns well with exact numerical solutions while offering a more intuitive and streamlined interpretation of transport within quantum stochastic resistors. Furthermore, we observe that the conductance of quantum ladders remains insensitive to the coherence of the dephasing process in the direction transverse to transport, even though the system attains distinct stationary states. Finally, we address the scenario of dissipative leads influenced by dephasing, deriving the specific conditions under which they effectively act as Markovian particle injectors for the system.

Sarcasm relies on ambivalence, characterized by stating something positive while implying negativity, or the reverse. Its core mechanism, which serves as both a sufficient and necessary condition, involves a clash between the literal and implied sentiments within a single utterance. However, detecting this conflict is challenging because the sentiments are often blended or implicit. Consequently, identifying complex and subtle emotional cues poses a significant hurdle for sarcasm detection. To address this, we introduce a Dual-Channel Framework that models literal and implied sentiments independently. Built upon this framework, we developed the Dual-Channel Network (DC-Net) to identify sentiment conflicts. Experimental results on political debate datasets (IAC-V1 and IAC-V2) and Twitter data demonstrate that our DC-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance in sarcasm recognition. Our code has been released to facilitate further research.

The rapid proliferation of webcams and mobile devices has resulted in billions of photos being uploaded online, enabling the collection of vast photo streams for diverse objectives like image clustering, 3D scene reconstruction, and other big data applications. However, these tasks remain difficult because retrieved images often exhibit significant variations in viewpoint, resolution, lighting, noise, and distortion. Moreover, the presence of occluding objects such as people or vehicles further complicates the process of identifying feature correspondences and reconstructing realistic scenes. This paper introduces a structure-based image completion algorithm designed for object removal, generating visually coherent content with consistent structure and texture. By employing an edge matching technique, the method infers the underlying structure of occluded regions. Guided by these estimated structures, texture synthesis is automatically executed along the inferred curves. The proposed approach was evaluated across various image types, ranging from highly structured indoor environments to natural scenes. Experimental results demonstrate satisfactory performance, with the method outperforming existing state-of-the-art techniques. These findings suggest potential utility in downstream big data processing tasks, including image localization, object retrieval, and scene reconstruction.

Usage-based insurance is rapidly becoming the industry standard, making the efficient utilization of drivers' data essential. By applying anomaly detection to vehicle trip summaries, we propose a method that generates both "routine" and "peculiarity" anomaly profiles for each vehicle. This approach employs anomaly detection algorithms to calculate two distinct scores for every trip: a routine score, which measures how atypical a trip is relative to that specific vehicle's own history, and a peculiarity score, which assesses how atypical it is compared to trips across all vehicles. These resulting score vectors form the vehicle's routine and peculiarity profiles. We subsequently extract features from these profiles and evaluate their predictive capability within a claim classification framework. Empirical analysis using real-world data indicates that features derived from the peculiarity profiles significantly enhance classification performance.

Over the years, the architecture of deep convolutional networks (CNNs) has advanced to achieve greater accuracy and speed. Nevertheless, designing network structures that maximize accuracy within limited computational constraints remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces the "Tree block," named for its visual resemblance, which enhances the One-Shot Aggregation (OSA) module by offering a more lightweight and flexible solution. Specifically, the Tree block substitutes each $3\times3$ convolutional layer in OSA with a stack comprising shallow residual blocks (SRBs) and a $1\times1$ convolutional layer. The $1\times1$ layer handles dimension expansion, while the SRB proceeds to the next stage. Consequently, when aggregating an equivalent number of subsequent feature maps, the Tree block achieves a deeper network structure with reduced model complexity. Furthermore, the integration of residual connections and efficient channel attention (ECA) into the Tree block further boosts network performance. Utilizing this block, we developed efficient backbone models termed TreeNets. With an architecture similar to ResNet, TreeNets offer the flexibility to replace ResNet across various computer vision frameworks. Comprehensive evaluations on standard benchmarks, including ImageNet-1k for classification, MS COCO for object detection, and instance segmentation, demonstrate that TreeNets are more efficient and perform competitively against current state-of-the-art backbone methods.

We developed an artificial system comprising attention-based neural network agents that selectively exchange messages to investigate the emergence of memetic evolution and its interaction with the genetic evolution of network weights. Our observations indicate that the capacity of agents to exert selection pressures on one another is crucial for memetic evolution to bootstrap itself, achieving both high-fidelity meme replication and the continuous generation of new memes. However, within this system, there is minimal interaction between this memetic "ecology" and the underlying tasks that drive individual fitness; the emergent meme layer appears to be neither beneficial nor detrimental to the agents' ability to learn and solve tasks. The source code for these experiments can be found at https://github.com/GoodAI/memes.

The Shortcut to Adiabatic Passage (STAP), originally introduced to expedite adiabatic quantum state transfer, has seen extensive application in both quantum and integrated optics. This study extends STAP to acoustics to engineer compact couplers and functional metamaterials. By utilizing dressed states within a three-level system, we tailor the spatially varying coupling strengths of acoustic waveguides (WGs), enabling efficient acoustic energy transfer among three WGs over a short distance. We demonstrate that introducing loss into the intermediate WG imparts a one-way characteristic to the acoustic coupler. Uniquely, by designing acoustic wave propagation to emulate a Hadamard transformation, we construct an acoustic metamaterial from an array of these couplers, which exhibits beam-splitting capabilities alongside unidirectional and broadband performance. This work bridges STAP with acoustic couplers and metamaterials, potentially significantly advancing the development of quantum technologies for sophisticated acoustic devices.

For any $\varepsilon > 0$, we present a straightforward, deterministic algorithm achieving a $(6+\varepsilon)$-approximation for the Nash social welfare (NSW) problem under submodular valuations, improving upon the prior best randomized bound of $380$. We also address the asymmetric variant, which seeks to maximize the weighted geometric mean of agents' valuations, providing an $(\omega + 2 +\varepsilon) e$-approximation when the ratio of the maximum weight to the average weight does not exceed $\omega$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that a $1/2$-EFX envy-freeness property can be achieved concurrently with a constant-factor approximation; specifically, a polynomial-time algorithm exists that yields an allocation which is both $1/2$-EFX and a $(12+\varepsilon)$-approximation for the symmetric NSW problem under submodular valuations, surpassing the previous linear-in-agents bound under $1/2$-EFX.

This paper introduces a multi-speaker Japanese text-to-speech (TTS) system for audiobooks that enhances synthetic speech prosody by utilizing multimodal context, specifically combining preceding acoustic data with bilateral textual information. Unlike prior approaches that rely on unilateral or single-modality contexts, our method employs dedicated acoustic and textual encoders to aggregate this information, enabling the TTS model to predict context-dependent prosody more effectively. Comprehensive objective and subjective evaluations on a multi-speaker Japanese audiobook dataset demonstrate that the proposed system significantly outperforms two existing methods. Furthermore, we provide novel insights regarding context modality choices, lateral information, and length configurations for audiobook TTS, addressing areas previously unexplored in the literature.

Automatic phenotyping involves identifying patient cohorts that meet specific criteria, a process that typically requires classifying lengthy clinical documents containing thousands of tokens. However, recent state-of-the-art transformer-based pre-trained language models restrict input lengths to a few hundred tokens (for instance, 512 tokens for BERT). We assessed multiple strategies for integrating pre-trained sentence encoders into document-level representations of clinical text and discovered that hierarchical transformers without pre-training perform competitively against models pre-trained for the specific task.

Let $G$ be a finite group, and let $\varphi(G)$ denote the count of elements $a \in G$ whose order $o(a)$ equals the group's exponent $\exp(G)$. Under a natural assumption, this note identifies all groups $G$ satisfying the condition that for any subgroups $H$ and $K$ of $G$, if $H \subseteq K$, then $\varphi(H)$ divides $\varphi(K)$. This result provides a partial solution to Problem 5.4 in \cite{6}.

We examine a real Klein-Gordon field within the Poincaré patch of $(d+1)$-dimensional anti-de Sitter spacetime, PAdS$_{d+1}$, subject to dynamical boundary conditions at the asymptotic boundary that explicitly involve the field's second time derivative. These conditions belong to the generalized Wentzell class. We derive the Wightman two-point function for the ground state of the Klein-Gordon theory whenever the theory's parameters—specifically the field mass, curvature coupling, and boundary condition coefficients—permit such a ground state. In scenarios where the field mass and curvature coupling result in an effectively massless theory, we define a boundary field governed by the dynamical boundary conditions. For these cases, we construct not only the Wightman function for the bulk field but also boundary-to-boundary, boundary-to-bulk, and bulk-to-boundary propagators.

We present a novel micro-macro Markov chain Monte Carlo approach (mM-MCMC) featuring indirect reconstruction for sampling invariant distributions in molecular dynamics systems characterized by a separation of time scales between fast microscopic processes and slow macroscopic dynamics along specific low-dimensional reaction coordinates. Designed to improve state space exploration in metastable environments, the algorithm permits larger proposal steps at the macroscopic level, subject to a conditional accept-reject mechanism. A full microscopic state is reconstructed only upon macroscopic acceptance and undergoes a subsequent accept/reject check. The computational advantage arises because most macroscopic proposals are rejected cheaply, whereas reconstructed microscopic states are nearly always accepted. This work details an indirect technique for recovering microscopic samples from macroscopic reaction coordinate values, useful even when direct reconstruction is difficult. This method generates microscopic samples by running a biased simulation from the prior state, steering it toward the proposed reaction coordinate. Numerical results demonstrate that incorporating indirect reconstruction significantly broadens the applicability of the mM-MCMC framework.

Using multi-band Hubble Space Telescope (HST) imaging, we have characterized the optical counterparts of the compact X-ray source population in the nearby spiral galaxy M81. By comparing the optical luminosities and colors of candidate donor stars and host clusters against stellar and cluster evolutionary models, we derived probable masses and upper age limits for both field and cluster X-ray binaries. Our analysis identified 15 low-mass X-ray binaries (donor mass $\leq$ 3 $M_{\odot}$) residing in ancient globular clusters, along with 42 candidate high-mass X-ray binaries (donor mass $\geq$ 8 $M_{\odot}$). To assess the reliability of our classifications, we injected 4,000 artificial sources into the HST mosaic, confirming that our identification of globular clusters and high-mass X-ray binaries is accurate at a level exceeding 90%. We observed that globular clusters hosting X-ray binaries are, on average, more massive and compact than those without. However, no clear correlation exists between cluster X-ray brightness and their mass or density, nor are the hosts of X-ray binaries significantly more luminous than the general field population of low-mass X-ray binaries. This study constitutes one of the first comprehensive analyses of the X-ray binary population within globular clusters in a spiral galaxy.

Although originally designed for natural language processing, vision transformers have recently gained considerable attention in audio and computer vision fields for their ability to model long-range dependencies. However, the data-intensive nature of transformers and the scarcity of labeled audio data have led researchers to fine-tune audio models from ImageNet-pretrained weights, despite the substantial domain mismatch between natural images and audio. To address this, research has shifted toward self-supervised pretraining for audio transformers, aiming to minimize reliance on large labeled datasets while learning concise representations of audio spectrograms. This paper introduces ASiT, a novel self-supervised transformer designed for general audio representation that captures both local and global contextual information through group masked modeling and self-distillation. We evaluate our pretrained models on various audio and speech classification tasks, including audio event detection, keyword spotting, and speaker identification. Furthermore, we perform extensive ablation studies assessing different pretraining strategies. The ASiT framework significantly enhances performance across all evaluated tasks and establishes new state-of-the-art results on five audio and speech classification benchmarks, surpassing recent methods, even those utilizing additional pretraining datasets. The code and pretrained weights will be released publicly for the scientific community.

To examine how processing variables influence microstructure, two ingots with a nominal composition of Fe-8Mn-4Al-2Si-0.5C-0.07V-0.05Sn were fabricated, weighing 400 g and 5 kg respectively. The larger 5 kg ingot simulated cooling rates typical of commercial production to identify scaling challenges related to casting segregation, whereas the smaller 400 g ingot experienced a high cooling rate and exhibited a distinct segregation pattern. Both ingots underwent homogenization at 1250 °C for varying durations to assess chemical uniformity and the dissolution of δ-ferrite. Within two hours, the Mn segregation range (maximum minus minimum) narrowed from 8.0 to 1.7 wt% in the 400 g ingot and from 6.2 to 1.5 wt% in the 5 kg ingot. Although some δ-ferrite persisted after two hours in both samples, the 5 kg ingot retained nearly three times as much as the smaller one. Microstructure modeling demonstrated strong agreement between predicted and observed segregation levels and distributions. Following thermomechanical processing, the coarse untransformed δ-ferrite in the 5 kg ingot evolved into coarse δ-ferrite stringers in the final product, causing a marginal reduction in yield strength. However, rolled strips derived from both ingots achieved yield strengths exceeding 900 MPa, tensile strengths over 1100 MPa, and elongation greater than 40%. These properties showed less than a 10% deviation in strength and no change in ductility compared to a fully homogenized reference sample.

Many natural optimization challenges are NP-hard, suggesting that finding exact solutions is likely difficult in the worst-case scenario. However, obtaining reasonably good solutions for most practical instances is often sufficient. This paper introduces a novel algorithm that computes approximate solutions for the Maximum Exact 3-Satisfiability (MAX-E-3-SAT) problem in ${\Theta(N})$ time by leveraging deep learning. This approach enables a learning algorithm to determine Boolean variables based on local information derived from the Survey Propagation algorithm. Through rigorous analysis of random CNF instances involving various numbers of Boolean variables, we demonstrate that this new method, which does not rely on any decimation strategy, generates assignments superior to random ones, even when message convergence is not achieved. Although this algorithm does not match the performance of state-of-the-art Maximum Satisfiability (MAX-SAT) solvers, it is capable of solving substantially larger and more complex problems than those encountered during its training phase.

Ensuring the privacy and security of big data within cloud computing environments, without compromising processing efficiency, remains an area ripe for advancement. A primary application highlighting these challenges is genome analysis. This study introduces a secure multi-label tumor classification approach leveraging homomorphic encryption, which employs two distinct machine learning algorithms—SVM and XGBoost—to categorize encrypted genomic data across various tumor types.

We demonstrate that the photospheres of "failed" Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs), characterized by bulk Lorentz factors significantly below 100, can exist outside the region of internal shocks. The radiation emitted by these photospheres is thermal and intense in the UV/Soft X-ray spectrum, persisting for approximately 1,000 seconds with a luminosity several times 10^46 erg/s. Such events are detectable by both existing and upcoming satellite missions. Furthermore, we show that the afterglows of failed GRBs exhibit unique characteristics during their early phase, enabling the differentiation of failed GRBs from ordinary GRBs and beaming-induced orphan afterglows.

Recent compilations of X-ray and UV flux measurements for quasars (QSOs) include objects that cannot be standardized using the $L_X-L_{UV}$ relation, rendering them unsuitable for constraining cosmological parameters. This study demonstrates that the largest sub-sample within these compilations—the SDSS-4XMM QSOs, which account for approximately two-thirds of the total—exhibits $L_X-L_{UV}$ relations that vary depending on the assumed cosmological model and redshift. This dependency is the primary reason for the standardization issues previously identified in the full dataset. The second and third largest sub-samples, SDSS-Chandra and XXL QSOs respectively, collectively comprise about 30% of the total and appear to be standardizable; however, they offer only weak constraints on cosmological parameters that remain consistent with the standard spatially-flat $\Lambda$CDM model and other well-established cosmological probes.
In this paper, we establish a tight upper bound for exceptional real zeros.

MIMO technology's enhanced throughput depends on the base station's access to channel state information (CSI). To keep CSI feedback overhead manageable for advancing MIMO systems, such as massive and ultra-massive variants, deep learning (DL) is employed for CSI compression. While current systems utilize DL-based CSI compression as source coding under the separation principle, this separate source-channel coding (SSCC) approach underperforms compared to joint source-channel coding (JSCC) in finite blocklength scenarios. This paper introduces a deep joint source-channel coding (DJSCC) framework for CSI feedback. Specifically, the proposed method concurrently learns from both the CSI source and the wireless channel. Rather than truncating CSI in the delay domain using Fourier transforms as existing techniques do, we utilize non-linear transform networks for compression. Additionally, an SNR adaptation mechanism is implemented to handle wireless channel fluctuations. Extensive experiments confirm the validity, adaptability, and generality of the proposed framework.

This study presents findings on the eta prime meson and topological susceptibility within two-flavor lattice QCD. Utilizing Wilson twisted mass fermions at maximal twist, we analyzed pion masses spanning from 340 MeV to the physical point. Furthermore, we compare these results with existing literature to evaluate discretization effects.

Point cloud registration represents a core challenge in 3D computer vision, particularly when dealing with the large-scale and complexly distributed nature of outdoor LiDAR data. To address this, we introduce HRegNet, an efficient hierarchical network designed for registering large-scale outdoor LiDAR point clouds. Rather than processing every point, HRegNet performs registration on hierarchically extracted keypoints and descriptors. By integrating reliable features from deeper layers with precise positional information from shallower layers, the framework achieves both robustness and accuracy. We also propose a correspondence network capable of generating accurate keypoint matches. This approach incorporates bilateral and neighborhood consensus for matching, alongside novel similarity features designed to enhance the correspondence network, significantly boosting registration performance. Additionally, the method maintains high efficiency by utilizing only a sparse set of keypoints. Extensive experiments on two large-scale outdoor LiDAR datasets validate the high accuracy and efficiency of HRegNet. The project website is available at https://ispc-group.github.io/hregnet.

Using the celestial CFT framework, we investigate exponentiated soft exchange within gauge and gravitational theories in $d+2$ dimensions. These models feature spontaneously broken asymptotic symmetries arising from gauge transformations with non-compact support, suggesting that the effective dynamics of the resulting Goldstone "edge" mode should be $d$-dimensional. However, the explicit inclusion of an infrared regulator breaks these symmetries, rendering the edge mode in the regulated theory a $d$-dimensional pseudo-Goldstone boson. Symmetry arguments dictate the leading terms of the effective action, with their coefficients governed by the infrared cutoff. Our computations reproduce abelian infrared divergences for $d=2$ and capture re-summed, infrared-finite soft exchange in higher dimensions, while also recovering leading soft theorems across all dimensions for both gauge and gravitational theories. Notably, we observe that the shadow transform of the Goldstone mode possesses local $d$-dimensional dynamics, whereas the effective action formulated directly in terms of the Goldstone mode is non-local for $d>2$. Furthermore, we introduce and analyze novel magnetic soft theorems. Our findings indicate that symmetry principles alone are sufficient to compute soft exchange in gauge theory and gravity.
This paper primarily aims to explore Paley type and Hardy-Littlewood type inequalities, as well as the strong convergence theorem for partial sums of Vilenkin-Fourier series.

Misiurewicz originally demonstrated that for the exponential family $E_{\kappa}:z\mapsto\kappa e^z$ with $\kappa>0$, the Julia set comprises the entire complex plane when $\kappa>1/e$. Subsequently, Devaney and Krych established that in the range $0<\kappa\leq1/e$, the Julia set consists of an uncountable collection of disjoint simple curves extending to infinity. Bergweiler later extended these findings to a three-dimensional analogue of the exponential map known as the Zorich map. In this work, we prove that for specific symmetric Zorich maps, the Julia set fills all of $\mathbb{R}^3$, thereby generalizing Misiurewicz's conclusion. Furthermore, we demonstrate that periodic points are dense throughout $\mathbb{R}^3$ and that the escaping set remains connected, which extends a result by Rempe. Finally, we also generalize a theorem concerning the measurable dynamics of the exponential function attributed to Ghys, Sullivan, and Goldberg.

Measurement-device-independent (MDI) quantum key distribution (QKD) enables two trusted entities to generate a shared secret key remotely without relying on the integrity of a central detection node; however, this security relies heavily on well-characterized quantum sources, as vulnerabilities at the source represent the protocol's primary security loophole. This study identifies a time-dependent side-channel in a standard polarization-based QKD source that utilizes a Faraday mirror for phase stabilization. By employing the recently established numerical proof methodology from [Phys. Rev. A 99, 062332 (2019)], we quantify how the secret key rate's sensitivity depends on the quantum optical model of this side-channel and propose strategies to reduce information leakage. Specifically, we observe that while the MDI three-state and BB84 protocols produce identical key rates under ideal conditions, their performance diverges when side-channels are present, with BB84 demonstrating superior advantages. Although our analysis focuses on a representative scenario, we anticipate that the developed mitigation strategies and key rate analysis framework will be broadly applicable to other sources with similar leakage issues.

It is widely accepted that pretrained language models can capture syntactic structures [Tenney et al., 2019; Jawahar et al., 2019; Hewitt and Manning, 2019]. This paper introduces UPOA, an unsupervised constituent parsing model that derives an Outside Association score exclusively from the self-attention weight matrix of a pretrained language model to serve as a syntactic distance metric for span segmentation. We also present an improved variant, UPIO, which leverages both inside and outside association scores to estimate span likelihood. Experiments reveal that the linear projection matrices for queries and keys within the self-attention mechanism are crucial for parsing; consequently, we adapt the unsupervised models into few-shot versions (FPOA and FPIO) that utilize a small number of annotated trees to refine these projection matrices. Results on the Penn Treebank indicate that UPIO achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods on short sentences (length ≤ 10). Furthermore, FPIO, trained with merely 20 annotated trees, surpasses a prior few-shot approach trained on 50 trees. Finally, cross-lingual experiments demonstrate that both our unsupervised and few-shot methods outperform previous techniques across most languages in the SPMRL benchmark [Seddah et al., 2013].

Since the X-FEM approximation avoids the need for meshing cracks, it has attracted significant interest from an industrial perspective. This thesis report outlines key concepts of the Nitsche approach for handling boundary conditions at embedded interfaces within XFEM. The study examines scenarios where either the jump of a field or the primary field itself is specified across the interface. The work begins by deriving the fundamentals of the Nitsche method, followed by its discretization using X-FEM with shifted basis enrichment. Finally, the method is implemented on the open-source Code-Aster platform.

HS Hydrae is a short-period eclipsing binary system ($P_{\text{orb}}=1.57$ days) within a rare class of binaries exhibiting rapidly varying inclinations. This dynamical evolution, driven by a third star on an intermediate orbit, causes substantial annual variations in eclipse depths and timings. Zasche & Paschke (2012) identified that the system's eclipses were fading quickly, forecasting their disappearance by 2022. Analysis of 25 days of TESS photometry from Sector 009 reveals that primary eclipses in March 2019 had a depth of only $0.00173 \pm 0.00007$ mag, suggesting these may be the final detected eclipses. Additionally, we queried the DASCH archive for historical records, creating a unique dataset spanning over 125 years—from photographic plates to precise space-based observations—that traces the emergence and decay of the eclipses to better constrain the system's evolution. Recent TESS observations from Sector 035 confirm that eclipses have ceased for HS Hya, with our estimates indicating they will resume around 2195.

This study examines the restoration of axial $U(1)$ symmetry at finite temperatures within two-flavor QCD, utilizing the Möbius domain-wall formalism to ensure robust chiral symmetry. We present measurements of the difference in meson susceptibilities, which serve as indicators of $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking; these signals are primarily driven by zero and near-zero modes. Furthermore, by reweighting the measure to match overlap fermions, we demonstrate that $U(1)_A$ breaking effects are suppressed above the chiral transition temperature.

We examine the field theory describing a perfect, incompressible two-dimensional fluid. A key characteristic of this system is that the quadratic action for fluctuations around the ground state lacks both mass and gradient terms. Quantum mechanically, this creates a technical challenge, indicating that the fluctuation Hilbert space is not a Fock space and rendering perturbation theory ineffective. We demonstrate that the correct approach requires recognizing the configuration space as the area-preserving Lie group $S\mathrm{Diff}$. While quantum mechanics on Lie groups is fundamentally a group theory problem, our specific case is more complex because $S\mathrm{Diff}$ is infinite-dimensional. By focusing on a fluid defined on the 2-torus $T^2$, we utilize the established result $S\mathrm{Diff}(T^2)\sim SU(N)$ as $N\to \infty$, which reduces the problem to a manageable finite $N$ case. $SU(N)$ provides ultraviolet regularization, yet physical quantities remain well-defined in the continuum limit where $N\to \infty$. Our primary finding is the existence of ungapped, localized excitations known as vortons, which exhibit a dispersion relation $\omega \propto k^2$ and carry a vorticity dipole. These vortons are further distinguished by unique derivative interactions, with their structure dictated by symmetry. Moving beyond the original incompressible fluid model, we developed a class of field theories in which vortons emerge directly as the quanta of either bosonic or fermionic local fields.

This paper introduces a high-order numerical scheme designed for linear Fokker-Planck equations featuring a constant diffusion term. By integrating Lagrange-Galerkin and semi-Lagrangian methods, the proposed approach is explicit, conservative, and consistent, demonstrating stability even with large time steps relative to spatial steps. We present a convergence analysis for the scheme based on exact Lagrange-Galerkin integration and also introduce a practical variant utilizing inexact integration. The primary application of this work is developing a high-order method to approximate solutions for time-dependent mean field game systems.

The existence of multiple magnetic skyrmion phases introduces an extra degree of freedom for skyrmion-based ultrahigh-density spin memory. Extending this concept to two-dimensional van der Waals magnets presents a promising challenge, where tunable parameters such as thickness, twisting angle, and electrical gating, combined with high skyrmion density, yield novel properties and improved functionality. We demonstrate a van der Waals interface created by stacking two 2D ferromagnets, Cr2Ge2Te6 and Fe3GeTe2, which possess Curie temperatures of approximately 65 K and 205 K, respectively. This heterostructure hosts two distinct groups of magnetic skyrmions. Below 60 K, while Cr2Ge2Te6 remains magnetically ordered, two sets of topological Hall effects are detected. Magnetic force microscopy directly visualizes these two skyrmion groups. Notably, these skyrmions remain stable in the remanent state without any applied magnetic field. Our findings offer significant potential for developing skyrmionic devices utilizing van der Waals heterostructures capable of supporting multiple skyrmion phases.

This paper examines the performance of a dual-hop mixed radio-frequency underwater wireless optical communication (RF-UWOC) system assisted by a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). As an emerging, low-cost technology, RIS is utilized to boost received signal strength and thereby enhance overall system performance. In the proposed setup, a ground source lacking a reliable direct link to a marine buoy communicates via an RIS mounted on a building; the buoy then functions as a relay to transmit the signal to an underwater destination. We derive analytical expressions for outage probability (OP), average bit error rate (ABER), and average channel capacity (ACC) under fixed-gain amplify-and-forward (AF) and decode-and-forward (DF) relaying protocols at the buoy. Furthermore, asymptotic analyses of OP and ABER are conducted to provide deeper insights into the analytical framework, specifically deriving the system diversity order, which depends on RF link parameters and UWOC detection schemes. Finally, the study demonstrates that RIS-assisted configurations can significantly improve the performance of mixed dual-hop RF-UWOC systems.

This paper examines binary response models for heterogeneous panel data featuring interactive fixed effects, accommodating scenarios where both the cross-sectional and temporal dimensions expand. Practically, the proposed framework supports applications such as predicting corporate bankruptcy and performing credit rating assessments. Theoretically and methodologically, we bridge maximum likelihood estimation with least squares methods, introduce a straightforward information criterion for determining the number of factors, and derive the corresponding asymptotic distributions. Furthermore, extensive simulations are performed to validate these theoretical results. In the empirical section, we analyze the sign prediction of stock returns and subsequently utilize these forecast results for portfolio analysis.

Autonomous Unmanned Aerial Manipulators (UAMs) hold significant promise for evolving passive sensing tasks into active, three-dimensional interactive operations, yet their widespread adoption is hindered by challenges such as target detection and stabilization. This paper introduces a vision-driven autonomous UAM equipped with a 3-degree-of-freedom robotic arm designed for rotational grasping, incorporating a center-of-gravity displacement compensation mechanism. Initially, the study details the hardware, software architecture, and state estimation techniques, releasing all mechanical designs as open-source resources for community reuse. Subsequently, the analysis of rotor-induced airflow is used to plan the robotic arm's trajectory. A novel detection method named Rotation-SqueezeDet is then proposed to facilitate rotation-aware grasping, delivering target position and orientation data in near real-time on a Jetson TX2 platform. Finally, multiple experimental trials validate the proposed framework, demonstrating its suitability for autonomous aerial grasping in GPS-denied environments.

Fifth-generation (5G) network slicing holds the promise of accommodating the varied service needs of diverse vertical sectors. Among these, the smart distribution grid represents a typical industry that introduces fresh challenges for communication infrastructure. This study examines network slicing behavior within 5G radio access networks serving smart grid applications characterized by heterogeneous traffic. To support slicing in this environment, we utilize distinct 5G radio access numerologies tailored to two traffic classes with differing radio resource and quality-of-service demands. We develop three multi-dimensional Markov models to evaluate the transient performance of resource allocation under both prioritized and non-prioritized traffic scenarios. Through analytical and simulation results, we explore the impact of smart grid protection and control traffic on concurrent traffic sessions and overall radio resource utilization.

This study examines differential operators constructed as Friedrichs extensions of quadratic forms featuring non-smooth coefficients. We establish a two-term optimal asymptotic formula for the Riesz means of these operators, which simultaneously provides a new proof of an optimal Weyl law under specific regularity assumptions. Furthermore, we extend these techniques to analyze more general admissible operators perturbed by a rough differential operator, deriving optimal spectral asymptotics under analogous conditions. Specifically, the validity of the Weyl law requires coefficients to be differentiable with Hölder continuous derivatives, whereas the optimal results for the Riesz means necessitate coefficients that are twice differentiable with Hölder continuous derivatives.

Policy gradient (PG) approaches are widely adopted and effective in large-scale reinforcement learning because of their incremental design and inherent stability. Following the empirical achievements of these methods, researchers have recently begun establishing a theoretical basis for them. This study extends that theoretical work by examining the global convergence of stochastic PG methods enhanced with momentum terms, a technique proven to boost PG performance. We analyze both soft-max and Fisher-non-degenerate policy parametrizations, demonstrating that incorporating momentum reduces the global optimality sample complexity of standard PG methods to $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\epsilon^{-1.5})$ and $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\epsilon^{-1})$ respectively, where $\epsilon > 0$ denotes the desired tolerance. To our knowledge, this is the first work to derive global convergence guarantees for momentum-based PG methods. Furthermore, for generic Fisher-non-degenerate parametrizations, we present the first single-loop, finite-batch PG algorithm to achieve a global optimality sample complexity of $\tilde{O}(\epsilon^{-3})$. Additionally, our approach offers a versatile framework for analyzing the global convergence rates of stochastic PG methods, which can be readily adapted to various PG estimators.

Following the launch of Bitcoin, cryptocurrencies have garnered significant research interest, a trend accompanied by a growing demand for smart contracts to facilitate these transactions. Essentially, smart contracts are digitally enforced agreements where multiple parties collaborate to achieve a shared objective. A critical limitation in existing smart contract systems is the lack of privacy, as participants' inputs are exposed to both the blockchain network and other involved parties. Our work extends the capabilities of the Hawk project, which offers transaction privacy and smart contract support, by addressing its reliance on a trusted manager who must be assumed not to disclose user inputs. Instead, this paper introduces a practical private smart contract protocol that substitutes the manager with a Multi-Party Computation (MPC) framework. This approach ensures the executed function remains lightweight with minimal overhead and leverages practical sigma protocols and homomorphic commitments to demonstrate to the blockchain that the total incoming balances equal the total outgoing balances.

Object motion and appearance are standard inputs for multiple object tracking (MOT), utilized either for associating detections in tracking-by-detection frameworks or for direct track prediction in joint-detection-and-tracking approaches. Nevertheless, these two data types are frequently treated in isolation and fail to directly optimize the use of visual information from the current frame. This paper introduces PatchTrack, a Transformer-based joint-detection-and-tracking system that predicts tracks using patches from the current frame. We employ a Kalman filter to forecast the locations of existing tracks from the previous frame, then feed patches cropped from these predicted bounding boxes into the Transformer decoder to infer new tracks. By leveraging object motion and appearance information encoded within these patches, the method focuses attention on regions where new tracks are most likely to appear. We demonstrate PatchTrack's effectiveness on recent MOT benchmarks, achieving a MOTA of 73.71% and IDF1 of 65.77% on MOT16, and a MOTA of 73.59% and IDF1 of 65.23% on MOT17. Results are available at https://motchallenge.net/method/MOT=4725&chl=10.

The Stefan problem describes liquid-solid phase transitions as the temporal evolution of temperature distributions and moving boundaries within such materials. This study introduces an observer-based event-triggered boundary control method for the one-phase Stefan problem, relying on measurements of the moving interface's position and velocity. The infinite-dimensional backstepping technique is employed to construct both the controller and the observer. A dynamic event-triggering condition is developed to implement the continuous-time observer-based controller, dictating when the control input must be refreshed.
