Although the majority operate in impractical white-box environments, a novel category of query-based hard-label (QBHL) black-box attacks presents a serious threat to real-world services, such as those provided by Google Cloud and Tencent API. Currently, no generalizable and practical defense exists for these attacks. This paper introduces PredCoin, a robust and adaptable solution designed to counter QBHL threats. PredCoin targets the gradient estimation step, a critical element in most QBHL attacks, by detecting queries manipulated by adversaries and injecting uncertainty into the output. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that PredCoin effectively defends against four leading QBHL attacks across diverse settings and tasks without compromising the target model's overall accuracy. Furthermore, PredCoin remains robust and effective even against defense-aware attacks that possess full knowledge of its internal mechanisms.

This study examines methods for transforming OpenStreetMap data into road networks suitable for subsequent applications. Among the various formats available, Extensible Markup Language (XML) is a key example. OpenStreetMap data comprises nodes, ways, and relations. Our approach involves processing OSM XML files to extract node and way information, thereby generating a street map of the Memphis region. This resulting map can be utilized in various downstream applications.

Standard deep neural network training typically updates every parameter during each iteration. Recent studies indicate that updating only a small subset of parameters can reduce storage and communication demands. In this paper, we demonstrate how to apply a fixed sparse mask to select a specific subset of parameters for updates across multiple iterations. We generate this mask by choosing the $k$ parameters with the highest Fisher information as a straightforward proxy for task importance. Through experiments on parameter-efficient transfer learning and distributed training, we show that our method matches or surpasses other sparse update techniques in performance while offering superior efficiency in memory and communication. We have made our code publicly available to encourage further exploration of this approach.

This paper introduces a new application of the coupled complex boundary method, originally developed by Cheng et al. (2014) for inverse source problems, to address the exterior Bernoulli problem—a classic stationary free boundary problem—within a shape optimization framework. The approach converts the overdetermined problem into a complex boundary value problem featuring a complex Robin condition that links the Dirichlet and Neumann conditions on the free boundary. By constructing a cost function based on the imaginary part of the solution across the entire domain, we identify the free boundary. We establish the existence of the shape derivative for the complex state with respect to the domain, compute the shape gradient of the cost functional, and characterize the shape Hessian at the optimal domain under both strong and mild regularity assumptions. Furthermore, we demonstrate the method's instability by proving the compactness of the relevant expression. An iterative algorithm utilizing a Sobolev gradient scheme via the finite element method is developed to solve the minimization problem. Finally, the method's effectiveness is validated through numerical examples in both two and three spatial dimensions.

Conditional variational autoencoders (CVAEs) represent flexible deep generative models that enhance the conventional VAE architecture by incorporating auxiliary covariates to condition generation. While the foundational CVAE assumes data independence, newer iterations like those utilizing Gaussian process (GP) priors are capable of modeling intricate correlations across the entire dataset. Although techniques exist for training standard VAEs on partially observed data, they remain inadequate for conditional variants. This study introduces a novel approach to train CVAEs even when auxiliary covariates contain missing entries. By integrating a prior distribution for these missing values and estimating their posterior via amortized variational inference, the method effectively handles data gaps. During training, the approach marginalizes uncertainty regarding the missing covariates while optimizing the evidence lower bound. We also establish computationally efficient strategies for learning both CVAEs and GP prior VAEs that support mini-batching. Empirical evaluations on both simulated data and a clinical trial demonstrate that our method surpasses existing approaches in learning conditional VAEs from non-temporal, temporal, and longitudinal datasets.

Category-level object pose estimation seeks to determine the 6D poses of unseen object instances from known categories without relying on object CAD models. To address the substantial annotation requirements typical of category-level learning, we introduce, for the first time, a self-supervised framework capable of estimating category-level 6D object poses from single 3D point clouds. Our approach requires no ground-truth pose labels, CAD models, or multi-view supervision during training. The core of our method involves disentangling shape and pose via an invariant shape reconstruction module and an equivariant pose estimation module, both powered by SE(3) equivariant point cloud networks. The invariant shape reconstruction module learns to generate aligned reconstructions, producing a category-level reference frame without any annotations. Meanwhile, the equivariant pose estimation module achieves accuracy comparable to fully supervised methods. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of our approach on both complete and partial depth point clouds from the ModelNet40 benchmark and on real-world depth point clouds from the NOCS-REAL 275 dataset. Project details, including code and visualizations, are available at: https://dragonlong.github.io/equi-pose.

Training object detectors via supervised learning depends on large-scale, well-annotated datasets, which are expensive to create. Consequently, researchers have explored cost-effective alternatives like cloud sourcing; however, datasets generated through these approaches often suffer from noisy annotations, including inaccurate bounding boxes and erroneous class labels. This study introduces a novel framework for training object detectors on datasets characterized by entangled noise in both class labels and bounding boxes. Our proposed approach efficiently disentangles this combined noise, rectifies the annotations, and then proceeds to train the detector using the corrected data. We validated the method's efficacy and compared it against a baseline across datasets with varying noise levels. The experimental results demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms the baseline.

The author created a uniform model applicable across various spaces, treating distance and angle measurement types as adjustable parameters. Although rooted in calculus, this framework also serves theoretical research. Its utility spans several domains: deriving uniform equations for geometric spaces, applying the model universally to simplify distance calculations, and determining plane and dihedral angles, areas, and volumes in any dimension. Additionally, it aids in detecting parallel and orthogonal properties (where relevant), investigating previously undefined spaces, and more.

We derive fundamental hyperspherical trigonometry equations within multidimensional Euclidean space by employing vector products and translating them into identities for elliptic functions. We demonstrate that the core addition rules for functions defined on a 3-sphere embedded in four-dimensional space generate addition formulas for elliptic functions tied to algebraic curves possessing two distinct moduli. Furthermore, we apply these formulas to the multidimensional Euler top, establishing a connection to the Double Elliptic model.

Achieving high-fidelity DNA capture is crucial for nanopore translocation. We present key findings regarding the capture and subsequent translocation of a model DNA polymer through a solid-state nanopore under an extended electric field, utilizing Brownian dynamics simulations to track conformational statistics at every stage. By releasing equilibrated DNA from various equipotentials, we found that the capture time distribution relies on the initial position and adheres to a Poisson process. The electric field gradient stretches the DNA during its approach to the pore, increasing the likelihood of successful translocation even after several failed threading attempts. Even within an extremely narrow pore, a fully flexible chain retains a finite probability of hairpin-loop capture; however, this probability diminishes with increased chain stiffness, thereby promoting single-file translocation. Our computational studies distinguish characteristic mean first passage time distributions arising from single-file translocation versus those caused by different folding types, offering direct evidence supporting experimental interpretations of observed folds [M. Gershow et al., Nat. Nanotech. 2, 775 (2007) and M. Mihovilovic et al. Phys. Rev. Letts. 110, 028102 (2013)] in an isolated nanopore. Finally, we demonstrate that attaching a charged tag to the $5^{\prime}$ end of the DNA enhances both the multi-scan rate and the probability of uni-directional translocation ($5^{\prime} \rightarrow 3^{\prime}$), which would significantly benefit genomic barcoding and sequencing applications.

Dwarf carbon (dC) stars, which possess carbon abundances exceeding oxygen levels, do not form in isolation; instead, they acquire carbon-rich matter from a previous asymptotic giant branch (AGB) companion. Unlike M dwarfs in post-mass-transfer systems, dCs can be identified using low-resolution optical spectroscopy through C$_2$ and/or CN molecular bands, even after the AGB remnant has cooled below detectable limits. The accretion of significant material from AGB stars should theoretically accelerate the rotation of dCs, potentially triggering X-ray detectable activity rejuvenation. While dozens of dCs exhibiting photometric variability with periods under a day have been discovered, the majority are likely post-common-envelope binaries (PCEBs) synchronized by tidal forces rather than spun up solely by accretion. In this study, we utilize $Chandra$ to examine the X-ray characteristics of the five nearest known dCs. Two of these were detected in X-rays, corresponding to the only two cases where short-period photometric variability was also observed. We propose that the coronal activity observed in dCs results from rapid rotation induced by tidal locking in close binary orbits following a common-envelope phase, occurring late in the thermally pulsing (TP) stage of the original C-AGB primary.

Sanskrit Word Segmentation (SWS) is critical for digitizing texts and enabling subsequent tasks, yet it remains challenging due to the *sandhi* phenomenon, which alters characters at word boundaries and requires specialized handling. Current lexicon-based SWS methods utilize the Sanskrit Heritage Reader, a lexicon-driven shallow parser, to create a complete candidate solution space for various downstream methods to select the most valid option. However, these approaches struggle with out-of-vocabulary tokens. Conversely, purely engineering-driven methods leveraging recent deep learning advances fail to incorporate latent word information.

To address the limitations of both existing approaches, we introduce the Transformer-based Linguistically Informed Sanskrit Tokenizer (TransLIST). This system comprises three key components: (1) a module that encodes character inputs alongside latent-word information, specifically accounting for the *sandhi* phenomenon to function effectively even with partial or absent candidate solutions; (2) a novel soft-masked attention mechanism to prioritize potential candidate words; and (3) a new path ranking algorithm to correct corrupted predictions. Experimental results on standard SWS benchmarks demonstrate that TransLIST surpasses the current state-of-the-art, achieving an average absolute gain of 7.2 points in the perfect match (PM) metric. The codebase and datasets are publicly accessible at https://github.com/rsingha108/TransLIST.

This paper examines the application of conformal mapping techniques within perturbative QCD. The methodology relies on a Borel-Laplace integral regulated by a principal value prescription, coupled with an expansion of the Borel transform in powers of a variable that maps the cut Borel plane onto the unit disk. We derive the conformal mapping expression applicable to the most general singularity configurations of the Borel transform and analyze the properties of the resulting correlator expansions. In contrast to the divergent nature of standard perturbative series, these modified expansions display controlled behavior at high orders and can even converge under specific conditions. Furthermore, the expansion functions themselves exhibit nonperturbative characteristics akin to the original function. Leveraging these traits, recent proposals suggest that conformally mapped Borel plane expansions could serve as an alternative to the standard Operator Product Expansion (OPE). We briefly outline the arguments supporting this conjecture and explore the method's application to the Adler function for massless quarks and the static quark self-energy derived from lattice QCD.

This paper examines exotic resonant structures observed in the LHCb experiment within $\Lambda^0_b$ and $\overline{B}^0$ decays producing charmonium. Analysis of the $J/\psi p$ system in $\Lambda^0_b\to J/\psi K^- p$ decays reveals two states, both composed of $uudc\overline{c}$ quarks and identified as charmonium pentaquarks. Their measured masses are $4380\pm 8\pm 29$~MeV and $4449.8\pm 1.7\pm 2.5$~MeV, with widths ($\Gamma$) of $205\pm 18\pm 86$ MeV and $39\pm 5\pm 19$ MeV, respectively. The favored $J^P$ assignments exhibit opposite parity, corresponding to spins of 3/2 and 5/2. The discussion also covers models regarding the internal binding of these pentaquarks. Additionally, the mesonic state $Z(4430)^-$, which decays into $\psi' \pi^-$ and was initially discovered by the Belle collaboration in $B^0\to \psi' K^+\pi^-$ decays, is addressed. Based on a dataset of roughly 25,000 signal events, LHCb establishes the $J^{P}$ quantum numbers as $1^{+}$.

This study introduces a new hyperspectral unmixing approach grounded in deep spectral convolution networks (DSCN). The paper highlights three key contributions: first, it substitutes fully-connected linear operations with spectral convolutions to capture local spectral features within a deeper network framework; second, it replaces batch normalization with a spectral normalization layer, which enhances filter selectivity by standardizing their spectral responses; and third, it presents two fusion strategies that generate optimal abundance maps by leveraging abstract representations derived from earlier layers. Experiments conducted on two real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed method surpasses baseline techniques, as validated by lower Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) results.

Relativistic hydrodynamics has proven highly effective in characterizing the strongly-interacting matter generated in heavy-ion collision experiments. Recently, this field has advanced significantly to account for the spin polarization of hadrons produced in such events. While existing models utilizing spin-vorticity coupling have explained certain experimental results, they fail to clarify differential measurements. This gap suggests that spin must be treated as an independent degree of freedom, with dynamics not strictly tied to flow circulation. Specifically, if spin constitutes a macroscopic property of the system, its equilibrium dynamics should adhere to hydrodynamic principles. This thesis establishes a framework of relativistic perfect-fluid hydrodynamics incorporating spin degrees of freedom derived from kinetic theory to model matter dynamics in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. Aligning with experimental observations, we assume small polarization effects and derive conservation laws for the net-baryon current, energy-momentum tensor, and spin tensor using the de Groot-van Leeuwen-van Weert pseudogauge. We then examine the properties and components of the spin polarization tensor, analyze the propagation characteristics of these components, and determine the spin-wave velocity for arbitrary statistics. Our findings indicate that only transverse spin components propagate, similar to electromagnetic waves. Finally, we investigate the spacetime evolution of spin polarization in systems adhering to specific spacetime symmetries and compute the mean spin polarization per particle for comparison with experimental data. We conclude that our spin polarization results align qualitatively with experimental findings and other model calculations for certain observables.

Despite the extensive study of non-Hermitian topology, the impact of correlations remains a critical area of inquiry. We examine correlated non-Hermitian systems, focusing particularly on one-dimensional point-gap topology. Our analysis reveals that correlations reduce the topological classification from $\mathbb{Z}\times \mathbb{Z}$ to $\mathbb{Z}$ for systems featuring one synthetic dimension with charge $\mathrm{U(1)}$ symmetry and spin-parity symmetry. Additionally, we investigate an extended Hatano-Nelson chain that displays significant correlation effects, where these interactions eliminate the skin effect present at the non-interacting level. This sensitivity of the skin effect to interactions aligns with the observed reduction in point-gap topology within one spatial dimension. These findings provide new insights into the topology of correlated systems and suggest novel research avenues in non-Hermitian topological physics.

Building on our prior research regarding the acoustic determinants of warmth and competence in synthetic speech, this study extends our inquiry to how these derived vocal characteristics can be manipulated to generate such traits. Specifically, we examined spectral flux, mean F1, mean F2, and their convex combinations to enhance perceived warmth in female speech, while analyzing voiced slope, spectral flux, and their convex combinations to boost perceived competence. To achieve this, we applied a feature quantization method within a conventional end-to-end Tacotron-based speech synthesis framework. Listening evaluations revealed that combining acoustic features via convex combinations yields higher Mean Opinion Scores for both warmth and competence compared to utilizing individual features in isolation.

For every effective log motive over a field $k$ of characteristic zero, we introduce higher pro-Albanese functors and calculate them for each smooth log smooth scheme $X=(\underline{X}, \partial X)$. The resulting construction comprises an inverse system derived from the coherent cohomology of the underlying scheme alongside a pro-group scheme $\mathrm{Alb}^{\log}(X)$, which serves as an extension of Serre's semi-abelian Albanese variety for $\underline{X}-|\partial X|$. This work generalizes the higher Albanese sheaves developed by Ayoub, Barbieri-Viale, and Kahn.

Let $\alpha > -1$ and $\beta > 0$. We define $\mathcal{B}_{\mathcal{H}}^0(\alpha, \beta)$ as the class of sense-preserving harmonic mappings $f=h+\overline{g}$ in the open unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ that satisfy the inequality $|zh''(z)+\alpha(h'(z)-1)|\leq \beta-|zg''(z)+\alpha g'(z)|$. First, we demonstrate that every function in this class is close-to-convex within the open unit disk provided $\beta \in (0, 1+\alpha]$. Subsequently, we derive coefficient bounds, establish growth estimates, and examine convolution properties. The paper concludes with applications, including the construction of harmonic univalent polynomials that belong to this class.

This study derives the most precise bounds for the likelihood that the optimal value of a maximization-type combinatorial optimization problem surpasses a specified threshold, relying solely on the marginal distributions of the objective coefficients. These bounds are termed "extremal" because they hold for any joint distribution consistent with the given marginals. We investigate the computational complexity of determining these bounds under discrete marginals, pinpointing scenarios where polynomial-time solutions exist. Specifically, for compact 0/1 V-polytopes, we demonstrate that calculating the tightest upper bound is weakly NP-hard by presenting a pseudopolynomial algorithm, whereas the tightest lower bound is strongly NP-hard, a result established by focusing on Bernoulli random variables. Furthermore, regarding compact 0/1 H-polytopes, we address the specific context of PERT networks in project management and prove that the tightest upper bound remains weakly NP-hard, supported by a corresponding pseudopolynomial algorithm. Overall, our findings extend and complement prior literature on computing such probabilities under conditions of independent random variables.

We report the measurement of a novel set of jet shape observables for track-based jets in central Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 2.76$ TeV. This collection comprises the first radial moment (angularity, $g$), momentum dispersion ($p_{\rm T}D$), and the difference in transverse momentum between leading and sub-leading constituent tracks ($LeSub$). These variables offer complementary insights into jet fragmentation and help constrain various aspects of theoretical models describing jet-medium interactions. Measured with a small resolution parameter of $R = 0.2$, these observables were fully corrected to the particle level. The observed modifications in jet shapes suggest that in-medium fragmentation is harder and more collimated than vacuum fragmentation, as modeled by PYTHIA calculations validated against proton-proton collision data at $\sqrt{s} = 7$ TeV. Comparing the measured distributions to templates for quark- and gluon-initiated jets indicates that in-medium fragmentation mimics the behavior of vacuum quark jets. Additionally, we argue that the observed changes are inconsistent with a scenario of totally coherent energy loss, where the jet acts as a single color charge; instead, this implies the medium resolves the jet structure at the angular scales probed by our measurements ($R=0.2$). Finally, we note that small-$R$ jets can effectively isolate pure energy loss effects from other modifications to the jet shower in the medium, such as correlated background or medium response.

This paper introduces and investigates a new continuous space-time model for wireless networks that accounts for stochastic interactions across both spatial dimensions (via interference) and temporal dimensions (due to traffic randomness). The model features an interacting particle birth-death process that integrates information-theoretic spectrum sharing. Conceptually, wireless links or particles arrive via a Poisson Point Process in space-time, remain for a duration dictated by the local configuration of existing points, and depart upon completing a file transfer. We examine this particle dynamics to establish a precise and tight condition for time ergodicity, or stability. Furthermore, we demonstrate that under ergodic conditions, the steady-state distribution of links displays a specific type of statistical clustering. Leveraging this clustering, we formulate a conjecture to derive approximations, bounds, and asymptotic results for performance metrics such as delay and the mean density of links in the stationary regime. Finally, we combine this mathematical analysis with discrete event simulations to evaluate the performance of such networks.

This paper examines the motivation and present state of modeling plasmas subjected to intense radiation fields, specifically within the context of cosmic X-ray sources. The discussion covers relevant astrophysical questions, essential model components, existing computational resources, constraints arising from current atomic data, and the soundness of standard assumptions. Furthermore, I outline future directions, including challenges posed by upcoming missions, potential benefits from enhanced computing power, and objectives for gathering atomic data.

It is well established that determining whether a graph contains a Hamiltonian cycle or path, or whether a Boolean formula $C$ admits a satisfying truth assignment, constitutes an {\it NP}-complete problem. This work investigates the corresponding problems regarding the {\it uniqueness} of such cycles or paths in undirected, directed, or oriented graphs, demonstrating that their complexity is polynomially equivalent to that of U-SAT, the problem of identifying a unique satisfying assignment for $C$. Consequently, these unique Hamiltonian problems are {\it NP}-hard and reside within the class~{\it DP}, mirroring the status of U-SAT.

Built environment features (BEFs) encompass elements of the human-made environment that can either facilitate or hinder health-related behaviors, thereby affecting overall health. This study investigates whether the spatial distribution and volume of fast food restaurants (FFRs) correlate with obesity risk among schoolchildren. To address this, we developed a two-stage Bayesian hierarchical modeling framework. The initial stage analyzes the positioning of FFRs relative to schools by modeling their distances as realizations of Inhomogeneous Poisson Processes (IPPs). To identify representative spatial exposure patterns, the IPP intensity functions are modeled using a Bayesian non-parametric approach with a Nested Dirichlet Process prior. The second stage links these exposure patterns to obesity risk using two distinct methods to account for uncertainty from the first stage: the first approach regresses school-level obesity odds against cluster indicators representing major exposure patterns, while the second employs Bayesian Kernel Machine regression to relate obesity odds to a multivariate vector indicating the similarity of each school to all others. Our analysis of FFR patterns and obesity among California schoolchildren revealed that in 2010, ninth graders attending schools consistently assigned to a cluster where FFRs were most distant within a one-mile radius had lower odds of obesity compared to their peers.

Pollard demonstrated the complete monotonicity of the Mittag-Leffler function by utilizing contour integration to establish it as the Laplace transform of a positive function. He also referenced Feller's discovery of the same result through probability theory methods, which Feller published using a two-dimensional Laplace transform of a bivariate distribution. Although both original approaches are fundamentally analytic, they involve the stable distribution. We instead employ a Bayesian probabilistic framework that assigns a prior distribution to the stable distribution's scale parameter, treating Feller's method as a specific case within this broader assignment. This Bayesian perspective allows for the generalization of Pollard's findings, yielding a new integral representation of the Mittag-Leffler function and a variant derived from polynomial tilting of the stable density.

In nano-capillaries with a large aspect ratio, the attractive force from image charges is sufficiently strong to alter ion trajectories and reduce the fraction of ions transmitted through the capillary. We calculated this theoretical transmission fraction using a computationally efficient approximation for the image charge force, applicable to static ions at an infinite cylindrical dielectric interface. However, comparing these theoretical results with experimental data for nano-capillaries having an inner diameter under 200 nm revealed a significant discrepancy; the calculated transmission fractions were roughly an order of magnitude lower than observed values. Recognizing that the image charge force is velocity-dependent due to the frequency-dependent relative permittivity of the insulator, we investigated whether incorporating this velocity dependence could resolve the disagreement. We provided exact expressions for the dynamical image charge force at both plane and cylindrical dielectric interfaces as a function of ion velocity. Subsequently, we re-evaluated the theoretical transmission fractions for SiO$_2$ and PET dielectric interfaces, and our findings are discussed in the context of existing experimental data.

This study theoretically examines the voltage thresholds required for the director reorientation between homeotropic and hybrid homeotropic-planar states in a flexoelectric nematic liquid crystal (NLC) cell under an electric field. The NLC contains a CTAB-like dopant that partially dissociates into positive and negative ions. While one cell surface exhibits strong homeotropic anchoring, the opposite surface adsorbs positive ions that act as orienting surfactants for the NLC molecules. At specific voltages, changes in the director conditions at the adsorbing surface enable orientational transitions within the bulk NLC. We compute these threshold voltages as functions of anchoring parameters and identify critical values for these parameters; exceeding them prevents any orientational transitions from occurring.

In metallic multilayers, interfaces do more than merely alter the momentum of incoming electrons; by reducing symmetry, they also amplify spin-orbit coupling effects, particularly the reversal of conduction electron spins. This phenomenon causes a substantial decrease in spin current across metallic interfaces, a loss quantified by the dimensionless spin memory loss (SML) parameter, $\delta$, which serves as the interface equivalent of the bulk spin-flip diffusion length. This study employs first-principles scattering calculations that account for temperature-driven lattice and spin disorder to systematically examine three key factors governing spin transport at Cu interfaces with Pt, Pd, Py (permalloy), and Co: interface resistance, spin polarization, and the SML. The calculated $\delta$ value for Cu|Pt interfaces aligns closely with our recent findings for Au|Pt interfaces [Gupta *et al.*, Phys. Rev. Lett. 124, 087702 (2020)]. Conversely, for Cu|Py and Cu|Co interfaces, $\delta$ declines steadily as temperature rises, becoming negligible at room temperature. These theoretical results match well with existing experimental data. Furthermore, introducing a Cu layer between Pt and Py or Co layers slightly increases total spin current dissipation at these composite interfaces.

This work examines the forward Kolmogorov equation associated with measure-valued processes derived from a specific class of interacting particle systems within population dynamics, featuring adaptations of the Bolker-Pacala-Dieckmann-Law model. Assuming detailed balance, we rigorously establish a generalized gradient structure that accounts for fluxes generated by particle birth and death. Furthermore, in the limit of large populations, we demonstrate that the forward Kolmogorov equation converges to a Liouville equation, representing a transport equation linked to the mean-field limit of the process. Additionally, we prove the convergence of the corresponding gradient structures via Energy-Dissipation Principles, thereby deriving a propagation of chaos result for the particle system and formulating a generalized gradient-flow description for the mean-field limit.

We utilize kernel-based techniques that leverage samples from a probability distribution to approximate a Kolmogorov operator on a manifold. Specifically, the self-tuning variable-bandwidth kernel method [Berry & Harlim, Appl. Comput. Harmon. Anal., 40(1):68--96, 2016] generates a large, sparse matrix to approximate the differential operator. By performing an eigendecomposition on this discretization, we achieve (i) the inversion of the operator to solve differential equations and (ii) the representation of gradient vector fields on the manifold. Since these approaches rely solely on samples from the underlying distribution, they remain applicable in high-dimensional spaces or on geometrically complex manifolds where spatial discretizations are unavailable. Additionally, we implement an efficient $k$-$d$ tree algorithm to compute the sparse kernel matrix, addressing a significant computational bottleneck.

Ensuring consistent model performance requires the systematic quantification of data quality. While previous research has primarily addressed out-of-distribution data, we focus on the equally important but underexplored challenge of characterizing incongruous areas within in-distribution (ID) data, often caused by heterogeneity in feature spaces. To address this, we introduce Data-SUITE, a data-centric AI framework that identifies these problematic regions independently of any specific task model. By integrating copula modeling, representation learning, and conformal prediction, Data-SUITE constructs feature-wise confidence interval estimators derived from training instances. These estimators assess how well test instances align with the training set to answer two key practical questions: (1) which test instances can a model trained on this data reliably predict, and (2) can we pinpoint incongruous feature space regions to help data owners understand dataset limitations or inform future collection efforts? We empirically validate Data-SUITE's performance and coverage guarantees, demonstrating through experiments on cross-site medical data, biased datasets, and data subject to concept drift that it effectively identifies ID regions where downstream models are likely to succeed, regardless of the specific model used. Furthermore, we show how these identified regions offer valuable insights into dataset characteristics and highlight their inherent constraints.

The {\em Arrowhead} and {\em diamond} graphs are hierarchical Cayley graphs constructed on a triangular grid. When considered as undirected graphs, they are isomorphic, representing the same structure in two different ways. This paper provides formulas for their diameter in both directed and undirected settings and details the complete distribution of antipodal vertices.

We introduce a radiative seesaw framework featuring a light dark matter (DM) candidate within a setup governed by modular $A_4$ and gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$ symmetries. In this model, neutrino masses arise at the one-loop level, accompanied by a bosonic DM candidate ranging from $\sim 0.01$ to $50$ GeV. The stability of DM is ensured by a non-zero modular weight and a residual $Z_2$ symmetry inherited from $U(1)_{B-L}$. The smallness of the DM mass is naturally explained indirectly through the radiatively generated mass of neutral fermions that interact with the DM, meaning the DM mass need not surpass these neutral fermion masses, which are assumed to scale at 50 GeV. By examining multiple benchmark DM masses, we perform a numerical analysis of neutrino oscillation data for both normal and inverted hierarchies, identifying several distinct features in each scenario.

Particle deflection in oriented crystals and aligned atomic strings involves a coherent process driven by averaged potentials alongside incoherent scattering from atomic cores. Although high-energy coherent deflection transitions toward classical behavior, the incoherent scattering of relativistic particles retains its essential quantum nature. While this scattering resembles that in amorphous media at high momentum transfers, it undergoes specific modifications at low transfers due to the inhomogeneity of atom distribution within crystal planes or axes. Focusing on the axial scenario as a representative case, we propose a unified theory of high-energy incoherent scattering in oriented crystals that accounts for both quantum effects and atom distribution irregularities, thereby highlighting the limitations of traditional scattering cross-section concepts. Furthermore, we detail a method to integrate these quantum features into standard classical trajectory simulations by introducing a novel definition for the mean square scattering angle.

The dynamic/regional integrated model of climate and economy (DICE/RICE) is the most extensively utilized integrated assessment model for analyzing the economics of climate change. This document initially frames the RICE-2011 model as a dynamic game, referred to as the RICE game, before examining both cooperative and non-cooperative solutions. It subsequently outlines how to access the RICE-GAME repository on GitHub. RICE-GAME serves as a Matlab and CasADi-based implementation of the RICE game, including its cooperative and non-cooperative solution methods.

Blockchains are designed for permanence, ensuring that posted transactions remain immutable and unalterable. However, when theft occurs, the scarcity of options for reversing disputed transactions has resulted in substantial financial losses within the blockchain ecosystem. This paper introduces reversible adaptations of ERC-20 and ERC-721, the most prevalent token standards. Under these new frameworks, transactions become eligible for reversal during a brief window following their on-chain posting; once this dispute period concludes, the transaction becomes irreversible. During this window, a sender may petition a decentralized panel of judges to first freeze the contested assets and subsequently execute the reversal. Integrating reversibility into ERC-20 and ERC-721 presents numerous technical hurdles, which this paper examines and addresses through a design for ERC-20R and ERC-721R standards. Additionally, we offer a prototype implementation, aiming to spark a broader dialogue on reversibility to help mitigate losses in the blockchain space.

This study examines the propagation of quasi-harmonic electromagnetic waves through a bulk hyperbolic dielectric metamaterial. When group velocity dispersion is neglected, the dynamics are governed by either the hyperbolic nonlinear Schrödinger equation or the hyperbolic Manakov equations. It is demonstrated that, unlike in conventional media, the region of wave vector space supporting modulation instability of a spatially homogeneous wave is unbounded.

This work investigates classes of quantum algebras derived from involutive, non-degenerate set-theoretic solutions to the Yang-Baxter equation, along with their q-analogues. Following a presentation of universal properties concerning quasi-bialgebras and admissible Drinfeld twists, we demonstrate that quantum algebras arising from both set-theoretic solutions and their q-analogues constitute quasi-triangular quasi-bialgebras. We provide specific illustrative examples that align with these general findings. Furthermore, in the context of q-deformed set-theoretic solutions, we construct admissible Drinfeld twists analogous to those in the set-theoretic case, adhering to additional constraints imposed by the q-deformation. These results significantly extend recent developments regarding set-theoretic solutions and their q-deformed counterparts.

Drawing inspiration from Heisenberg algebra, the concept of minimal length is integrated into the geometrical collective Bohr-Mottelson model (BMM) of nuclei. Utilizing a deformed canonical commutation relation alongside the Pauli-Podolsky prescription, we derive a quantized Hamiltonian operator for triaxial nuclei, extending our prior work on axial prolate $\gamma$-rigid systems (M. Chabab et al., Phys. Lett. B 758 (2016) 212-218). By modeling the $\beta$ collective shape variable with an infinite square well potential, we obtain the Hamiltonian's eigenvalues as zeros of Bessel functions of irrational order, explicitly dependent on the minimal length parameter. The symmetry inherent in this constructed model represents a novel quasi-dynamical critical point symmetry (CPS) within nuclear structure. Theoretical findings reveal that the minimal length exerts a dramatic "Low effect" on energy levels at low angular momenta, whereas it produces a regular, significant effect at higher values. These characteristics suggest that the minimal length framework is particularly valuable for characterizing the properties of real deformed nuclei with high spins or strong rotational behavior. Finally, numerical computations for nuclei such as ${}^{124,128,130}$Xe and ${}^{114}$Pd demonstrate qualitative agreement with experimental data.

Cosmic voids serve as valuable cosmological laboratories for investigating dark energy and alternative gravity models. Recent focus on these regions is driven by new-generation galaxy spectroscopic surveys that cover vast volumes and extensive redshift ranges. Two key statistical measures in void research are the void size function, which describes void abundance, and the void-galaxy cross-correlation function, which encodes information regarding density and velocity fields. However, reliable cosmological tests require a comprehensive understanding of both geometrical (Alcock-Paczynski effect) and dynamical (Kaiser effect, Redshift Space Distortions) distortions surrounding voids. Unmodeled observational anisotropies can result in biased cosmological constraints. This thesis resolves this issue by establishing a theoretical and statistical framework grounded in dynamical and cosmological principles to describe all underlying effects: the expansion effect (t-RSD), off-centring effect (v-RSD), AP-volume effect, and ellipticity effect (e-RSD). These phenomena arise from mapping voids between real and redshift space, providing a basis for accurately modeling the relevant statistics. Furthermore, the thesis introduces a novel cosmological test utilizing two perpendicular projections of the correlation function. This fiducial-cosmology-free approach effectively breaks degeneracies between cosmological parameters and significantly reduces the number of mock catalogues required for covariance estimation.

The tourism and hospitality industries have faced substantial disruptions due to the COVID-19 pandemic, with public measures like travel bans and lockdowns severely curtailing tourist engagement and compromising the operational viability and profitability of service businesses. Consequently, creating an interpretable forecasting model to aid managerial and organizational decision-making is crucial. To address this, we introduced DemandNet, an innovative deep learning architecture designed to predict time series data within the context of the pandemic. This framework begins by identifying key static and dynamic features inherent in the data, followed by the integration of a nonlinear model capable of offering interpretable insights into historical patterns. Finally, a prediction model is constructed to utilize these attributes for generating robust long-term forecasts. We validated the framework using daily hotel demand and revenue data from eight U.S. cities. Our results demonstrate that DemandNet surpasses state-of-the-art models and effectively predicts the pandemic's impact on hotel demand and revenue.

This paper introduces new identification results for a key class of structural models that examine skill formation drivers and the optimal timing for interventions. It analyzes how seemingly trivial scale and location restrictions on parameters influence outcomes. First, I characterize the identified set of all parameters absent these constraints, demonstrating that critical policy-relevant parameters are point identified under weaker assumptions than typically employed in existing literature. While the consequences of imposing standard scale and location restrictions vary by model specification, they generally alter parameter interpretation and impact counterfactual analysis. Crucially, with the widely used CES production function, common scale restrictions are overidentifying, resulting in biased estimators. Therefore, merely altering the units of measurement for observed variables can produce flawed investment strategies and erroneous policy advice. I demonstrate how current estimators can be readily adapted to resolve these problems. Additionally, as a secondary contribution, the paper offers a formal and general definition of when restrictions constitute true normalizations.

Current Person Re-identification (Re-ID) methods largely rely on feature maps that are either segmented to isolate body parts or compressed into global representations. Although part localization has proven effective, it typically employs either simple position-based divisions or static feature templates. These methods assume parts and their locations are fixed within an image, neglecting image-specific context, which restricts their effectiveness in difficult scenarios like Re-ID with partial occlusions or incomplete probe images. To address this, we propose a Spatial Attention-based Dynamic Part Template Initialization module. This module dynamically creates part templates using mid-level semantic features from early backbone layers. Following a self-attention layer, we utilize backbone part-level features to extract diverse human part templates via a simplified cross-attention mechanism. These templates then identify and aggregate representations from semantically rich features, enhancing the model's overall discriminative power. Additionally, we investigate adaptive weighting of part descriptors to detect missing or occluded local attributes, thereby reducing their impact on the matching process. Extensive experiments across holistic, occluded, and partial Re-ID benchmarks demonstrate that our architecture achieves competitive performance. The source code will be provided in the supplementary material and released publicly.

Speech enhancement systems are frequently trained without accounting for human perception, often resulting in audio that sounds artificial. Recently, there has been growing interest in addressing this by integrating psychoacoustic speech perception metrics into model training through a predictor network. However, the effectiveness of these predictors is constrained by the limited range of metric scores present in the training data. To overcome this, we introduce MetricGAN+/−, an extension of the MetricGAN+ framework that incorporates a novel "de-generator" network. This component aims to enhance the robustness of both the predictor and generator by ensuring the training process covers a broader spectrum of metric scores. Experiments conducted on the VoiceBank-DEMAND dataset demonstrate a relative improvement in PESQ scores of 3.8% (rising from 3.05 to 3.22), alongside improved generalization to unseen noise and speech conditions.

When fine-tuning a convolutional neural network (CNN) on data from a new domain, catastrophic forgetting can degrade performance on the original training set. Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) is a recent method designed to mitigate this issue; we evaluated it by training and re-training a CNN for glioma segmentation across two datasets. The model was initially trained on the public BraTS dataset and subsequently fine-tuned on an in-house dataset containing non-enhancing low-grade gliomas. While EWC successfully reduced catastrophic forgetting in this scenario, it also limited the network's ability to adapt to the new domain.

Reinforcement learning (RL) methods are typically classified as on-policy or off-policy based on whether they utilize data from a target policy or a distinct behavior policy. This paper examines a nuanced difference between on-policy data and on-policy sampling within the RL task of policy evaluation. We find that on-policy sampling can deviate from the expected distribution of on-policy data after observing only a finite number of trajectories, a discrepancy that impedes data-efficient policy evaluation. To enhance data efficiency, we demonstrate that non-i.i.d., off-policy sampling can generate data more closely resembling the expected on-policy distribution, thereby improving the accuracy of Monte Carlo estimators for policy evaluation. We propose a technique named Robust On-Policy Sampling and provide both theoretical and empirical evidence that it converges to the expected on-policy distribution more rapidly than standard on-policy sampling. Empirically, this accelerated convergence results in reduced mean squared error for policy value estimates.

This study presents a deep learning approach for addressing elliptic hemivariational inequalities (HVI). The proposed method initially formulates an expectation minimization problem derived from the variational principle of the underlying HVI, which is then resolved via stochastic optimization algorithms employing three distinct strategies for updating network parameters. This approach is utilized to tackle two practical contact mechanics issues: a frictional bilateral contact scenario and a frictionless normal compliance contact scenario. Numerical outcomes demonstrate that the deep learning technique is efficient for solving HVIs, with the adaptive mesh-free multigrid algorithm yielding the most accurate results among the three learning methods tested.

Split learning (SL) enhances user data privacy by partitioning deep models across client and server nodes while retaining sensitive data locally. While SL matches the accuracy of centralized learning, this paper examines the risk of data leakage arising from local weight sharing among multiple clients during aggregation, using model inversion attacks as a proof of concept. To counter this vulnerability, we introduce Privacy-Enhanced Split Learning (P-SL), which eliminates local weight sharing to strengthen client-side privacy. We further propose Paralleled P-SL, which utilizes multiple servers to accelerate training without compromising accuracy. Additionally, we explore P-SL in scenarios with late-joining clients, implementing a server-based caching mechanism to mitigate the forgetting phenomenon. Experimental findings indicate that P-SL reduces client-side data leakage by up to 50% compared to standard SL. Furthermore, both P-SL and its caching-enabled variant achieve accuracy comparable to SL across diverse data distributions while lowering computational and communication overhead. The caching strategy in P-SL also alleviates forgetting effects, stabilizes the learning process, and facilitates efficient, low-complexity training in dynamic environments featuring delayed client participation.

Golay complementary matrices (GCM) have recently attracted significant attention due to their potential applications in omnidirectional precoding. In this paper, we extend GCMs to multi-dimensional Golay complementary arrays (GCA) and introduce new construction methods for GCA pairs and quads. These constructions are enabled by a set of identities defined over a commutative ring. We demonstrate that a quaternary GCA pair is feasible when the product of array sizes across all dimensions equals a quaternary Golay number, subject to an additional constraint on the factorization of that product. Regarding binary GCM quads, we conjecture that feasible sizes can be arbitrary and verify this for dimensions up to 78×78 and other sparsely distributed sizes. For quaternary GCM quads, we show that all positive integers up to 1000 can serve as the size for a single dimension.

Weakly-Supervised Semantic Segmentation (WSSS) enables object segmentation without requiring extensive dense annotations. However, the resulting pseudo-masks often contain significant noise, leading to sub-optimal models. Despite the inevitability of such noise even after improvements, few studies address it; therefore, we focus on mitigating noise to enhance WSSS. We observed that many noisy pixels exhibit high confidence, particularly when the response range is excessively wide or narrow, indicating uncertainty. Consequently, this paper proposes URN (Uncertainty estimation via Response scaling for Noise mitigation), which simulates noisy variations by scaling the prediction map multiple times to estimate uncertainty. This uncertainty is then used to weight the segmentation loss, effectively reducing the impact of noisy supervision signals. Experimental results demonstrate that URN achieves state-of-the-art performance, reaching 71.2% on PASCAL VOC 2012 and 41.5% on MS COCO 2014 without relying on auxiliary models like saliency detection. The code is accessible at https://github.com/XMed-Lab/URN.

In neutron electric dipole moment experiments, 199Hg serves as a comagnetometer, which is susceptible to a false EDM caused primarily by first-order magnetic field gradients (dBz/dz). This study investigates higher-order multipole corrections to this false EDM in 199Hg. We demonstrate that for spherical traps, all higher-order multipoles vanish identically. Furthermore, we show that for the standard cylindrical traps employed in EDM experiments, choosing quasi-spherical dimensions can mitigate these higher-order contributions. These findings underscore the significance of trap geometry for experiments aiming to control this systematic error.

Assessing predictive models is a fundamental aspect of predictive analytics, a task that becomes particularly difficult with time series data due to temporal dependencies. While numerous studies have compared various performance estimation methods for approximating a model's true loss, few have examined their effectiveness in model selection—choosing the optimal solution from multiple candidates. This research addresses that gap by evaluating several estimation methods specifically for time series forecasting selection. We investigate two primary questions: (i) how frequently do these estimators identify the best possible model, and (ii) what is the resulting performance degradation when they fail to do so. Our empirical results indicate that estimator accuracy in selecting the optimal solution is generally low, leading to an overall forecasting performance loss between 1.2% and 2.3%. Furthermore, we found that specific factors, such as sample size, significantly influence the relative performance of these estimators.

Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication systems depend on large-scale antenna arrays to mitigate significant path-loss inherent to the mmWave spectrum. However, due to hardware limitations and environmental factors, these systems are susceptible to antenna element failures and blockages, creating a need for diagnostic methods to identify faulty components for calibration. Existing diagnostic approaches typically rely on full or partial channel state information (CSI), which is difficult to obtain when antenna failures are present. This letter introduces a blind diagnostic technique capable of identifying faulty antenna elements in mmWave large-scale systems without requiring any CSI. The method jointly leverages the sparsity of the mmWave channel and the failure pattern, initially framing the diagnosis task as a joint sparse recovery problem. Subsequently, the atomic norm is employed to enforce channel sparsity over a continuous Fourier dictionary. To solve this problem, an efficient algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is developed. The efficacy of the proposed technique is validated through numerical simulations.

This paper primarily examines two categories of traveling stratified periodic water waves: those characterized by negative or absent surface tension, and those featuring a constant Bernoulli function with stagnation points. Initially, we derive a symmetry result for stratified water waves with negative (or no) surface tension that lack stagnation points, employing a modified maximum principle. Subsequently, we establish the symmetry property for stratified water waves with a constant Bernoulli function and stagnation points, contingent upon the prior knowledge of their monotonic behavior.

Current semiconductor research prioritizes either increased speed or enhanced linearity, or both, serving diverse sectors including consumer, industrial, healthcare, and military applications. These circuits are typically manufactured in standard low-voltage silicon CMOS processes, occasionally utilizing combined BJT-CMOS technologies like Gallium-Arsenide or Indium-Phosphide. However, these nodes encounter numerous challenges, such as reduced dynamic range caused by mismatch, distortion, and noise, alongside thermal and electromigration issues stemming from high currents. Furthermore, lower supply voltages restrict achievable amplifier gain. Traditional circuit techniques, including chopping, cascoding, and calibration, are approaching their performance limits. This paper introduces a novel approach to analog design by leveraging macroscopic quantum effects, specifically superconductivity, which have not yet gained traction in the design community. By employing staggered superconductors in amplifiers, integrators, and comparators, we achieve gain determined solely by physical quantum constants, rendering it invariant to process variations, temperature, supply fluctuations, and interference. This inherent gain stability significantly enhances linearity. Additionally, the proposed comparator can detect a minimum magnetic flux of 2.07 femtoteslas, and when integrated into a Delta-Sigma loop, it achieves a resolution 100 times finer, thereby pushing the boundaries of sensing capabilities.

This paper outlines recent experimental measurements [1, 2, 3] conducted at CESRTA [4] alongside supporting simulations designed to investigate electron-cloud interactions with stored beams. By testing across a broad spectrum of beam energies, emittances, bunch currents, and fill patterns, these studies aim to comprehensively characterize the beam-electron-cloud interaction and validate simulation tools. The selected beam conditions closely mirror those of the ILC damping ring, ensuring that validated simulations can accurately predict electron-cloud-related performance in these rings. Utilizing the Synrad3D code to model the synchrotron radiation environment, a vacuum chamber design for the ILC damping ring was developed that meets the necessary photoelectron suppression criteria. To estimate the anticipated electron cloud density, EC buildup simulations were performed based on the modeled radiation environment and the projected performance of the damping ring's mitigation measures. Finally, these density estimates were compared against analytical thresholds for instability to confirm that the vacuum chamber design effectively suppresses single-bunch head-tail instabilities caused by the electron cloud.

This paper examines the primary impacts of a discontinuous forcing term within a fourth-order wave equation defined on a bounded domain, which models the adhesion of an elastic beam to a substrate via an elastic-breakable interaction. Utilizing a spectral decomposition approach, we demonstrate that the principal effects of the nonlinearity occurring during the transition between attached and detached states manifest as a reduction in solution regularity and a redistribution of total energy across different scales.

We introduce Neural Activation Coding (NAC), a new method for deriving deep representations from unlabeled data to facilitate downstream tasks. We contend that a deep encoder should optimize its nonlinear expressivity to enable downstream predictors to fully leverage its representational capabilities. Consequently, NAC maximizes the mutual information between an encoder's activation patterns and the input data across a noisy communication channel. We demonstrate that learning noise-robust activation codes increases the count of distinct linear regions in ReLU encoders, thereby enhancing maximum nonlinear expressivity. Notably, NAC learns both continuous and discrete data representations, which we assess on two downstream applications: (i) linear classification using CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-1K, and (ii) nearest neighbor retrieval on CIFAR-10 and FLICKR-25K. Empirical findings indicate that NAC achieves performance equal to or superior to recent baselines such as SimCLR and DistillHash on both tasks. Furthermore, NAC pretraining yields substantial benefits for training deep generative models. The source code is accessible at https://github.com/yookoon/nac.

GRB 171205A represents a low-luminosity, long-duration gamma-ray burst linked to SN 2017iuk, a broad-line type Ic supernova. This event is consistent with either the core-collapse of a single carbon-oxygen (CO) star or a widely separated binary system, a scenario we term the Binary-driven Hypernova (BdHN) of type III. In this model, the collapse of the CO star produces a newborn neutron star ($
u$NS) and triggers the supernova explosion. Through fallback accretion, the $
u$NS gains mass and angular momentum; the energy released during this accretion drives the prompt emission. The observed multiwavelength power-law afterglow arises from synchrotron radiation by electrons within the supernova ejecta, energized by the rotating $
u$NS. We have calculated the mass and angular momentum accreted by the $
u$NS and modeled its rotational evolution. The neutron star spins up to a period of 58 ms before releasing its rotational energy to power the afterglow's synchrotron emission. The relatively slow spin of the $
u$NS accounts for the burst's low luminosity and explains why the supernova's optical light, generated by nickel radioactive decay, dominates over the synchrotron emission. Based on the $
u$NS evolution, we infer that the supernova explosion occurred no more than 7.36 hours prior to the GRB trigger. For the first time, this analysis of GRB data determines the specific timing of the associated supernova explosion, establishing a strict delay between the neutrino emission from the supernova and the electromagnetic signal of the GRB.

Boundary effects play a pivotal role in the dynamics of dilute charged gases described by the Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann (VPB) system. This paper investigates the existence and regularity of solutions to the VPB system featuring soft potentials within a bounded convex domain subject to in-flow boundary conditions. We demonstrate the existence of strong solutions over an arbitrary time interval $[0,T]$ for any $T>0$, provided the initial distribution function is sufficiently close to an absolute Maxwellian. Our results rely on a novel weighted energy estimate formulated in specific $W^{1,p}$ and $L_x^3 L_v^{1+}$ spaces tailored for soft potentials. Furthermore, by applying the classical $L^2$--$L^\infty$ technique alongside a bootstrap argument, we extend the validity of these local solutions from a small time scale to a large one.

Approximation Fixpoint Theory (AFT) offers an algebraic approach to analyzing fixpoints of operators on bilattices, serving as a foundation for defining semantics in various logic programs and nonmonotonic systems. This paper presents an additional application of AFT: it demonstrates that the alternating fixpoint operator by Knorr et al., originally designed for the well-founded semantics of hybrid MKNF knowledge bases, is essentially an AFT approximator in disguise. Leveraging AFT's abstraction capabilities, this perspective characterizes not only the well-founded semantics but also two-valued and three-valued semantics for these knowledge bases. Moreover, we introduce an enhanced approximator for hybrid MKNF knowledge bases where the least stable fixpoint contains more information than that derived from Knorr et al.'s method, thereby enabling more efficient computation of the well-founded semantics. This research extends AFT to handle consistent and inconsistent pairs within the induced product bilattice, addressing inconsistencies inherent in hybrid MKNF knowledge bases. Consequently, this extension generalizes the original AFT from symmetric to arbitrary approximators.

This paper presents and evaluates approaches for calculating $p$-values and confidence sets that maintain strong family-wise error rate and coverage control for treatment effect estimates in cluster randomised trials involving multiple outcomes. Although the necessity of multiple testing corrections is sometimes contested, the rationale for applying them is that uncorrected procedures inflate the probability of rejecting at least one null hypothesis beyond the nominal level, thereby reducing confidence set coverage below its intended rate. Currently, few $p$-value correction methods exist for this specific context, and none address the derivation of confidence intervals, which restricts their practical utility. We examine the Bonferroni, Holm, and Romano \& Wolf (2005) methods, along with their adaptations for cluster randomised trials via permutational inference utilizing efficient quasi-score test statistics and weighted generalised residuals. Additionally, we introduce a search algorithm for determining confidence interval limits through permutation tests to generate sets of intervals under each correction method. A simulation study compares the family-wise error rates, coverage probabilities, and efficiency of these procedures against uncorrected analyses, employing both model-based standard errors and permutation tests. Our results demonstrate that Romano-Wolf type procedures achieve nominal error rates and coverage even under non-independent correlation structures and exhibit superior efficiency compared to other methods in simulations. We further compare findings from these analyses with results from a real-world trial.

While models can be incorrect, this does not inherently hinder inference. Consider the standard $t$-test used to assess the significance of a variable $X$ in predicting $Y$ while adjusting for $p$ covariates $Z$ within a random design linear framework. This test ensures correct asymptotic type~I error rates for the null hypothesis that $X$ is conditionally independent of $Y$ given $Z$, even under an arbitrary regression model for $Y$ on $(X, Z)$, as long as the relationship between $X$ and $Z$ is linear. A similar robustness to model misspecification, which we label the "double-estimation-friendly" (DEF) property, applies to Wald tests in generalised linear models with minor adjustments. This paper examines this phenomenon and introduces methods suitable for high-dimensional regression that maintain the DEF property. We recommend specifying (sparse) generalised linear models for both the response $Y$ and the predictor $X$; our approach yields valid inference for the conditional independence null if either specification is accurate. When both are linear, our method reduces to a slight modification of the widely used debiased Lasso test. Furthermore, we explore constructing confidence intervals for the regression coefficient of $X$ by inverting these tests, offering coverage guarantees even in partially linear models where the effect of $Z$ on $Y$ is unrestricted. Numerical studies confirm the efficacy of this methodology.

Analyzing customer purchasing behavior is essential for crafting effective communication strategies between online vendors and their clientele. To address the growing trend of e-commerce, this study introduces a system that leverages supervised, unsupervised, and semi-supervised learning techniques to analyze purchasing behaviors at both the session and user-journey levels. This approach identifies distinct customer clusters, providing scalable insights for targeted marketing. Our findings reveal that session-level purchasing prediction is highly sensitive to the design of online shopping portals, achieving accuracy and recall rates between 91-98% and 73-99%, respectively. The user-journey analysis uncovered five unique clusters, where "New Shoppers" proved the most predictable, while "Impulsive Shoppers" stood out as the most distinct group, characterized by low browsing but high carting activity. Additionally, metrics regarding cluster transformation and partial label learning confirm the robustness of these clusters against new or unlabeled events. Consequently, these customer clusters can significantly enhance strategic targeted nudge models.

The Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUROC) has been widely adopted for imbalanced classification tasks, often integrated with deep learning methods. Yet, no current research offers reliable guidance for selecting suitable deep AUROC maximization strategies. This study addresses that gap through three key contributions. First, we evaluate various loss functions and algorithmic configurations for optimizing deep AUROC, covering ten functions across two categories: pairwise and composite losses. Our results indicate that composite losses generally outperform pairwise losses regarding training convergence and testing generalization, though pairwise symmetric losses are preferable when dealing with highly corrupted labels. Second, we analyze critical algorithmic decisions, including positive sampling rates, regularization, normalization/activation functions, and optimizers. We find that higher positive sampling rates tend to benefit AUROC maximization, dataset-specific regularization weights are necessary, and normalization techniques like sigmoid and $\ell_2$ score normalization can enhance performance. Third, we compare SGD-type, Momentum-type, and Adam-type optimizers for both loss categories. While Adam-type methods demonstrate superior training performance, they do not consistently outperform other optimizers in terms of testing results.
We introduce a class of interacting lattice boson models that exhibit full Bose-Einstein condensation in their ground state.

Proxima Centauri, the Sun's nearest stellar neighbor, is a small, mid-M dwarf star confirmed to host an Earth-mass exoplanet with an 11.2-day orbit within the habitable zone, alongside a longer-period planet candidate nearing a 5-year cycle. This study presents an analysis of extensive ESPRESSO spectrograph data collected at the VLT, designed to rigorously evaluate a previously hinted third low-mass planetary companion. Radial velocities (RVs) were derived using both cross-correlation function (CCF) and template matching techniques, with a Gaussian process (GP) employed to model stellar activity. The CCF's full width at half maximum helped constrain the GP, while other simultaneous activity indicators were examined to determine the nature of any detected RV signals. A signal was identified with a period of $5.12 \pm 0.04$ days and a semi-amplitude of $39 \pm 7$ cm/s. Subsequent analysis of ESPRESSO data subsets, activity markers, and chromatic RVs indicates that this signal stems from a planetary companion rather than stellar variability. The companion has a minimum mass of $0.26 \pm 0.05\ M_\oplus$ (approximately double the mass of Mars), orbits at a distance of 0.029 au, and exhibits an orbital eccentricity consistent with a circular path.

Observations of $J/\psi$ pair production in proton-proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy of 7 TeV have been achieved using 37.5 pb⁻¹ of integrated luminosity recorded by the LHCb detector. The cross-section for pairs where both \jpsi reside within the rapidity interval $2<y^{J/\psi}<4.5$ and possess a transverse momentum $p_{T}^{J/\psi}<10 GeV/c$ is determined to be $$ \sigma^{J/\psi J/\psi} = 5.1\pm1.0\pm1.1 nb, $$ with the first error representing statistical uncertainty and the second systematic uncertainty.

This study introduces the inaugural multidimensional simulations of core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) incorporating QCD axions to evaluate their influence on the explosion mechanism. Axions are incorporated via nucleon-nucleon bremsstrahlung emission and modeled as a pure energy sink, assuming free-streaming post-emission. We conduct both spherically symmetric (1D) and axisymmetric (2D) simulations; the 1D runs employ a parameterized heating scheme to induce explosions, while the 2D simulations achieve them self-consistently through neutrino heating. Our 2D results for a $20 M_\odot$ progenitor indicate that axion emission affects shock dynamics and explosion timing for Peccei-Quinn energy scales ($f_a$) up to $2 \times 10^8$ GeV. This intense cooling accelerates core contraction, enhancing neutrino heating efficiency and precipitating earlier explosions. Although the $f_a$ values influencing these outcomes are near, yet in tension with, limits derived from SN1987A neutrinos, the non-linear emission behavior and multidimensional dynamics suggest that fully exploring axion bounds and their impact on CCSNe requires self-consistent, multidimensional simulations that account for late-time accretion and cooling.

We constrain degenerate higher-order scalar-tensor (DHOST) theories by utilizing Planck 2018 likelihood data. Building on our prior work, which introduced a Boltzmann solver based on the effective field theory framework defined by six time-dependent parameters ($\alpha_i$ for $i={\rm B},{\rm K},{\rm T},{\rm M},{\rm H}$ and $\beta_1$), we employ the Markov-Chain Monte-Carlo method to determine the viable regions for both DHOST model parameters and standard cosmological parameters. First, within a $\Lambda$CDM background, we analyze a simple model where $\alpha_{\rm K} = \Omega_{\rm DE}(t)/\Omega_{\rm DE}(t_0)$, all other $\alpha$ functions vanish, and $\beta_1=\beta_{1,0}\Omega_{\rm DE}(t)/\Omega_{\rm DE}(t_0)$; this yields $\beta_{1,0}=0.032_{-0.016}^{+0.013}$ at 68% confidence level. Next, we examine a specific theory defined by the Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}_{\rm DHOST} = X + c_3X\Box\phi/\Lambda^3+ (M_{\rm pl}^2/2+c_4X^2/\Lambda^6)R + 48c_4^2X^2/(M_{\rm pl}^2\Lambda^{12}+2c_4\Lambda^6X^2)\phi^\mu\phi_{\mu\rho}\phi^{\rho\nu}\phi_\nu$ (with $X:=\partial_\mu\phi\partial^{\mu}\phi$), featuring two positive constants, $c_3$ and $c_4$. By consistently treating both background dynamics and perturbations in this model, we derive $c_3 = 1.59^{+0.26}_{-0.28}$ and establish an upper limit for $c_4$ of $c_4<0.0088$ (68% c.l.).

This study examines on-shell and off-shell Higgs boson production within the four-lepton final state, utilizing 80.2 fb$^{-1}$ of data from the CMS experiment at the LHC, recorded at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV. Joint limits are established on the Higgs boson's total width and its anomalous couplings to two electroweak vector bosons. These findings are merged with results from data collected at 7 and 8 TeV, corresponding to integrated luminosities of 5.1 and 19.7 fb$^{-1}$, respectively. Matrix element techniques are employed to combine kinematic data from decay products and associated jets, thereby identifying the production mechanism and enhancing sensitivity to Higgs couplings in both production and decay. The derived constraints on anomalous HVV couplings align with Standard Model predictions in both on-shell and off-shell regimes. Assuming a coupling structure analogous to the Standard Model, the Higgs boson width is constrained to 3.2 $^{+2.8}_{-2.2}$ MeV, compared to an expected constraint of 4.1 $^{+5.0}_{-4.0}$ MeV based on simulations. Including tested anomalous HVV interactions does not significantly alter these width constraints.

In the highly anisotropic organic superconductor (TMTSF)$_2$ClO$_4$, the superconducting (SC) phase coexists with metallic and spin density wave phases as distinct domains. By employing the Maxwell-Garnett approximation (MGA), we developed a methodology to derive the volume fraction and morphology of these embedded SC domains using resistivity measurements. Because of SC domain percolation, zero resistance can be attained even when the SC volume ratio $\phi$ is well below the critical threshold $\phi_c$. This percolation limit, which varies based on domain and sample geometry, may exhibit anisotropy. Applying our theoretical framework to various cooling rates of (TMTSF)$_2$ClO$_4$ samples, we determined the corresponding $\phi$ values and analyzed how disorder influences domain shape. Our results indicate that SC domains possess an oblate geometry, with their shortest dimension aligned along the interlayer z-axis. This finding contradicts the prevailing assumption of filamentary superconductivity along the z-axis, which has been used to explain the onset of anisotropic superconductivity. We demonstrate that the observed anisotropic resistivity drop at the SC transition is accurately described by analytical MGA theory incorporating anisotropic background resistance, whereas the anisotropic critical temperature ($T_c$) can be accounted for by considering the finite size and flat geometry of the samples. Specifically, due to the flat or needle-like sample shape, the probability of percolation via SC domains is maximized along the shortest sample dimension (z-axis) and minimized along the sample length (x-axis). This theory is applicable to other heterogeneous superconductors where the domain size $d$ significantly exceeds the SC coherence length $\xi$, such as in cuprates, iron-based, or other organic superconductors. Furthermore, the approach remains valid when spin or charge-density wave domains are embedded within a metallic background, or conversely.

Most current Vision Transformers (ViTs) struggle to match the efficiency of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in real-world industrial settings like TensorRT and CoreML, largely due to their intricate attention mechanisms and architecture. This creates a critical challenge: can a visual neural network achieve the speed of CNNs while retaining the power of ViTs? Although recent efforts have explored CNN-Transformer hybrids, their results remain unsatisfactory. To resolve this, we introduce Next-ViT, a next-generation Vision Transformer optimized for efficient industrial deployment that excels in the latency/accuracy trade-off, outperforming both CNNs and ViTs. We developed the Next Convolution Block (NCB) and Next Transformer Block (NTB) to capture local and global features, respectively, using deployment-friendly techniques. These are integrated via the Next Hybrid Strategy (NHS), an efficient stacking method that enhances performance across various downstream tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Next-ViT significantly surpasses existing CNNs, ViTs, and hybrid architectures in terms of the latency/accuracy balance. On TensorRT, it beats ResNet by 5.5 mAP (40.4 to 45.9) on COCO detection and 7.7% mIoU (38.8% to 46.5%) on ADE20K segmentation at similar latencies, while matching CSWin's performance with a 3.6x speedup. On CoreML, it exceeds EfficientFormer by 4.6 mAP (42.6 to 47.2) on COCO detection and 3.5% mIoU (45.1% to 48.6%) on ADE20K segmentation under comparable latency conditions. Our code and models are publicly available at: https://github.com/bytedance/Next-ViT

The emergence of scalable persistent memory (PM) has enabled the development of indexes that store and access data directly on the memory bus, offering the potential for instant recovery, low latency, and high throughput. Although initial evaluations of PM indexes occurred when real PM hardware, such as Intel Optane DCPMM, first launched, more recent designs have since emerged. However, it remains unclear how these newer approaches compare to one another and to earlier proposals, as well as what challenges persist. This paper tackles these gaps by experimentally assessing and analyzing current state-of-the-art PM range indexes designed for real PM.
