The network comprises fixed Base Stations (BS) with antennas whose vertical tilt angles can be adjusted via Remote Electrical Tilt (RET) optimization. While recent studies have applied Reinforcement Learning (RL) to RET optimization due to its ability to self-learn and adapt to uncertain environments, our approach prioritizes safety by enforcing specific KPI bounds to maintain performance in live deployments. Safety is guaranteed in our proposed architecture through model-checking techniques applied to discrete system models (automata) abstracted during the learning phase. Furthermore, we have developed a user interface (UI) that assists users in defining intent specifications and visualizing the distinction between an agent's proposed actions and those permitted or blocked by the safety rules.

This paper investigates properties of $\mathsf{Lie}$-centroids concerning central, generalized, and almost inner $\mathsf{Lie}$-derivations. Furthermore, we compute the $\mathsf{Lie}$-centroid associated with the tensor product of a commutative associative algebra and a Leibniz algebra.

Recent breakthroughs in image-based dietary assessment have enabled nutrition experts and researchers to enhance the precision of dietary evaluations by capturing food intake via smartphones or wearable technology. These images are subsequently processed using computer vision algorithms to estimate nutritional and caloric values, with food image segmentation—identifying specific food regions within an image—serving as a critical component. However, existing approaches rely heavily on data, limiting their ability to generalize across diverse food categories. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a class-agnostic food image segmentation technique. This method utilizes a pair of eating scene images: one taken before consumption begins and another after the meal is finished. By leveraging the difference between these pre- and post-meal images, our approach segments food by detecting salient missing objects without requiring prior knowledge of food classes. We adopt a top-down saliency paradigm that mimics the human visual system's task-oriented attention to locate these missing elements. Validation on food images gathered from a dietary study demonstrates that our method yields promising results.

Spoken Question Answering (SQA) involves identifying answers within spoken documents based on user queries, a capability essential for personal assistants. Current SQA approaches depend entirely on Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) transcripts. However, ASR requires extensive annotated data, which is costly and time-consuming to gather, especially for low-resource languages. Furthermore, ASR often fails to correctly recognize proper nouns or out-of-vocabulary terms that may constitute the actual answers. Since ASR optimizes for uniform accuracy across all words—including function words irrelevant to the task—it is highly desirable, though challenging, to develop textless SQA methods that bypass ASR transcripts.

This study introduces Discrete Spoken Unit Adaptive Learning (DUAL), a framework that utilizes unlabeled data for pre-training and adapts to the SQA downstream task. The system directly predicts the time intervals of spoken answers from audio documents. Additionally, we present NMSQA, a new benchmark corpus designed for more realistic scenarios. Empirical results demonstrate that DUAL achieves performance comparable to cascading ASR with text-based QA models while maintaining robustness in real-world conditions. The associated code and models will be made open-source.

Convolutional sparsely encoding neural networks share significant similarities with spin glasses, which are characterized by intricate dynamics and complex phase diagrams. By adapting established spin glass methodologies to analyze such a neural network, we observe power-law finite-size scaling in both sparsity and reconstruction error during the denoising of 32×32 RGB CIFAR-10 images. This scaling behavior suggests a continuous phase transition occurring at a specific critical sparsity level. Leveraging the inherent power-law relations of finite-size scaling, we can identify the optimal sparsity for any given network size by calibrating the system to its critical point, thereby achieving the lowest possible denoising error.

Deep learning methods are increasingly utilized in natural sciences for tasks such as material discovery, property prediction, and optimization. A critical requirement for these methods is a large volume of labeled training data, which creates significant hurdles in data-scarce environments where acquiring labels demands extensive computational power or labor. To address this, we present Surrogate- and Invariance-Boosted Contrastive Learning (SIB-CL), a deep learning framework that leverages three readily available auxiliary data sources to mitigate data scarcity: 1) abundant unlabeled data, 2) prior knowledge of symmetries or invariances, and 3) surrogate data acquired at near-zero cost. We validate the effectiveness and versatility of SIB-CL across various scientific challenges, including predicting the density-of-states for 2D photonic crystals and solving the 3D time-independent Schrödinger equation. Our results demonstrate that SIB-CL consistently reduces the number of required labels by orders of magnitude while maintaining equivalent network accuracy.

This paper investigates how electroweak sphaleron transitions or the electroweak phase transition (EWPT) can balance baryon excess against the surplus of stable quarks from the $4^{th}$ generation. By conserving all quantum numbers and charges, sphaleron transitions are shown to be possible between baryons, leptons, and the $4^{th}$ generation's quarks and leptons. We attempt to define a specific relationship between the magnitude and sign of the $4^{th}$ family's excess relative to baryon asymmetry within the framework of a second-order EWPT. Additionally, we demonstrate a small, albeit negligible, dilution of the pre-existing dark matter density caused by the sphaleron transition.

Standard multi-component silicate glasses are amorphous insulators that typically exhibit no unique magnetic properties, limited only to Larmor diamagnetism arising from core electrons and extrinsic Langevin paramagnetism caused by dilute Fe-group impurities. This study demonstrates that the macroscopic magnetization of three specific glass types, measured via SQUID-magnetometry, cannot be accounted for by Larmor-Langevin mechanisms alone. Specifically, we identify a novel {\em intrinsic} bulk magnetization contribution stemming from the amorphous structure itself; this effect displays distinctive temperature and magnetic-field dependencies and constitutes the first genuine magnetic phenomenon observed in nominally non-magnetic glasses. The sole known theoretical framework capable of consistently explaining these experimental results requires a re-evaluation of atomic organization at the nanometric scale within glasses.

The global COVID-19 crisis has resulted in catastrophic losses, prompting health officials to repeatedly advocate for vaccination to safeguard individuals and curb transmission. Despite these efforts, vaccine hesitancy has hindered vaccination rates in the United States. This research investigates the influence of such hesitancy on disease propagation by developing an SIRS-V$_\kappa$ model that categorizes populations into susceptible, infected, recovered, and vaccinated groups. We utilize the concept of carrying capacity to represent vaccine hesitancy through a vaccine confidence parameter $\kappa$, defined as the peak number of individuals expected to be vaccinated throughout the epidemic; consequently, vaccine hesitancy is expressed as its inverse, $(\frac{1}{\kappa})$. The study analyzes the stability and equilibria of this SIRS-V$_\kappa$ model to demonstrate, both analytically and through simulations, how vaccine hesitancy affects the trajectory of the epidemic.

Studies indicate that specific brain neurons respond selectively to particular stimuli; for instance, the fusiform face area (FFA) activates specifically in response to faces rather than non-face objects. Yet, the mechanisms through which the primary visual system channels information to appropriate higher brain regions remain unclear. Our research addresses this by developing a new computational model that replicates high-level perceptual mechanisms through hierarchical competition involving lateral and top-down feedback. We demonstrate that these components clarify information flow and selectivity in high-level brain areas and establish the basis for a novel classification framework that performs comparably to traditional supervised learning in computer vision. Furthermore, both quantitative and qualitative evidence confirms that our generative approach aligns with neurological principles while enabling simple yet robust category-level classification.

We have measured the complete elastic tensors of Mn$_3$Ge and Mn$_3$Sn across their respective antiferromagnetic phase transitions as a function of temperature. Significant discontinuities in the bulk moduli observed at the N\'eel transitions reveal strong magnetoelastic coupling in both materials. Notably, these discontinuities are nearly an order of magnitude larger in Mn$_3$Ge compared to Mn$_3$Sn. By utilizing the magnitudes of these jumps, we calculated the pressure derivatives of the N\'eel temperature, finding values of 39 K/GPa for Mn$_3$Ge and 14.3 K/GPa for Mn$_3$Sn. Additionally, we measured the in-plane shear modulus $c_{66}$, which exhibits strong coupling to magnetic order, under magnetic fields up to 18 T, observing quantitatively similar behavior in both compounds. Given that recent studies have established strong piezomagnetism in Mn$_3$Sn, our findings suggest that Mn$_3$Ge could be an even more promising candidate for this phenomenon.

Using first-principles density-functional theory, we investigate LaNiO$_{3}$-BaTiO$_{3}$ superlattices featuring various interface types. Our findings indicate that ferroelectricity is significantly strengthened in the superlattice containing (NiO$_2$)$^-$/(BaO)$^0$ interfaces compared to those with (LaO)$^+$/(TiO$_2$)$^0$ interfaces. This enhancement stems from polar discontinuities at the boundaries: these cause holes to localize within the (NiO$_2$)$^-$/(BaO)$^0$ interface, whereas they induce electron penetration into the BaTiO$_3$ component near the (LaO)$^+$/(TiO$_2$)$^0$ interface. These calculations suggest a viable pathway to achieving robust ferroelectricity in ultrathin BaTiO$_{3}$ films.

In social networks, true and false information often coexist and compete to influence how they spread. An effective approach to curb misinformation is to proactively determine whether nodes along the propagation path are likely to endorse or refute false content. This paper introduces SCARLET (truSt and Credibility bAsed gRaph neuraL nEtwork model using aTtention), a model designed to forecast the probable actions of nodes within these spread paths. By aggregating trust and credibility features derived from a node's neighborhood—utilizing both historical behavioral data and network structure—the model analyzes how the characteristics of spreaders' surroundings vary. Using real-world Twitter datasets, we demonstrate that SCARLET can identify false information spreaders with an accuracy exceeding 87%.

Quaternion-valued differential equations (QDEs) represent a novel class of differential equations with significant applications in physics and the life sciences. The primary distinction between QDEs and ordinary differential equations (ODEs) lies in their algebraic structure, specifically the non-commutativity of quaternion algebra, which renders the solution space of QDEs fundamentally different from that of ODEs. Rather than forming a linear vector space, these solutions constitute a left- or right-free module.

This paper constructs a systematic framework for linear QDEs, applicable to diverse fields such as quantum mechanics, fluid dynamics, Frenet frames in differential geometry, kinematic modeling, attitude dynamics, Kalman filter design, and spatial rigid body dynamics. We demonstrate that the algebraic nature of QDE solutions is that of a left- or right-module, not a linear vector space. Due to the non-commutative properties of quaternions, many concepts and properties standard in ODE theory are inapplicable and must be redefined. Within this framework, we introduce a quaternion-based definition of the Wronskian that differs from the conventional ODE version and derive a corresponding Liouville formula. Additionally, eigenvalue problems must be addressed by considering both left- and right-sides.

Building on these foundations, we analyze the solutions to linear QDEs and propose two algorithms for computing the fundamental matrix. Concrete examples are provided to validate the feasibility of these algorithms. The paper concludes with a summary and discussion.

We have analytically examined Rayleigh-Sommerfeld scalar diffraction under oblique incidence conditions. Explicitly, we derived the Fraunhofer diffraction formulas for plane scalar waves striking various apertures—including single slits, circular openings, and diffraction gratings—at oblique angles. These derivations, grounded in the Rayleigh-Sommerfeld scalar diffraction framework, hold significant value for undergraduate optics curricula.

We introduce the Posterior Bootstrap, a suite of algorithms that expand upon the Weighted Likelihood Bootstrap to effectively integrate prior information and mitigate model misspecification issues within Bayesian inference. Our approach incorporates prior knowledge through two distinct methods: penalizing the Weighted Likelihood Bootstrap objective function and utilizing pseudo-samples drawn from the prior predictive distribution. Additionally, we present novel methodology for hierarchical models, an area previously unexplored by Weighted Likelihood Bootstrap techniques. Guided by Edgeworth expansions, our framework offers deeper insights into the properties of the Weighted Likelihood Bootstrap than were previously available. Empirical results validate our theoretical findings and demonstrate a significant reduction in the adverse effects of model misspecification compared to standard Bayesian inference.

The LHCb experiment analyzed $pp$ collision data at $\sqrt{s}=7$ and 8 TeV, totaling an integrated luminosity of 3 fb$^{-1}$, to search for the rare decays of $B^{0}$ and $B^{0}_{s}$ mesons into the $J/\psi\gamma$ final state. The number of observed signal candidates aligns with the background-only hypothesis. Consequently, branching fractions exceeding $1.7\times 10^{-6}$ for $B^{0}\to J/\psi\gamma$ are ruled out at the 90% confidence level. Similarly, for the $B^{0}_{s}\to J/\psi\gamma$ channel, values greater than $7.4\times 10^{-6}$ are excluded at 90% confidence level, marking the first established limit for this decay mode.

Using the string-melting version of the AMPT multiphase transport model, we examine the transverse momentum dependence of the HBT radius $R_{\rm s}$ and the single-pion transverse angle distribution in central Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{S_{NN}}=19.6, 27, 39, 62.4,$ and $200$ GeV. By establishing a numerical link between these two observables through a series of functions, we can estimate the single-pion transverse angle distribution based on HBT analysis results.

Extracting geological lineaments from digital satellite imagery represents a core task in remote sensing. Identifying features like faults and dykes is crucial for various purposes, especially given their link to hydrothermal mineralization. While computer vision methods have been widely applied, there remains no standardized workflow for their use in mineral exploration. This study introduces a framework that combines edge detection and line extraction algorithms to identify geological lineaments within optical remote sensing data. The system incorporates additional computer vision tools to reduce data dimensionality, eliminate noise, and enhance lineament visibility. We evaluated this framework using Landsat 8 data from the mineral-rich Gascoyne Province in Western Australia, testing various dimension reduction techniques and convolutional filters. Validation involved comparing the extracted lineaments against manual photointerpretations and geological maps provided by the Geological Survey of Western Australia (GSWA). Results indicate that a Minimum Noise Fraction transformation paired with a Laplacian filter yielded the strongest correlation with the GSWA lineament map. Conversely, using a directional filter demonstrated a better match with our manual interpretations and known hydrothermal mineralization sites. Consequently, this framework, utilizing either filter type, offers a viable approach for mineral prospectivity mapping in other regions where faults are detectable in optical remote sensing data.

Given a graph $G$ with terminal sets $S$ and $T$ of size $k$ (which may overlap), our goal is to compute a vertex sparsifier $H$ that minimizes the vertex count while containing $S \cup T$ and preserving the size of the minimum $(A,B)$-vertex cut for all subsets $A \subseteq S$ and $B \subseteq T$, even when terminals participate in the cut. Assuming unweighted graphs, Kratsch and Wahlström (FOCS 2012/JACM 2020) previously leveraged matroid theory to demonstrate that a randomized polynomial-time algorithm exists for arbitrary digraphs, yielding a sparsifier $H$ with $O(k^3)$ vertices. Since then, no reduction in this size bound has been achieved.

This paper draws on Bollobás's Two-Families Theorem from extremal combinatorics and integrates total orderings into the methods of Kratsch and Wahlström. This approach enables the construction of a sparsifier $H$ with $\Theta(k^2)$ vertices specifically for directed acyclic graphs (DAGs). Additionally, we present an algorithm to compute $H$ in near-linear time relative to $G$'s size, surpassing the prior $O(n^{\omega+1})$ complexity. Our constructed $H$ also uniquely identifies the closest minimum cut in $G$ for every partition $(A,B)$, a capability absent in previous work. Finally, we establish that a sparsifier size of $\Omega(k^2)$ is necessary for both DAGs and undirected edge cuts.

We present a system capable of generating Mandarin pronunciations for Chinese text without relying on a pronunciation dictionary. By leveraging unsupervised methods, it constructs a many-to-many mapping between Chinese characters and pinyin syllables from separate, non-parallel data streams, effectively converting written text into speech. This approach achieves a token-level character-to-syllable accuracy of 89%, a substantial improvement over the 22% accuracy recorded in previous studies.

This study investigates the compact blister HII region BFS 10 and its highly filamentary molecular cloud. Using 12CO data from the Five College Radio Astronomy Observatory, we determined the cloud's distance, dimensions, mass, and velocity architecture. To characterize the central HII region, we combined infrared data from the UKIRT Infrared Deep Sky Survey and Spitzer Infrared Array Camera with radio continuum observations from the Canadian Galactic Plane Survey. These datasets revealed the ionizing photon rate and infrared luminosity, alongside a rich embedded star cluster linked to the central O9 V star. Analysis of the HII region's expansion timescale and the ionizing star's lifetime suggests a high probability that BFS 10 will evolve into a bipolar HII region. However, despite this expectation, the cloud's velocity structure provides no evidence for star formation triggered by colliding clouds. Furthermore, a search for embedded young stellar objects (YSOs) within the molecular cloud identified two distinct groups: one associated with the rich embedded cluster and another sparse group centered on an intermediate-mass YSO.

By analyzing the molecular fraction within the Galactic Center (GC), we quantitatively investigate the extent of molecular gas in the Central Molecular Zone (CMZ). Using archival CO and HI-line data, we calculate the column-molecular fraction ($f_{\rm mol}^\Sigma$) and volume-molecular fraction ($f_{\rm mol}^\rho$). The column fraction represents the ratio of projected H$_2$ mass density to total gas density (H$_2$ + HI) derived from line intensities, while the volume fraction reflects the ratio of H$_2$ to total gas volume densities based on brightness temperature. Our results indicate that $f_{\rm mol}^\Sigma$ reaches approximately 0.9–0.95 in the CMZ, whereas $f_{\rm mol}^\rho$ ranges from 0.93 to 0.98 in the GC Arms I and II, peaking at roughly 0.98 toward Sgr B2. The expanding molecular ring (EMR) exhibits a marginally lower $f_{\rm mol}^\Sigma$, between 0.9 and 0.93. We define the CMZ as the region where $f_{\rm mol}^\Sigma \ge 0.8–0.9$, situated between the shoulders of a plateau-like H$_2$ column density distribution spanning Galactic longitude $l = -1^\circ.1$ to $+1^\circ.8$, with a Gaussian vertical structure of $\pm 0^\circ.2$ half-thickness. This zone lies within the Central HI Zone (CHZ), an HI disc extending from $l \sim -2^\circ$ to $+2^\circ.5$ and $b = -0^\circ.5$ to $+0^\circ.5$. Finally, we discuss the CMZ's origin and interstellar physics, specifically inferring volume filling factors for molecular and HI gases by comparing $f_{\rm mol}^\Sigma$ and $f_{\rm mol}^\rho$.

Anticipating the availability of extensive Upsilon data samples at future high-luminosity heavy-flavor facilities, we investigated nonleptonic two-body weak decays of ${\Upsilon}(nS)$ states below the open-bottom threshold for $n$ = 1, 2, and 3. Our findings indicate that the branching ratios for ${\Upsilon}(1S, 2S, 3S) \to B_{c}\rho$ transitions are notably significant compared to other Upsilon decays into $B_{c}M$ final states (where $M$ represents $\pi$, $K$, or $K^{\ast}$), potentially reaching magnitudes as high as $10^{-10}$. This makes their detection promising at the currently operating LHC and the upcoming SuperKEKB experiments.

Gaussian process state-space models (GP-SSMs) constitute a highly adaptable class of models designed for nonlinear dynamical systems. These models integrate a Bayesian nonparametric framework to represent system dynamics with specific hyperparameters that control the characteristics of this nonparametric structure. By utilizing Bayesian formalism, the approach allows for rigorous and systematic inference regarding uncertainty within the system's dynamics. We introduce a method for maximum likelihood parameter estimation in GP-SSMs that maintains the complete nonparametric description of the dynamics. This technique relies on a stochastic approximation variant of the EM algorithm, leveraging recent advancements in particle Markov chain Monte Carlo to achieve efficient identification.

This study investigates excited quarks of both light and heavy flavors that decay into $\gamma$+jet final states, utilizing data with an integrated luminosity of 35.9 fb$^{-1}$ from the CMS experiment at the LHC, recorded during proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s} =$ 13 TeV. A potential signal would manifest as a resonance in the invariant mass spectrum of the $\gamma$+jet system, rising above the background predicted by standard model processes. No such resonant excess was observed; consequently, upper limits were established for the product of the excited quark cross section and its branching fraction across various mass values. These results represent the tightest constraints to date for the $\gamma$+jet channel, ruling out excited light quarks with masses under 5.5 TeV and excited b quarks with masses under 1.8 TeV, under the assumption of standard model-like couplings.

Despite the case of compact operators, a full characterization of Hilbert space operators generating weakly amenable algebras remains unresolved. Farenick, Forrest, and Marcoux posed the question of whether every compact weakly amenable operator on a Hilbert space $\mathfrak{H}$ must be similar to a normal operator. In this paper, we provide a counterexample: a compact triangular operator on an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space that is both weakly amenable and character amenable, yet not similar to a normal operator.

This work introduces two novel all-reduce algorithms tailored for imbalanced process arrival patterns (PAPs): the sorted linear tree (SLT) and the pre-reduced ring (PRR), alongside a new method for online PAP detection that incorporates process arrival time (PAT) estimation and distribution analysis among cooperating processes. The paper provides the underlying concept, pseudo-code, implementation specifics, performance benchmarks, and a real-world machine learning case study. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed solution offers superior scalability and enhanced performance compared to standard ring and Rabenseifner algorithms.

Autonomous quantum thermal machines offer a promising approach for managing thermal conditions in quantum systems because they operate without needing external coherent drives or work inputs. In this study, we introduce an autonomous quantum thermal machine where two uncoupled macroscopic mechanical or microwave resonators generate significant entanglement through interaction with a hot thermal bath. This phenomenon occurs when the resonators are linked to a shared two-level system or third harmonic oscillator, which is driven by the incoherent hot bath. A crucial component of this process is the engineering of the hot bath, specifically achieved through bath spectrum filtering. Our findings indicate that filtering the bath spectrum provides an alternative method to traditional non-autonomous reservoir engineering techniques for generating exotic quantum states.

We introduce PQuAD, a crowdsourced reading comprehension dataset derived from Persian Wikipedia articles. Comprising 80,000 questions and their corresponding answers, the dataset features 25% adversarially unanswerable queries. We analyze the dataset's properties to demonstrate its diversity and difficulty as a Machine Reading Comprehension (MRC) benchmark. By making this dataset publicly available, we aim to facilitate research in Persian reading comprehension and the advancement of Persian question answering systems. Furthermore, our experiments with various state-of-the-art pre-trained contextualized language models yield a 74.8% Exact Match (EM) score and an 87.6% F1-score, which serve as baseline metrics for future work in Persian QA.

This article investigates the narrow capture problem on a Riemannian 2-manifold, focusing on calculating the mean first passage (sojourn) time for a surface-bound ion modeled as a Brownian particle. By combining layer potential arguments with microlocal analysis, we derive both the leading-order singularity and the O(1) term for the mean first passage time and its corresponding spatial average.

Many machine learning tasks involve predicting structural data, such as graphs. For instance, in natural language processing, it is standard practice to convert text into dependency trees or Abstract Meaning Representation (AMR) graphs. Conversely, ensemble methods aggregate predictions from various models to generate a new, more robust, and accurate result than any single model could achieve alone. While numerous ensembling techniques have been developed for classification and regression, ensemble graph prediction has received limited attention. This study formalizes the challenge as identifying the largest graph most consistently supported by a set of graph predictions. Given that this problem is NP-Hard, we introduce an efficient heuristic algorithm to approximate the optimal solution. To evaluate our method, we conducted experiments on AMR parsing tasks. The results show that our approach successfully leverages the capabilities of state-of-the-art AMR parsers to produce predictions that surpass the accuracy of individual models across five standard benchmark datasets.

This paper introduces a dual formulation for Lyapunov's stability test and the Bounded-real Lemma applicable to Partial Integral Equations (PIEs). We leverage this formulation to address the $H_{\infty}$-optimal controller synthesis problem for ODE-PDEs that can be transformed into PIEs. Initially, we establish a general dual criterion for Lyapunov stability and the Bounded-real Lemma for PIEs utilizing quadratic Lyapunov functionals. Subsequently, we employ Partial Integral (PI) operators to parameterize these functionals, expressing the dual criterion as an operator-valued convex optimization problem featuring sign-definite constraints on PI operators, termed Linear PI Inequalities (LPIs). As a result, the optimal controller synthesis problem for PIEs—and consequently for PDEs—is cast as an LPI problem. Finally, we resolve these LPI optimization problems using the PIETOOLS computational toolbox and validate the proposed method through various examples.

Accurate motion forecasting within dynamic environments is essential for autonomous vehicles, yet it remains a difficult challenge due to scene heterogeneity and inherent uncertainties. To enhance forecasting accuracy, this study introduces a new consistency constraint: an agent's predicted future trajectory must align with its historical observations, and vice versa. To exploit this principle, we propose a novel cycle consistency training framework and a corresponding cycle loss function. Specifically, this method reverses the predicted future trajectory to feed it back into the model for history prediction, calculating the resulting discrepancy as an additional loss term. Experiments on the Argoverse dataset demonstrate that incorporating this cycle loss improves the performance of leading motion forecasting models.

As the core component of Hadoop, the dominant cloud framework for data-intensive processing, the Hadoop scheduler plays a pivotal role. Due to the significant impact of failures on application performance within this ecosystem, rigorously testing and verifying the scheduler's performance is essential. However, current methods, including performance simulation and analytical modeling, fall short of providing complete verification because they cannot adequately address the extensive range of constraints and aspects inherent to Hadoop. To overcome this limitation, this paper introduces a novel methodology that unifies simulation and model checking techniques to achieve formal verification of Hadoop schedulers. This approach specifically targets three key properties: schedulability, fairness, and freedom from resource deadlocks. By formally describing the scheduler using the CSP language and verifying its properties with the PAT model checker, we establish a robust verification framework. Furthermore, we apply this formal model to analyze the scheduler of OpenCloud, a Hadoop-based cluster designed to simulate Hadoop loads, thereby demonstrating the practical utility and advantages of our approach. The results indicate that this methodology can detect up to 78% of task failures early, prior to their execution on the cluster.

This technical report outlines the "Efficient" team's approach to the Multi-Moments in Time challenge at ICCV 2019. We begin by evaluating established Image-Based action recognition techniques, specifically TRN, TSN, and TSM. Subsequently, we introduce a novel temporal interlacing network designed for rapid and precise recognition, alongside an exploration of the SlowFast network and its variations. By ensembling these models, we attained 67.22% accuracy on the validation set and 60.77% on the test set, securing first place on the final leaderboard. Furthermore, we have made available a new PyTorch-based code repository that unifies state-of-the-art 2D and 3D video understanding methods and includes our challenge solution, accessible at https://github.com/Sense-X/X-Temporal.

This study extends the MacDowell-Mansouri framework of gravity through the application of strict 2-groups. We achieve this by developing a categorical generalization of the ISO(4,1) group, termed the de Sitter 2-group. Subsequently, we generalize the MacDowell-Mansouri theory via two distinct approaches: first, as a Yang-Mills-type model where explicit symmetry breaking yields an Einstein-Cartan theory coupled to Kalb-Ramond fields; second, by employing the categorical extension of BF theory, known as 2-BF theory. Adding specific symmetry-breaking and constraint terms to this 2-BF formulation results in the same Einstein-Cartan theory with Kalb-Ramond fields, accompanied by additional topological terms.

Plasma emission (PE), characterized by electromagnetic radiation at the plasma frequency and its second harmonic, is a ubiquitous phenomenon in both laboratory and astrophysical plasmas. While the dominant theory attributes this process to the resonant coupling of beam-driven Langmuir waves with ion-acoustic waves, we investigate an alternative mechanism: the generation of fundamental PE through the resonant interaction of Z-mode and whistler (W) waves. Although previous research has debated the viability and importance of this mechanism, our study demonstrates that the three-wave resonance condition (Z + W → O) is achievable across a broad parameter range according to magnetoionic theory. We further confirm the occurrence of this process and quantify the energy conversion rate from the pumped Z or W modes to the fundamental O mode using particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of wave pumping. This work proposes an alternative pathway for fundamental PE that may be significant in diverse astrophysical and laboratory contexts where both Z and W modes are readily excited via the electron cyclotron maser instability.

Semantic technologies are increasingly influential in scientific communication, finding extensive use across fields such as Life Sciences, Computer Science, and Social Sciences. Formal languages like RDF and OWL enable scientific knowledge to be accessible to both humans and automated systems. While previous efforts have primarily structured publications, methods, equipment, and datasets, the core claims or hypotheses of research have received only superficial treatment, often limited to linking entities to identifiers. Consequently, this study investigates whether existing semantic formalisms can systematically express the full content of high-level scientific claims. An analysis of claims from a diverse sample of articles reveals that their semantics are more complex than what standard RDF or OWL applications capture; however, we identified a distinct semantic structure termed the "super-pattern." We demonstrate how instantiating the five components of this pattern generates a strictly defined statement in higher-order logic. When applied to an expanded dataset of scientific claims, this pattern proved effective. Furthermore, knowledge representation experts achieved a high degree of consistency and convergence when independently instantiating the pattern for complex, subject-specific claims. These findings pave the way for representing high-level scientific discoveries in a format suitable for automatic interpretation, ultimately enabling automated consistency checking and advanced analytical capabilities.

The superconducting weak link (WL), functioning as a Josephson junction (JJ), is a fundamental component in superconductor research and quantum circuits. A hysteretic JJ capable of robustly switching between superconducting and resistive states is a prime candidate for single-photon detection. However, ubiquitous fluctuations within the junction significantly impact the stability of these states, thereby affecting the switching transitions. This study presents an experimental investigation into the switching statistics of critical and retrapping currents for a niobium-based WL JJ operating in its hysteretic regime. The mean lifetimes of the two metastable states—the zero-voltage superconducting state and the finite-voltage resistive state—are derived from their respective distributions. Additionally, near the hysteresis crossover temperature, telegraphic noise observed in the time domain, resulting from random state switching, directly yields these lifetimes. We introduce a thermal model featuring a double-well (bistable) characteristic and a unique parameter related to the device's temperature states, demonstrating how temperature fluctuations influence state stability. Finally, we discuss these findings in the context of enhancing the efficiency of superconducting WL or nanowire single-photon detectors.

Previous research by Mishura (2008), Prakasa Rao (2010), and others has explored both parametric and nonparametric inference for stochastic processes driven by fractional Brownian motion. Similarly, Prakasa Rao (2004, 2013), Cialenco (2009), and other scholars have addressed analogous issues involving processes driven by infinite-dimensional fractional Brownian motion. This article focuses on parametric estimation for processes driven by infinite-dimensional mixed fractional Brownian motion.

We design, simulate, and experimentally characterize a reconfigurable elastic metamaterial featuring beyond-nearest-neighbour (BNN) coupling, constructed using the widely recognized British Meccano$^{\text{TM}}$ system. This Meccano$^{\text{TM}}$-based metamaterial supports backward waves where phase and group velocities propagate in opposite directions. We experimentally confirm three distinct configurations and acoustically determine their spatial vibration spectra.

By combining dispersive representations of nucleon gravitational form factors, absorptive parts derived from chiral effective field theory in curved spacetime, and mechanical stability conditions, we derive a model-independent inequality for the gravitational $D(t)$ form factor at zero momentum transfer (the Druck-term). Specifically, this inequality yields a conservative bound for the Druck-term in the chiral limit of $D \leq -0.95(9)$, which imposes a constraint on the low-energy constant $c_8$ of the effective chiral action for nucleons and pions in an external gravitational field: $c_8 \leq -1.1(1) \text{ GeV}^{-1}$. For the physical pion mass, we establish a model-independent bound of $D \leq -0.20(2)$.

Using asymptotic approximations from Wilks and Wald within likelihood-based statistical frameworks for high-energy physics, we derive generalized formulas to estimate discovery significance across various measurement models. These models accommodate any number of signal and control regions alongside Gaussian constraints. We further extend these expressions to utilize the "Asimov" dataset concept introduced by Cowan et al., rendering them independent of specific data. Although many of these generalized formulas are complex and require solving systems of coupled multivariate equations, we demonstrate that they simplify into closed-form solutions under specific assumptions. Additionally, we validate the predicted significance through toy-based data simulations in selected scenarios.

Current methods for mapping-based cross-lingual word embeddings rely on the premise that the structural properties of source and target embedding spaces are analogous. These structures are primarily shaped by word co-occurrence statistics, which are dictated by the selection of the context window. Although the link between context window size and mapping-based cross-lingual embeddings is evident, previous research has largely overlooked this relationship. This study offers a comprehensive evaluation across multiple languages, domains, and tasks regarding bilingual embeddings trained with varying context window sizes. Our key finding demonstrates that enlarging both source and target window sizes enhances the performance of bilingual lexicon induction, particularly for frequent nouns.

We introduce Banker-OMD, an innovative framework that extends the classical Online Mirror Descent (OMD) technique for designing online learning algorithms. This approach enables algorithms to robustly manage delayed feedback and provides a general methodology for attaining $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{T} + \sqrt{D})$-style regret bounds across various delayed-feedback online learning tasks, where $T$ represents the time horizon and $D$ denotes the cumulative feedback delay. We illustrate the efficacy of Banker-OMD by applying it to three significant bandit scenarios involving delayed feedback: delayed adversarial Multi-armed bandits (MAB), delayed adversarial linear bandits, and a new delayed best-of-both-worlds MAB setting. Banker-OMD delivers nearly-optimal performance in all three contexts. Notably, it establishes the first delayed adversarial linear bandit algorithm capable of achieving $\tilde{O}(\text{poly}(n)(\sqrt{T} + \sqrt{D}))$ regret.

A recent proposal for a superdeterministic interpretation of quantum mechanics, termed Invariant-set theory, attempts to integrate concepts from chaos theory, number theory, and dynamical systems into quantum foundations. However, the absence of a well-defined hidden-variable model has hindered a rigorous evaluation of this proposal from a foundational standpoint. In this article, we construct a hidden-variable model grounded in the proposal and subsequently critically examine various facets of it. We demonstrate that several arguments within the proposal—pertaining to counter-factual measurements, nonlocality, the non-commutativity of observables, and measurement independence—fail when analyzed through our model. Furthermore, we establish that our model is both superdeterministic and nonlocal, featuring an ontic quantum state. We argue that the bit string defined within the model constitutes a hidden variable characterized by redundant information. Finally, by applying the analytical framework from our prior work (Proc. R. Soc. A, 476(2243):20200214, 2020), we illustrate the problem of superdeterministic conspiracy inherent in the model. These findings provide additional evidence that superdeterminism is improbable as a solution to the puzzle of Bell correlations.

We investigate Neural Networks (NNs) for keyword spotting (KWS) on IoT devices such as smart speakers and wearables. Given the goal of running these NNs within strict memory and computational limits, we propose a CNN architecture that (i) employs a minimal count of multiplications and (ii) maintains a low number of model parameters.

We present a straightforward proof of the Baillon-Haddad theorem for convex functions defined on open, convex subsets of Hilbert spaces, alongside several generalizations and limitations. Specifically, we examine equivalent characterizations of the Lipschitz continuity of the derivative for convex functions on open, convex subsets of Banach spaces.

Public perception often views solar energy as humanity's ultimate solution, with media frequently emphasizing the need to boost efficiency and lower costs. Yet, inconvenient physical realities regarding the limits of photovoltaics are rarely acknowledged by the public or by scientists and institutions biased toward an oil-free future. This work examines these physical constraints using Hubbert's peak theory, demonstrating that research disproportionately focuses on efficiency—a metric that is frequently overestimated. Often, higher efficiencies stem from complex, costly technologies that lack scalability. Consequently, if fossil fuels prove irreplaceable, our socioeconomic frameworks rooted in the past will likely collapse under an energy transition toward high-cost, low-quality sources.

Big data analysis faces a dual challenge of balancing privacy protection with data utility, specifically determining how to maintain accurate analyses after transforming data to safeguard individual privacy while ensuring the results remain meaningful. This paper examines multiple datasets to evaluate how different fully synthetic data generation methods perform a priori in terms of utility before specific analyses are defined, how closely their outcomes align with those from original data a posteriori, and whether these two factors are correlated. Our findings indicate that decision-tree-based methods outperform others generally, that imputation parameter choices—particularly the number of released datasets—have significant impacts, and that there is no correlation between broad utility metrics and analysis accuracy, though correlations vary for narrow metrics. Additionally, we observed promising results when using synthetic data to train machine learning models for classification tasks, suggesting a need for further exploration into leveraging these models to mitigate privacy attacks such as membership inference and model inversion.

This study focuses on coregular submanifolds within the framework of Poisson geometry. We demonstrate that the local Poisson saturation of these submanifolds constitutes an embedded Poisson submanifold and provide a normal form for this structure in the vicinity of the coregular submanifold. This finding not only recovers the normal form associated with Poisson transversals but also establishes Poisson analogues of certain normal form and rigidity results for constant rank submanifolds in symplectic geometry. As a practical application, we prove a uniqueness theorem regarding coisotropic embeddings of Dirac manifolds into Poisson manifolds. Furthermore, we illustrate how our findings extend to the context of coregular submanifolds in Dirac geometry.

Recent studies indicate that knowledge distillation effectively reduces network size and enhances generalization. For instance, a pre-trained, large teacher network can bootstrap a student model that surpasses the teacher's performance, particularly in settings with limited labels. However, the underlying reasons for this efficacy remain unclear; specifically, it is not well understood what enables the student model to perform "better." To investigate this, we employ two non-linear, low-dimensional embedding techniques—t-SNE and IVIS—to visualize the representation spaces across various network layers. Through extensive experiments involving different architectural parameters and distillation strategies, our visualizations and metrics demonstrate that distillation steers the network toward a more compact representation space, achieving higher accuracy in earlier layers compared to non-distilled counterparts.

This research investigates automated intrusion prevention through reinforcement learning. We adopt a novel framework that models intrusion prevention as an optimal multiple stopping problem. This formulation reveals structural insights into optimal policies, demonstrating that they possess threshold characteristics. Since dynamic programming is often impractical for deriving optimal defender policies in real-world scenarios, we propose a reinforcement learning method to approximate these optimal threshold policies. Specifically, we introduce T-SPSA, an efficient algorithm that utilizes stochastic approximation to learn such policies. Our results indicate that T-SPSA surpasses current state-of-the-art algorithms for this specific application. Our comprehensive methodology for policy learning and validation comprises two integrated systems: a simulation environment where defender policies are iteratively learned, and an emulation system that generates statistics to guide simulation runs and assess the performance of learned policies. We demonstrate that this dual-system approach yields effective defender policies suitable for practical IT infrastructure.

Binomial logistic regression is a staple in statistical practice, yet the maximum likelihood estimate can fail to exist when data are separable. To resolve this, we introduce a conjugate prior penalty that guarantees finite estimates. This approach offers a distinct Bayesian interpretation and possesses multiple invariance properties, making it an attractive prior selection. We demonstrate that the proposed method provides a precise approximation of Firth's (1993) reduced-bias technique, yielding estimators with diminished asymptotic bias compared to standard maximum likelihood and ensuring their existence. Furthermore, the penalized likelihood can be formulated as a true likelihood by substituting original data with a set of pseudo-counts, thereby enabling the use of existing, scalable logistic regression algorithms. When compared to other reduced-bias methods, our estimator significantly enhances computational efficiency while delivering strong inferential outcomes.

Surface adsorption serves as a foundational mechanism across diverse disciplines such as medicine, energy, catalysis, and environmental science. For decades, the surface and interface science community has sought an adsorption model capable of predicting binding energy within minutes, a goal that has remained unattained because determining the intrinsic factors governing adsorption energy across varying structures, compositions, and environments is inherently complex. We present a novel, adaptable model for forecasting adsorption energies on metal substrates, grounded in the readily calculable intrinsic properties of both the adsorbate and the substrate. This model was parameterized via machine learning using first-principles calculations of probe molecules (including N$_2$, O$_2$, CO$_2$, and H$_2$O) on various pure metal surfaces. When applied to a large dataset from \textit{Catalysis-Hub.org} spanning a 15 eV range of molecular adsorption energies, the model achieves a correlation coefficient of 0.93 and a mean absolute error of 0.77 eV for predicted dissociative adsorption energies. Because the model relies on pre-computed quantities, it delivers near-instantaneous energy estimates, offering sufficient accuracy to filter approximately 90% of candidates in screening studies for new adsorbates. Consequently, this approach substantially advances current research initiatives aimed at discovering novel molecular coatings for numerous applied fields.

Over the last few decades, the discovery of numerous complex organic molecules in interstellar space, many with prebiotic significance, has highlighted the immense challenge of tracing the origins of interstellar prebiotic chemistry and its link to biochemistry and life. While complexity theory and network science have not yet been fully leveraged to address this, we propose a theoretical and computational framework to model the progression from simple networked structures to complex ones. In our model, complex networks stand in for simplified chemical compounds, interacting to maximize the dynamical significance of their nodes. We observe a transition from simplicity to complexity occurring when an environmental parameter reaches a critical threshold. Remarkably, despite not simulating specific chemical rules or relying on external data, our results accurately reflect the emergence of complexity in chemical diversity within the interstellar medium. Additionally, the findings uncover a previously unknown correlation between molecular abundances in dark clouds and the potential number of reactions producing them, validating the framework's ability to illuminate real-world scenarios. Ultimately, this work supports the idea that the intricate journey from space chemistry to prebiotic chemistry and life may be governed by relatively simple and universal patterns.

This study applies the spectroscopy-based stellar color regression (SCR) technique to approximately 700,000 common stars found in both LAMOST DR7 and Gaia EDR3 to derive color corrections for the G - GRP and GBP - GRP bands, achieving sub-mmag precision. Our findings indicate that enhancements in the EDR3 calibration process have largely eliminated the color term in GBP - GRP and mitigated discontinuities resulting from instrument configuration changes, though minor systematic trends persist as a function of G magnitude. We provide the corresponding color correction terms across the 9.5 < G < 17.5 mag range and compare them with other determinations. We conclude that these corrections are ideally suited for color-color analyses, whereas color-magnitude studies might benefit from alternative corrections due to systematic effects related to reddening. Finally, we discuss potential applications of our results.

In collaborative filtering, data biases often propagate into recommendation outcomes. This paper specifically addresses mainstream bias, where systems favor users with popular tastes over those with niche preferences. We introduce NAECF, a straightforward yet effective approach to mitigate this issue. The method integrates autoencoder (AE) layers into text-based Convolutional Neural Networks for learning user and item representations. Functioning as adversaries during the minimization of rating prediction errors, these AEs—one for users and one for items—ensure that the distinct characteristics of all entities are adequately captured and retained. The resulting bottleneck representations are designed to reduce bias toward mainstream users, thereby offering more equitable recommendation utility across the entire user base. Experimental findings validate this approach, demonstrating significant improvements for non-mainstream users without compromising quality for mainstream ones. Furthermore, our results highlight the critical role of incorporating extensive content-based features, such as online reviews, to enhance user and item representation and maximize de-biasing efficacy.

The Earth's surface environment is predominantly shaped by the budgets of major volatiles: carbon (C), nitrogen (N), and hydrogen (H). While these volatiles are believed to have been supplied by chondritic materials, the bulk silicate Earth (BSE) exhibits a specific depletion sequence of N, C, and H. Previous research suggested that non-chondritic sources were necessary to explain this pattern. However, by modeling volatile abundance evolution across the atmosphere, oceans, crust, mantle, and core during accretion—accounting for elemental partitioning and impact erosion—we demonstrate that the observed BSE depletion can be replicated using solely chondritic bodies. This reproduction occurs through the partitioning of C into the core and H retention within the magma ocean during the main accretion phase, coupled with atmospheric loss of N during late accretion. This model relies on a relatively oxidized magma ocean ($\log_{10} f_{\rm O_2}$ $\gtrsim$ $\rm{IW}$$-2$), a dominance of small impactors in the late accretion period, and the sequestration of H and C into oceanic water and carbonates during the same late stage. All these conditions are naturally anticipated in the formation of an Earth-sized planet within the habitable zone.

We present a novel metric for regular languages called nondeterministic syntactic complexity, defined as the minimal degree of any extension of the canonical boolean representation of the syntactic monoid. Equivalently, it represents the smallest number of states in any subatomic nondeterministic acceptor. Notably, nearly all prior structural research on minimizing nondeterministic states effectively calculates this measure. Our methodology relies on an algebraic perspective that views nondeterministic finite automata as deterministic finite automata equipped with a semilattice structure. Importantly, these structures constitute a self-dual category.

This study outlines a method for identifying idiomaticity solely through the contextualized representation of MWEs using multilingual pretrained language models. Our experiments indicate that larger models generally perform better in idiomaticity detection; however, selecting a higher layer does not necessarily ensure improved results. In multilingual settings, convergence varies across languages, with resource-rich languages holding a significant advantage over others.

Neutrinos may exist as pseudo-Dirac particles, which are Majorana fermions that effectively behave like Dirac fermions. In this framework, active and sterile neutrinos possess nearly identical masses, meaning oscillations between them driven by their minute mass-squared difference $(\delta m^2)$ require extremely long baselines to manifest. Based on this hypothesis, an analysis of data from SN1987A reveals a slight preference for a non-zero $(\delta m^2)$. Furthermore, this dataset allows for the exclusion of $(\delta m^2)$ values around $10^{-20}{\rm eV}^2$, representing the most stringent lower bound established to date. We also examine the potential of future facilities, such as DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande, to investigate this scenario in the event of a galactic supernova.

Accurately forecasting stochastic spreading dynamics on complex networks is essential for managing epidemics, tracking opinion shifts, and executing viral marketing campaigns. Our research centers on estimating the time-evolving marginal probabilities of node states, which collectively measure spreading outcomes. While Dynamic Message Passing (DMP) serves as a highly efficient inference method for various spreading models and achieves asymptotic exactness on locally tree-like structures, it often falters when applied to diffusion networks containing numerous local loops. To overcome this constraint, we employ Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to implicitly capture message dependencies. We introduce a hybrid framework where the GNN component operates concurrently with DMP equations; specifically, the GNN refines the aggregated messages within DMP iterations by learning directly from simulation data. Numerical experiments confirm that, after training, our approach significantly surpasses DMP in inference accuracy across diverse network structures and dynamic parameters. Furthermore, unlike purely data-driven models, our hybrid architecture demonstrates superior generalization on out-of-training cases by leveraging explicit dynamic priors. A PyTorch implementation is available at https://github.com/FeiGSSS/NEDMP.

This study meticulously explores the persistent current in a mesoscopic cylinder penetrated by an Aharonov-Bohm flux $\phi$ using a Hartree-Fock mean field framework. We analyze how second-neighbor hopping and Hubbard correlations jointly enhance the persistent current amidst disorder. A marked variation in current amplitude is noted when compared to conventional nearest-neighbor hopping models, bringing the theoretical predictions into closer alignment with experimental observations. Furthermore, our investigation yields several intriguing findings that have previously been overlooked.

Co-Salient Object Detection (CoSOD) seeks to emulate the human visual system by identifying common and salient objects across a set of related images. Although recent approaches utilizing advanced deep learning models have significantly enhanced CoSOD performance, two critical limitations remain: insufficient modeling of inter-image relationships and a lack of attention to inter-image separability. To address these issues, we introduce the Co-Salient Object Detection Transformer (CoSformer), which leverages Transformer architecture to capture both salient and common visual patterns from multiple inputs. This design mitigates the impact of input ordering and substantially improves task stability. Furthermore, we propose a novel concept of inter-image separability, employing a contrastive learning framework to model this separability and create a more discriminative embedding space capable of distinguishing genuine common objects from noise. Extensive evaluations on three demanding benchmarks—CoCA, CoSOD3k, and Cosal2015—demonstrate that CoSformer surpasses current state-of-the-art models. We anticipate that CoSformer will inspire future research into broader visual co-analysis applications.

An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) serves as a critical security tool capable of automatically scrutinizing network traffic to identify suspicious behavior. While extensively deployed across various business networks to ensure security, these systems often generate a deluge of unnecessary alerts due to a high rate of false positives, burdening security analysts. This project addresses the false-positive issue within esNetwork, an IDS product developed by eSentire Inc., by employing a Random Forest (RF) classifier. The RF model is designed to categorize alerts into high and low likelihood tiers, ensuring that only high-probability alerts are forwarded to analysts. Experimental evaluations indicate the model achieves 97% accuracy on training validation data, 88% on recent testing data, and 58% on events reviewed by the Security Operations Centre (SOC). These intermediate results are attributed to a lack of clearly labeled training data and limited SOC-reviewed events for assessment. Consequently, further fine-tuning is required for the model to satisfy industry deployment standards.

This study focuses on the blind identification of graph filters from graph signals, specifically aiming to ascertain whether the generating filter is a first-order lowpass type without prior knowledge of the graph topology. Such a filter is a fundamental requirement for applying graph signal processing techniques in sampling, denoising, and graph learning. Drawing inspiration from the Perron Frobenius theorem, we observe that for a first-order lowpass graph filter, the top eigenvector of the output covariance matrix is uniquely characterized by elements sharing the same sign. Leveraging this property, we propose a straightforward detector to determine if a given dataset originates from such a filter. Furthermore, we evaluate the detector's performance under varying conditions, including finite sample sizes, graph dimensions, observation noise levels, and the strength of the lowpass filter. Numerical experiments conducted on both synthetic and real-world data validate our conclusions.

The discrepancy between training datasets and real-world production data is a widely recognized challenge. Since training sets are typically built within a specific timeframe through careful curation for labeling, they often fail to capture the full range of variations found in live environments. In this case study, we examine an entity resolution system designed to identify and merge records representing the same individual, which initially showed a significant performance drop when moving from training to production. We detail our human-in-the-loop, data-centric approach to bridging this gap and conclude with broader insights applicable to data-centric learning.

Recent theoretical investigations have demonstrated that the interplay between coherent unitary evolution and stochastic environmental measurements along wavefunction trajectories can trigger transitions in entanglement scaling. Building on these findings, we examine a scenario where the roles of Hamiltonian and dissipative dynamics are inverted. Specifically, we investigate engineered dissipation that stabilizes an entangled phase in a quantum spin-1/2 chain, which competes against single-particle or interacting Hamiltonian dynamics driving the system toward a disentangled phase. Focusing on single-particle unitary dynamics, we observe an entanglement transition from logarithmic growth to an area law as the ratio between unitary and non-unitary dynamics increases. We show that this transition appears in state-dependent observables at a finite competition ratio for Hamiltonian and measurement dynamics. Conversely, it does not manifest in trajectory-averaged steady-state dynamics described by a Lindblad master equation; while purely dissipative dynamics maintains an entangled state, any non-zero Hamiltonian contribution inevitably drives the system into a disordered phase. Furthermore, single-trajectory analysis indicates that the distribution of entanglement entropy serves as a sensitive marker for this transition. Additionally, we explore the competition between dissipation and coherent dynamics arising from an interacting Hamiltonian, confirming that the entanglement transition persists in this second model. These results imply that such transitions occur across a broader range of Hamiltonians, highlighting their robustness within monitored open quantum many-body systems.

We present CaloFlow, a high-speed detector simulation framework built upon normalizing flows. This work establishes, for the first time, that normalizing flows can replicate multi-channel calorimeter showers with exceptional fidelity, offering a novel alternative to computationally intensive GEANT4 simulations and other leading fast simulation methods based on GANs and VAEs. Beyond standard histograms and shower images, we propose a new metric for evaluating generative modeling quality: the ability of a classifier to distinguish between real and generated images. Our results show that classifiers can identify GAN-generated images with nearly 100% accuracy, whereas CaloFlow-generated images successfully evade detection. More broadly, normalizing flows surpass current state-of-the-art approaches (GANs and VAEs) by providing tractable likelihoods, stable and convergent training, and principled model selection. Additionally, the bijective mapping between data and latent space inherent in normalizing flows opens possibilities for applications beyond simulation, such as detector unfolding.

Current and upcoming cosmological studies utilizing Type Ia Supernovae (SNe Ia) encounter three major hurdles: determining redshifts from the supernova or its host galaxy, classifying SNe without spectral data, and managing correlations between SNe Ia properties and their host environments. This work introduces a new method to tackle all three issues within the Dark Energy Survey (DES) framework. By analyzing a sample of SNe Ia located in the redMaGiC catalog of Luminous Red Galaxies—where photo-$z$ estimates are projected to have an accuracy of $\sigma_{\Delta z/(1+z)}\sim0.02$—we evaluate a photometrically classified SNIa dataset containing roughly 1600 events, 125 of which reside in redMaGiC galaxies. Our findings indicate that redMaGiC galaxies predominantly host SNe Ia, thereby mitigating classification uncertainties. Using this subset, we achieve Hubble scatter comparable to spectroscopic redshifts (within $\sim0.01$ mag) when relying on photometric redshifts. Extensive simulations reveal that employing photo-$z$s from redMaGiC hosts introduces a bias in the dark energy equation-of-state parameter $w$ of up to $\Delta w \sim 0.01-0.02$, whereas actual data analysis shows a difference of $\Delta w = 0.005$ between photometric and spectroscopic redshifts. Furthermore, we observe that SNe in redMaGiC galaxies form a more standardizable population than the DES-3YR group, evidenced by a weaker color-luminosity relation ($\beta$) significant at $\sim5\sigma$. This aligns with theoretical expectations that redMaGiC hosts exhibit lower reddening ratios ($\textrm{R}_\textrm{V}$) compared to the general host galaxy population. Ultimately, these results confirm the viability of conducting redMaGiC-based SN cosmology using photometric survey data even without spectroscopic information.

Video frames vary in their utility for action recognition, making it computationally impractical to train deep networks on every frame when actions unfold over hundreds of frames. While a common approach involves uniformly sampling a limited subset of frames, we propose a full video action recognition framework that leverages all available frames. To ensure computational feasibility, we cluster frame activations along the temporal axis based on their task-relevant similarity and then aggregate frames within each cluster into condensed representations. Our method is both end-to-end trainable and efficient, relying on temporally localized clustering paired with rapid Hamming distance calculations in feature space. We validate our approach on UCF101, HMDB51, Breakfast, and Something-Something V1 and V2, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing heuristic sampling techniques.

The optical properties of bulk germanium sulfide (GeS) have been systematically analyzed using various polarization-resolved methods, including photoluminescence (PL), reflectance contrast (RC), and Raman scattering (RS). Results indicate that although low-temperature (T=5 K) optical band-gap absorption stems from a single resonance associated with the neutral exciton, the corresponding emission is primarily driven by disorder, impurity, and/or phonon-assisted recombination. Both RC and PL spectra exhibit linear polarization along the armchair direction. Raman spectra collected at both low and room temperatures (T=300 K) display six distinct peaks—identified via Density Functional Theory (DFT) as A$^1_{\textrm{g}}$, A$^2_{\textrm{g}}$, A$^3_{\textrm{g}}$, A$^4_{\textrm{g}}$, B$^1_{\textrm{1g}}$, and B$^2_{\textrm{1g}}$—whose polarization characteristics were examined across four different excitation energies. It was determined that the polarization orientations of the A$^2_{\textrm{g}}$ and A$^4_{\textrm{g}}$ modes at specific excitation energies serve as effective indicators for identifying the armchair and zigzag crystallographic directions in GeS.

Deep neural networks typically require vast amounts of training data, yet real-world scenarios often face data scarcity. To address this limitation, unsupervised methods are employed to train models with limited datasets. This report outlines an unsupervised semantic feature learning approach designed to recognize geometric transformations applied to input data. The core principle is that without knowledge of the objects within images, it is impossible to accurately predict the geometric transformations undergone. This self-supervised framework relies on a pretext task and a downstream task. Specifically, the pretext classification task aims to quantify geometric transformations, thereby compelling the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to learn high-level, salient object features beneficial for image classification. In our baseline model, image rotations are defined in multiples of 90 degrees. The CNN trained on this pretext task is subsequently utilized for image classification within the CIFAR-10 dataset as the downstream task. We evaluated the baseline method using various architectures, including ResNet, DenseNet, VGG-16, and NIN, experimenting with different rotation counts and feature extraction or fine-tuning configurations. Furthermore, we extended this baseline by exploring pretext tasks involving transformations beyond simple rotation. We compared the performance of selected models across diverse settings, including different applied transformations, various data augmentation techniques, and distinct optimizers. This comprehensive series of experiments aims to demonstrate the recognition accuracy of our self-supervised model when applied to the downstream classification task.

Let $K$ represent prefix-free Kolmogorov Complexity, with $K^A$ denoting its relativized counterpart with respect to oracle $A$. We demonstrate that for every $n$, $K^{\emptyset^{(n)}}$ can be defined exclusively using the unrelativized $K$. While it was previously established that 2-randomness is characterizable via $K$ (and plain complexity $C$) as the set of reals exhibiting maximal complexity infinitely often, our characterization enables a proof that $n$-randomness is likewise definable solely in terms of $K$. This result is achieved by extending a specific "limsup" formula found in existing literature and applying the Symmetry of Information principle. This extension involves an innovative application of semilow sets and a refined analysis regarding the complexity of $\Delta_2^0$ sets containing minimal descriptions.

This study employs a direct method to examine the generalized Hyers-Ulam stability of the reciprocal functional equation
\begin{equation*}f(2x+y)+f\left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right)
=\frac{2f(x)f(y)}{f(x)+f(y)}+\frac{2f(x+y)f(y-x)}{3f(y-x)-f(x+y)}\end{equation*}
within the framework of non-Archimedean spaces.

Phase I oncology trials are designed to identify the maximum tolerated dose (MTD), typically based on the rate of short-term dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs). While many existing model-based strategies focus solely on DLTs observed during the initial treatment cycle, patients often continue therapy for multiple cycles. This study introduces a Bayesian cumulative modeling framework to estimate the probability of DLTs across sequences of treatment cycles, accounting for both the cumulative impact of the drug and the specific cycle in which toxicity occurs. We propose a new design termed DICE (Dose-fInding CumulativE) to guide dose escalation and de-escalation based on historical toxicity data, with the goal of determining the optimal MTD sequence (MTS). Through extensive simulations comparing our method against the time-to-event continual reassessment method (TITE-CRM) and a standard benchmark, we found that our approach achieved equal or superior accuracy in selecting the correct MTS. Additionally, we evaluated the predictive performance of the DICE model.

This paper investigates the component-wise equivariant estimation of order-restricted location and scale parameters within a general bivariate distribution framework, subject to broad conditions on the underlying distributions and loss functions. It consolidates existing literature findings regarding sufficient conditions for enhancing arbitrary location/scale equivariant estimators, demonstrating their utility through multiple examples. Furthermore, a simulation study evaluates the risk performance of various estimators under bivariate normal and independent gamma models, while a real-life data analysis confirms the practical applicability of the derived results.

This report supports the release of a dataset comprising visual and thermal imagery, outlining a method for aligning these multi-modal frames to establish pixel-level correspondence without relying on intrinsic or extrinsic calibration data. We leverage advancements in multi-modal image alignment, specifically utilizing the Mattes Mutual Information Metric to drive the registration process. The released dataset includes the raw visual and thermal recordings, the corresponding aligned frames, and calibration parameters, all intended to facilitate deeper investigation into local and global features shared across these multi-modal image streams.

This study presents integral field spectroscopic data of the nearby galaxy NGC 5972, acquired using the Multi Unit Spectroscopic Explorer (MUSE) on the VLT. NGC 5972 hosts an active galactic nucleus (AGN) alongside an extended emission line region (EELR) that extends approximately 17 kpc from the center. By examining spatially resolved spectra, we investigate the physical conditions of the EELR, specifically analyzing the radial variation in ionization states and utilizing light-travel time distances to probe AGN variability over timescales exceeding $10^4$ years. Kinematic analysis reveals three distinct components: (a) a faint feature tracing the large-scale disk rotation, (b) gas associated with the EELR indicative of extraplanar material linked to tidal tails, and (c) a kinematically decoupled nuclear disk. Both the kinematics and observed tidal tails point to a significant past interaction event. Diagnostic analysis of emission lines along the EELR arms typically indicates Seyfert-like characteristics, suggesting the region is primarily ionized by the AGN. We constructed photoionization models fitted to various regions along the EELR to estimate the bolometric luminosity required at different radii to produce the observed gas states. Our findings indicate that NGC 5972 is a fading quasar, exhibiting a steady decline in intrinsic AGN luminosity and, consequently, the supermassive black hole's accretion rate by a factor of roughly 100 over the last $5 \times 10^4$ years.

Contact algebra serves as a fundamental instrument within the region-based theory of space. It has been extended in works such as \cite{dmvw1, dmvw2,iv,i1} by eliminating the Boolean complement operation. Further generalization involves removing the meet operation as well, yielding contact join-semilattices (CJS) and distributive contact join-semilattices (DCJS). We establish a set-theoretical representation theorem for CJS and a relational representation theorem for DCJS, from which topological representation theorems follow as corollaries. Additionally, we demonstrate that the universal theories of both CJS and DCJS are identical and decidable.

We establish a lower bound for the time of classical existence of smooth solutions to the relativistic Euler equations, expressed through norms quantifying the "(sound) wave-part" of the data in Sobolev spaces and the "transport-part" in higher-regularity Sobolev and Hölder spaces. These solutions may possess nontrivial vorticity and entropy. Our primary finding demonstrates that the $H^{2+}$ Sobolev norm of the "wave-part" variables and the $C^{0,0+}$ Hölder norm of the "transport-part" variables can be bounded by the initial data over short time intervals. Notably, the $H^{2+}$ assumption for the "wave-part" represents an optimal result. In contrast to low-regularity findings for quasilinear wave equations and the 3D non-relativistic compressible Euler equations, the principal novelty lies in the necessity to manage the fact that vorticity and entropy gradients act as four-dimensional space-time vectors governed by a div-curl-transport system, where the space-time div-curl component lacks ellipticity. To surmount this obstacle, we demonstrate that the space-time div-curl systems induce elliptic div-curl-transport systems on constant-time hypersurfaces, supplemented by error terms featuring favorable differentiations and contractions relative to the four-velocity. Leveraging these structural properties, we successfully control the vorticity and entropy gradients by integrating energy estimates for transport equations, elliptic estimates, Schauder estimates, and Littlewood-Paley theory.

This study characterizes the three-dimensional spatial variations of [Fe/H], [Mg/H], and [Mg/Fe] in stars at their formation epochs across 11 simulated Milky Way- and M31-mass galaxies from the FIRE-2 simulations, aiming to inform initial conditions for chemical tagging. The overall scatter in [Fe/H] within a galaxy declined until approximately 7 Gyr ago, after which it increased to the present day; this trend results from a competition between decreasing azimuthal scatter and a steepening radial abundance gradient over time. The radial gradient is generally negative and evolved from an initially flat state ($\gtrsim 12$ Gyr ago) to a steeper configuration. The current strength of the abundance gradient does not correlate with the timing of disk settling but instead correlates most strongly with the galaxy's radial velocity dispersion. Azimuthal variation strength is nearly radius-independent, with the 360-degree scatter decreasing over time from $\lesssim 0.17$ dex at $t_{\rm lb} = 11.6$ Gyr to $\sim 0.04$ dex today. Consequently, stars formed at $t_{\rm lb} \gtrsim 8$ Gyr originated in a disk dominated by azimuthal abundance scatter. All stars formed in a vertically homogeneous disk, with $\Delta$[Fe/H] $\leq 0.02$ dex within 1 kpc of the midplane, except for young stars in the inner $\approx 4$ kpc at $z \sim 0$.
